To address both simultaneously through a closed-loop waste-treats-waste strategy, this study upcycled an authentic chemical polishing effluent into a hierarchical calcium silicate hydrate-calcium hydroxide (CSH-CH) composite. Unlike conventional CSH synthesized from pure chemicals, this waste-derived material exploits the unique chemical signature of the effluent to inherently retain highly mobile Na + , creating a dual-cation (Na + /Ca 2+ ) exchange advantage. Acting as a multi-target scavenger, CSH-CH exhibited rapid adsorption kinetics toward five co-existing heavy metals (Cd 2+ , Cu 2+ , Zn 2+ , Pb 2+ , and Ni 2+ ), reaching equilibrium within 30-60 min, with sequestration governed by a synergistic mechanism. The practical applicability and ecological safety of CSH-CH were further evaluated using hydroponic Pisum sativum (pea) seedling assays under multi-metal co-contamination (5 mg/L each). CSH-CH treatment substantially reduced metal bioavailability in the root zone, decreasing root accumulation by 85-90% (to 0.90-1.11 mg/kg) and suppressing bioconcentration factors to below 0.3. Root-to-shoot translocation was likewise effectively restricted (translocation factor < 0.2), limiting metal accumulation in the aerial shoots to near-negligible levels (<0.03 mg/kg). Consequently, CSH-CH treatment markedly alleviated metal-induced phytotoxicity, restoring seed germination and seedling growth comparable to unpolluted controls. Collectively, this work demonstrates a viable waste-treats-waste route for converting a hazardous industrial effluent into a low-cost, biosafe composite for multi-metal wastewater remediation.

title: Cardiac injury and purine metabolic remodeling in Carassius auratus under environmentally relevant carbonate alkalinity exposure
abstract: With the intensification of global warming and human activities, inland freshwaters are increasingly salinized and alkalized, often with carbonate alkalinity predominating. Such conditions disrupt acid-base and ion homeostasis in freshwater fish and may induce systemic energy metabolic reprogramming. However, the effects of carbonate alkalinity stress on the heart, an organ with high energy demands, remain poorly understood. Therefore, Carassius auratus (C. auratus), which exhibits relatively high tolerance to carbonate alkalinity, was selected as the experimental species in the present study. The fish were exposed to 0, 20, or 40 mM NaHCO 3 , representing carbonate alkalinity levels reported in saline-alkaline lakes of the Songnen Plain. Carbonate alkalinity exposure caused cardiac injury, evidenced by increased TUNEL-positive signals and mitochondrial swelling, cristae disruption, and vacuolization. These changes were accompanied by reduced mitochondrial membrane potential (P < 0.0001) and ATP content, increased cardiac ammonia, and disrupted redox homeostasis. Reactive oxygen species increased by 1.08- and 1.65-fold in the 20 and 40 mM groups, respectively, whereas glutathione content and glutathione peroxidase and superoxide dismutase activities decreased. Untargeted metabolomics revealed marked remodeling of purine metabolism, glycolysis, oxidative phosphorylation, starch and sucrose metabolism, glycerophospholipid metabolism, and unsaturated fatty acid biosynthesis. Targeted assays further showed increased cardiac ADP, AMP, IMP, hypoxanthine, xanthine, and uric acid, together with decreased xanthine dehydrogenase activity and increased xanthine oxidase activity, indicating that altered terminal purine oxidation may contribute to cardiac oxidative stress. Collectively, carbonate alkalinity stress was associated with cardiac injury in C. auratus, potentially via increased cardiac ammonia burden, mitochondrial energy dysfunction, perturbed purine metabolism, and xanthine oxidase-related oxidative stress.

title: Hydroxyapatite mineralization-driven granulation enables rapid start-up and stable operation of the one-stage partial nitritation/anammox process
abstract: Severe biomass washout remains a major bottleneck limiting the rapid startup and long-term stability of one-stage partial nitritation/anammox (PN/A) processes. In this study, a novel hydroxyapatite-based partial nitritation/anammox (HAP-PN/A) strategy was developed to enhance biomass retention and improve operational stability through HAP mineralization-driven granulation. An HAP-PN/A reactor was established using anammox sludge and partial nitrification sludge as inocula, and the effects of different Ca/P ratios on reactor startup, nitrogen removal performance, sludge characteristics, and microbial community succession were systematically investigated. The results demonstrated that Ca/P regulation promoted HAP precipitation and facilitated granular sludge reconstruction, enabling successful startup within 40 days at a Ca/P ratio of 3. The HAP-PN/A system achieved a maximum nitrogen removal efficiency of 85.24% at a nitrogen loading rate of 1.25 g N/(L·d), while simultaneously achieving an average phosphorus removal efficiency of 59.52%. The developed HAP-based granules exhibited excellent settleability, with an average particle size of 346 μm and a sludge volume index of 15.11 mL/g. Microbial analysis revealed that Ca. Brocadia became the dominant anammox genus after reactor acclimation, accounting for 9.6-13.9% of the microbial community, indicating successful enrichment of functional AnAOB within the HAP matrix. Overall, this study demonstrates that HAP mineralization-driven granulation provides an effective approach for accelerating PN/A startup, enhancing microbial retention, and achieving simultaneous nitrogen removal and phosphorus recovery from ammonia-rich wastewater.

title: Extreme temperatures and workplace injuries by economic sectors in Santiago, Chile, from 2012-2019
abstract: Background Climate change increases extreme temperature events, posing critical risks to occupational safety. However, quantitative evidence for Latin America remains scarce. This study estimated relative risks (RR) and occupational injury burden associated with extreme heat and cold in Santiago Metropolitan Area (SMA), Chile, across economic sectors and demographic groups. Methods A time-stratified case-crossover study (2012–2019) analyzed 603,676 occupational injuries using distributed lag non-linear models (DLNMs) with conditional quasi-Poisson variance to capture non-linear exposure-response associations and delayed-lag effects (5-day lag), controlling for humidity, PM 2.5 , and ozone. Risks at the 2.5th (4.8 °C) and 97.5th (23.4 °C) percentiles were compared to the all-industry Minimum Injury Temperature (10.7 °C). Results Extreme heat increased injury risk in Hotel (RR=1.36; 95% CI: 1.09–1.70) and Transportation (RR=1.25; 95% CI: 1.02–1.53) sectors, affecting males (RR=1.30; 95% CI: 1.12–1.52) and females (RR=1.40; 95% CI: 1.20–1.65). Extreme cold increased risk in Other Industrial Activities (RR=1.18; 95% CI: 1.06–1.32) and Construction (RR=1.12; 95% CI: 1.02–1.24). Overall, 5,542 injuries were attributable to non-optimal temperatures. Workers aged 25–34 showed the highest heat (RR=1.43; 95% CI: 1.22–1.68), whereas workers aged 55 and older were most vulnerable to cold (RR=1.14; 95% CI: 1.04–1.24). Conclusion Extreme temperatures elevate occupational injury risks in a Latin American metropolitan setting, displaying differential vulnerability across sectors and demographic profiles. These findings underscore the urgency of integrating climate-based early warning systems into regional occupational health policies.

title: Nitrate accumulation and transformation processes within a karst conduit system: Insights from hydrochemistry, stable isotopes, metagenomics, and tracer tests
abstract: Nitrate (NO 3 - ) pollution in karst groundwater threatens drinking water security. However, limited subsurface accessibility makes tracing its migration and transformation within karst conduits challenging. This study integrated hydrochemistry, multiple isotopes, functional genes, and tracer tests to elucidate NO 3 - sources and transformation in the Lanfeng watershed, a representative karst conduit system in southwestern China. Nitrification dominated the watershed nitrogen cycle, with soil organic nitrogen (SON) as the primary NO 3 - source, contributing 69.4% and 74.0% to surface and groundwater, respectively. High dissolved oxygen (DO) and low dissolved organic carbon (DOC) conditions in the conduit favored nitrification. Along the flow path, NO 3 - concentrations increased from 1.56 mg L -1 (inlet) to 14.23 mg L -1 (outlet), accompanied by increases in the NO 3 - /Cl - molar ratio (0.14 → 1.55) and nitrification functional gene abundances (24.74 → 97.28 CPM), supporting nitrification as an important nitrogen transformation process within the conduit. However, lateral recharge or water mixing cannot be completely excluded as contributors to the observed NO 3 - enrichment. A conditional apparent NO 3 - concentration change index, based on spatial concentration differences normalized by tracer-derived peak-time differences, ranged from 0.20 to 0.89 mg L -1 d -1 . This study demonstrates that karst conduits are not passive transport pathways, but rather "reactors" with an intrinsic capacity for NO 3 - production. These findings highlight the need to consider endogenous NO 3 - production within subsurface flow paths, alongside external anthropogenic nitrogen inputs, in NO 3 - risk assessment and mitigation, providing broader insights into NO 3 - pollution management in karst aquifers worldwide.

title: Analysis of carbon cycle interference mechanisms in karst rivers under the combined influence of acid mine drainage and multi-source anthropogenic pollution
abstract: Acid mine drainage (AMD) triggers complex environmental chain reactions, including hydrochemical imbalance, heavy metal accumulation, and carbon cycle disruption. In karst regions, the coupled surface-subsurface structure accelerates pollutant migration and environmental risks. AMD-induced dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) loss and enhanced carbonate dissolution weaken the karst carbon sink. To clarify the AMD effects on carbon cycling in karst rivers, this study investigated the Yudong River Basin in Kaili City, Guizhou Province, China. Based on multi-temporal sampling data collected from 2024 to 2025, combined with hydrochemical ions, DIC, and carbon isotopes (δ 13 C DIC ) analyses, we examined hydrochemical evolution and carbon cycling under AMD and anthropogenic influences. Results showed that the dominant hydrochemical type was SO 4 2- ·Ca·Mg-type water, indicating a shift from carbonate-driven to sulfate-driven weathering. AMD significantly increased SO 4 2- , Ca 2+ , and Mg 2+ concentrations, weakened the HCO 3 - -dominated carbonate system, lowered pH, and enhanced partial pressure of carbon dioxide (pCO 2 ) and CO 2 emissions (FCO 2 ). The average pCO 2 and FCO 2 in AMD-affected reaches were approximately 9.94 and 9.37 times higher, respectively, than those in unaffected reaches, contributing up to approximately 63% of the basin's CO 2 emissions (25.57 Gg C yr -1 km -2 ) and markedly reducing the basin's net carbon sequestration efficiency. Redundancy analysis showed that hydrochemical indicators explained 62.86% of the relative contribution to the carbon cycle, indicating a pronounced anthropogenic effect. Without significant DIC enrichment, sulfide oxidation and Fe 3+ hydrolysis may jointly promote DIC conversion to CO 2(aq) in AMD source areas. During downstream dilution, enhanced CO 2 degassing led to δ 13 C DIC enrichment, whereas under low-pH mixed pollution, carbonate dissolution, organic matter mineralization, and sulfate reduction may increase DIC and shift δ 13 C DIC negatively. Overall, AMD is the primary driver of carbon cycle imbalance and increased carbon emissions in the karst river basin, while multiple anthropogenic pollution sources significantly alter carbon migration and transformation pathways.

title: Multi-level toxicity of 6PPD-Q and TiO2 nanoparticles in Mytilus coruscus: Links among neurochemical, circadian and metabolic responses
abstract: Tire-derived 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) and titanium dioxide nanoparticles (TiO 2 NPs) are increasingly detected in aquatic environments, yet their combined effects on marine bivalves remain poorly understood. In this study, the thick-shell mussel Mytilus coruscus was exposed to 6PPD-Q, TiO 2 NPs, and their mixtures to evaluate multi-level physiological, biochemical, histological, and molecular responses. The results demonstrated that 6PPD-Q and TiO 2 NPs, particularly under high-concentration co-exposure, significantly impaired mussel physiological performance, as indicated by reduced clearance rate and O:N ratio, increased oxygen consumption and excretion rate, and pronounced gill histopathological injury. Co-exposure also caused clear energy metabolic disruption, including decreased ATP content and inhibited CS, LDH, and PK activities, together with suppressed neurotransmitter levels of DA, ACh, and GABA. In addition, the expression patterns of circadian rhythm- and metabolism-related genes, including CRY, Per2, PPARγ, ACO, and PEPCK, were markedly altered, suggesting disruption of neuro-circadian-metabolic regulation. Oxidative stress was evident in both gills and digestive gland, as reflected by altered CAT and SOD activities and elevated MDA levels. These responses were accompanied by significant modulation of inflammatory and apoptotic genes, including TNF-α, IL-17, TGF-β, Caspase-3, Caspase-8, and Bcl-2. These findings suggest that 6PPD-Q and TiO 2 NPs may jointly impair mussel health by linking gill first-contact injury with metabolic dysregulation, oxidative stress, and immune-apoptotic damage.

title: Functional upcycling of nanomodified cementitious waste into recycled aggregate with multiscale reinforcement and environmental performance assessment
abstract: The growing accumulation of cementitious waste and continued extraction of natural sand have increased the need for high-value recycling of cement-based materials. However, recycled cementitious particles are often limited by old hydration products, residual pores, and crushing-induced microcracks. Nano-modified cementitious waste may offer an alternative pathway because residual nanomaterials, if retained after crushing, could still influence pore structure and interfacial bonding. In this study, graphene oxide-modified recycled concrete particles (GO-RCP), produced from crushed GO-modified mortar, were used to partially replace natural sand in fresh mortar. At 40% sand replacement, metal-accessible cumulative porosity decreased from 18.87% to 14.38%, mean interfacial transition zone (ITZ) porosity within 0-40 μm decreased to 18.75%, and the normalized pore enrichment index declined from 9.27% to 4.37%. Compared with the control, compressive and flexural strengths increased by 27.39% and 21.95%, respectively. Deep Taylor decomposition revealed distinct classification-relevant regions, while the extracted-feature fractal dimension showed a strong correlation with compressive strength (R 2 = 0.94). Molecular dynamics simulations further indicated that residual GO nanosheets can improve stress transfer, crack bridging, crack deflection and energy dissipation at the C-S-H/RCP interface. Under the baseline cut-off scenario, at 40% replacement, direct production cost and PED decreased by 15.97% and 1.23%, respectively, while absolute GHG emissions remained nearly unchanged (+0.08%). After strength normalization, PC, GHG, and PED decreased by 34.05%, 21.43%, and 22.46%, respectively. These findings demonstrate a potential route for converting GO-modified cementitious waste into a recycled fine aggregate with improved 28-day mechanical and microstructural performance, together with resource-saving and strength-normalized environmental and economic benefits.

title: Desert dust storm, ambient temperature, and pulmonary function among children with asthma in the Eastern Mediterranean
abstract: Background Climate change has contributed to increased dust events and rising ambient temperature, posing potential health risk for susceptible populations including children with asthma. The study aims to examine associations between exposure to desert dust storm (DDS) and higher ambient temperature with pulmonary function indicators, including forced expiratory volume in 1s (FEV 1 ), forced vital capacity (FVC) and FEV 1 /FVC% among asthmatic children during the dust season in the Eastern Mediterranean. Methods We conducted exploratory secondary analyses of repeated pulmonary function measurements from schoolchildren with asthma in Cyprus and Crete, Greece during spring of 2019 and 2021. Dust exposure was defined using short-term (at least one DDS day on the assessment day or during the preceding 7 days) and cumulative days (over the spring season) metrics based on site-specific DDS classifications as well as ambient temperature assessed from the nearest meteorological station. Associations were examined using linear mixed-effect models. Results Among the 135 children included, short-term DDS exposure was associated with a non-significant decrement in FEV 1 (-20.46 mL, 95% CI: -50.38, 9.46) and FVC (-27.21 mL, 95% CI: -59.45, 5.02). Cumulative dust exposure was associated with -3.52 mL (95% CI: -5.90, -1.14) difference in FEV 1 per DDS day. Ambient temperature averaged over 0-7 days before assessment was inversely associated with FEV 1 (-19.77 mL; 95% CI: -37.91, -1.63 per 5°C increase) and FEV 1 /FVC% (-0.81; 95% CI: -1.36, -0.25 per 5 °C increase), with no statistical evidence of effect modification by short-term DDS exposure. Conclusions This exploratory secondary analysis demonstrated inverse associations of cumulative DDS exposure and ambient temperature with pulmonary function among children with asthma, while short-term DDS associations were not statistically significant. These findings may inform the management of children with asthma during desert dust seasons, but confirmation in larger studies is required.

title: Enhancement of mechanical performance and heavy metal immobilization in red mud-based cementitious materials through sodium silicate optimization and CaO modification
abstract: Red mud (RM), a highly alkaline by-product of alumina production, poses serious environmental risks, while its high-value utilization remains challenging. Although red mud-based cementitious materials have been widely investigated, simultaneously achieving high mechanical performance and effective heavy metal immobilization remains difficult because the coupling mechanism between hydration evolution and contaminant stabilization is still unclear. This study developed an optimized red mud-based cementitious material to simultaneously enhance compressive strength and heavy metal stabilization while elucidating the underlying mechanism. The final optimized formulation achieved a 28-day compressive strength of 9.02 MPa while maintaining acceptable flowability. At the final 56-day test point, the leaching concentrations of Pb, As, Cd, and Mn were more than 98% lower than those of the freshly prepared reference mixture. XRD and SEM observations were consistent with AFt formation, the development of poorly crystalline gel-like products, and progressive matrix densification. These structural changes were consistent with the observed decrease in heavy metal leaching. However, the chemical states and binding environments of the immobilized metals were not directly determined. These findings suggest a link between hydration-driven microstructural evolution, strength development, and contaminant stabilization, supporting the sustainable use of red mud in low-carbon cementitious materials.

title: Retraction notice to “Breakthrough in plasmonic enhanced MOFs: Design, synthesis, and catalytic mechanisms for various photocatalytic applications” [Environ. Res. 277 (2025) 121257]

Retraction notice to “Biodegradable composites from poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) with carbon nanoparticles: Preparation, characterization and performances” [Environ. Res. 235 (2023) 116634]
Retraction notice to “Development of artificial neural networks software for arsenic adsorption from an aqueous environment” [Environ. Res. 203 (2022) 111846]
Variable effectiveness of raw rice, cooked rice, and water in recapitulating dietary inorganic and organic arsenic exposure in the health effects of arsenic longitudinal study
abstract: The interaction between water and rice arsenic (As) has long raised questions about what type of As exposure monitoring is both feasible and effective. Here, we leverage matched samples of raw rice, cooked rice, cooking water, and spot urine from 396 participants in the Health Effects of Arsenic Longitudinal Study (HEALS) in Araihazar, Bangladesh, to determine which sample type is most informative of overall As exposure. First, we find that the difference in cooked and raw rice As is most pronounced when cooking water As exceeds the Bangladeshi 50 μg As/L safety limit. Second, we find that cooking rice in high As water can push rice with "safe" levels of As while uncooked into the unsafe range (>200 ng inorganic iAs/g dry rice) after cooking. Third, we find that cooked rice is a more reliable indicator of dietary As exposure across a wide range of water arsenic levels, but also find that neither rice or water As explain much variation in urinary As when As is low in both water and rice. Rice explains moderate urinary variance only when water As is low. Lastly, we find that mono- and di-methylated forms of As (MMA and DMA, respectively) from cooked rice minimally contribute to urinary MMA and DMA levels and do not bias common measures of As methylation efficiency in this population. These data suggest that methylation efficiency measures derived from urinary MMA and DMA levels are robust to dietary influences and support their continued use in epidemiological studies.

title: Riverine CH4 emission hotspots are more closely associated with local sediment and DOM properties than with broad land-use categories
abstract: Land-use differences can substantially influence methane (CH 4 ) production and emissions in rivers, but whether they can reliably explain the occurrence of high-emission hotspots remains unclear. This uncertainty limits the development of targeted strategies for reducing riverine CH 4 emissions. This study quantified CH 4 fluxes across the sediment-water and water-air interfaces along a river continuum spanning forested mountain, urban-plain, and rural cropland reaches and identified the mechanisms driving riverine CH 4 emission hotspots. The results showed that CH 4 fluxes were significantly higher in July than in February, and the hotspot reaches accounted for 90.36% and 91.08% of the summed sediment-water CH 4 flux measured across the 12 reaches in July and February, respectively, with ebullition representing the dominant emission pathway in July. However, these hotspots were not concentrated within a single land-use type, but exhibited strong spatial heterogeneity, indicating that broad land-use categories did not consistently distinguish hotspot reaches. The strong association between sediment-water and water-air CH 4 fluxes, together with the occurrence of hotspot reaches in fine, silt-rich sediments, suggests that local sediment conditions may contribute to hotspot formation. The environmental and microbial characteristics associated with hotspots differed between the two sampling campaigns: February hotspots were characterized by higher DOC concentrations, whereas July hotspots coincided with DOM characteristics indicative of greater bioavailability and higher relative abundances of methanogens and methanogenesis-related genes, suggesting greater methane-production potential. This study highlights the local environmental and microbial factors associated with riverine CH 4 emission hotspots and provides scientific guidance for developing management-based mitigation strategies for riverine CH 4 emissions.

title: Antibiotic resistance profiles and associated factors in aquatic ecosystems with contrasting hydrodynamic settings
abstract: Antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) are ubiquitous in aquatic ecosystems, but the ecological risk patterns and associated factors remain unclear across aquatic environments with contrasting hydrodynamic conditions. Using an integrated analytical framework, we explored interactions among antibiotics, microbial communities, mobile genetic elements (MGEs), and ARGs in a dynamic river and a slow-flow wetland. Antibiotics were widely detected in both systems, with generally higher total concentrations in the dynamic river (50.0-148.4 ng/L) than in the slow-flow wetland (2.5-101.7 ng/L). The total abundance of ARGs was also higher and more homogeneous in the dynamic river (49529.4-58542.5 RPKM) compared to the slow-flow wetland (24091.8-53003.0 RPKM), which exhibited greater spatial heterogeneity. Structural equation modeling (SEM) revealed different ARG-associated factor patterns in the two aquatic ecosystems with contrasting hydrodynamic settings. Bacterial communities and MGEs showed stronger associations with ARG variation in the Qiantang River, with standardized total effects (STEs) of 0.953 and 0.442, respectively, whereas antibiotics and MGEs showed stronger associations with ARG variation in the Xixi Wetland, with STEs of 0.816 and 0.747, respectively. Sulfamonomethoxine (SMM) was identified as the antibiotic most strongly associated with ARG variation in the wetland based on random forest analysis (importance score = 46.90%). This study indicates that the Qiantang River and Xixi Wetland exhibited distinct antibiotic resistance profiles and ARG-associated factor patterns, characterized by a host community-associated mode in the river and an antibiotic-associated mode in the wetland, with MGEs associated with ARG variation in both ecosystems.

title: Coexistence of biocrusts and vascular plants reduces soil organic carbon stability by increasing labile fractions in drylands
abstract: Vascular plants and biocrusts serve as stable ecological units in dryland landscapes and significantly influence soil organic carbon (SOC) pools. However, intensified global climate change and the resulting shifts in moisture regimes are promoting the emergence of biocrust-plant coexistence (abbreviated as "coexistence patches") as a new stable landscape unit. It remains unclear how this novel combination of vascular and non-vascular plants affects SOC stability. To address this, we conducted a field experiment on China's Loess Plateau, comparing bare soil, pure plant patches (shrubs and grasses), and coexistence patches (shrubs and grasses with biocrusts). Surface soil samples were collected to measure total SOC alongside its labile (LOC) and recalcitrant (ROC) fractions to comprehensively assess differences in SOC stability. Associated environmental factors were also analyzed to uncover underlying regulatory mechanisms. Compared with bare soil, coexistence patches enhanced SOC, LOC, and ROC content by 2.05, 1.15, and 2.83 times, respectively. More importantly, compared with pure plant patches, coexistence patches increased LOC content by 12.5% but decreased SOC and ROC content by 36.5% and 49.7%, respectively, leading to a 20.0% decrease in SOC stability. Structural equation modeling revealed that coexistence patches enhance soil microbial richness and diversity mainly through their positive effect on surface soil moisture, which accelerated LOC accumulation and indirectly diminished SOC stability. In summary, although coexistence patches lower C stability relative to pure plant patches by stimulating LOC fractions, they substantially improve overall soil C storage relative to bare soil. Thus, when accurately evaluating how dryland C pools respond to intensifying global changes, especially altered precipitation, it is crucial to account for such temporary or irreversible transitions between ecosystem stable states (whether through degradation or succession) and their consequences for SOC stability.

title: Hydrological seasonality reshapes sources and health risks of potentially toxic elements in a megacity river system of the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei urban agglomeration
abstract: Reclaimed water has been increasingly used to sustain urban river flows, whereas the influence of seasonal hydrological variations on the behavior of potentially toxic elements (PTEs) remains insufficiently characterized. In this study, the PTEs characteristics in China's most typical reclaimed water-influenced river system were investigated during the whole hydrological year. PTEs in wet season was accumulated in mainstream under stronger hydrological connectivity, whereas that in dry season shifted toward tributaries and local hotspots under reduced discharge and weaker dilution. PTEs sources during wet season were dominated by geological background coupled with Fe-mediated particle transport (37%), integrated industrial/urban inputs (39%), and urban non-point pollution (23%), while dry season was mainly associated with industrial activities, reclaimed water inputs, and internal remobilization. Estuary remained at the lowest pollution level throughout the hydrological year and was not the principal PTEs pollution accumulation zone. Although integrated pollution indices indicated more severe pollution during the dry season (Pn: 2.55-3.34), Monte Carlo simulations identified As as the dominant risk contributor, with higher mean non-carcinogenic and carcinogenic risks during the wet season. Wet-season mean hazard quotients (HQs) for As were 0.64 in adults and 1.44 in children; corresponding mean carcinogenic risks were 1.26 × 10 -4 and 5.83 × 10 -5 , respectively. To address the seasonal mismatch among PTEs pollution, this study proposed a differentiated management framework for megacity river system that integrates seasonal diagnosis, source prioritized mitigation, reclaimed water upgrading, ecological buffer interception, and early warning of probabilistic risk, providing an innovative strategy for precise PTE control in reclaimed water-replenished urban rivers.

title: Government extension, social support and farmers’ response to climate-adaptive technologies: Insights from a discrete choice experiment
abstract: Climate change poses substantial challenges to agricultural production systems and rural livelihoods. Leveraging agricultural extension programs to promote climate-adaptive technologies is an important pathway to enhancing agricultural resilience and ensuring food security. However, how government extension services, social support mechanisms, and economic incentives jointly shape farmers' preferences for climate-adaptive technologies remains insufficiently understood. Based on survey data from 1547 farm households in the main maize-producing region of Liaoning Province in China, this study employs a discrete choice experiment to examine farmers' preferences and subsidy-equivalent monetary valuations for climate-adaptive technology packages by simultaneously incorporating technological attributes, government extension services, and social support mechanisms. The results show that: (1) Farmers generally prefer technology options associated with higher perceived production benefits, indicating a significant positive preference for new crop varieties and smart water management technologies, while their preferences for agrometeorological risk mitigation technologies and improved conservation tillage are relatively weak. (2) Providing technical training has a significant negative effect on farmers' choices, whereas cooperative technical support and direct subsidies significantly increase farmers' likelihood of choosing climate-adaptive technology options. (3) The subsidy-equivalent valuation estimates show that farmers assign the highest monetary value to new crop varieties (approximately CNY 26/mu), while technical training exhibits a negative valuation (approximately CNY -31/mu), suggesting that farmers may perceive the current design of technical training as involving additional participation costs. (4) The latent class logit model further divides farmers into two groups: a relatively cautious group (13.13%) and a more technology-oriented group (86.87%). The two groups differ significantly in technology preferences, acceptance of extension modes, and reliance on social support. This paper provides empirical evidence for optimizing agricultural technology extension systems and implementing differentiated incentive policies.

title: Citizen science-based mapping of radiofrequency electromagnetic field exposure in Europe: A proof-of-concept validation study
abstract: Characterising population-level radiofrequency electromagnetic field (RF-EMF) exposure from mobile telecommunications networks at fine spatial resolution has been limited by the cost and scale of conventional measurement methods. The ETAIN 5G Scientist app, developed within the ETAIN (Exposure To electromAgnetic fIelds and plaNetary health) project uses citizen science smartphone data to produce calibrated RF-EMF exposure maps for 4G/5G networks at 25 x 25 m 2 spatial resolution across Europe. As of 2026, the app had collected over 19 million measurements globally. We conducted a proof-of-concept validation of these exposure maps in two European cities with contrasting urban and network characteristics: Utrecht (Netherlands) and Basel (Switzerland). Walking measurement campaigns used the ETAIN app installed on smartphones and the ExpoM-RF4 reference exposimeter carried simultaneously in a backpack. App-derived exposure estimates were compared with spatiotemporally matched reference measurements at the grid-cell level. Validation was performed separately for 4G Long-Term Evolution (LTE) and combined 4G LTE and 5G New Radio (NR) environmental exposure estimates. 4G LTE exposure estimates correlated strongly with measured exposure in both Utrecht ( r s = 0.87, 95% CI: 0.80-0.91, N = 127) and Basel ( r s = 0.71, 95% CI: 0.63-0.78, N = 214; both p < 0.001). The combined 4G LTE and 5G NR exposure estimates correlated strongly in Utrecht ( r s = 0.88, 95% CI: 0.81-0.92; 19.7% of grid cells with 5G NR detection) but showed moderate correlation in Basel ( r s = 0.41, 95% CI: 0.29-0.53; 45.3% of grid cells with 5G NR detection). Sensitivity analyses showed map reliability stabilised at five or more observations per grid cell and improved when data from two network operators were combined. These results demonstrate that the ETAIN 5G Scientist application can produce validated, spatially continuous RF-EMF exposure maps at scale. The approach is well suited for characterising exposure trends as mobile networks continue to evolve.

title: Corrigendum to “Trends and causal drivers of extreme snowfall intensification in China under climate warming” [Environ. Res. 290 (2026) 123525]
From primary to secondary aerosol: chemical transformation and toxicity of gasoline vehicle exhaust under contrasting driving conditions
abstract: Secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation from gasoline vehicle exhaust represents a significant contributor to urban air pollution, yet the integrated effects of driving dynamics, atmospheric ageing, and gas-particle interactions on aerosol toxicity remain poorly characterised. This study investigated primary and secondary particle emissions from a plug-in hybrid Euro 6 gasoline vehicle equipped with a gasoline particulate filter (GPF), tested under two chassis dynamometer driving cycles of contrasting aggressiveness: a mild Real Driving Emissions cycle (mRDE) and a highly dynamic Combined cycle, each under cold and hot engine operation. Diluted exhaust was photochemically aged in a Tampere Secondary Aerosol Reactor (TSAR) and characterised physically, chemically, and toxicologically. Chemical analysis included offline quantification of particle-bound polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), nitro-PAHs (NPAHs), oxy-PAHs (OPAHs), and water-soluble elements, alongside real-time aerosol mass spectrometry (SP-AMS). Toxicological assessment used a mobile Air-Liquid Interface (ALI) system to expose human lung epithelial (A549) cells to fresh and aged whole exhaust and gas-phase-only streams. Atmospheric ageing consistently shifted aerosol composition from a mixed primary aerosol to an organic-dominated secondary aerosol (organic fraction increasing from ∼60% to ∼87%), enhanced ultrafine particle formation, and increased the deposited particle dose. Whole exhaust exposures produced stronger cytotoxic and inflammatory responses than gas-phase-only exposures across all conditions. For the tested vehicle and experimental conditions, driving dynamics exerted the strongest influence on biological response, while atmospheric ageing amplified the particle-associated biological response. Cold-start operation had a more moderate effect, primarily manifested through changes in gaseous emissions rather than particle toxicity.

title: Compensation-deterioration effect of phosphogypsum-red mud-based backfill under chloride salt conditions and wet-dry cycles
abstract: The use of bulk industrial solid wastes such as phosphogypsum and red mud for mine backfilling promotes synergistic solid waste utilization and ecological restoration in mining areas. However, uncertainties remain in the long-term performance of backfill and heavy metal stability under chloride-rich groundwater erosion. In this study, a multisource industrial solid waste synergistic cementation system (PRFQ) was prepared from raw phosphogypsum (PG), red mud (RM), fly ash (FA), and quicklime (QL). Its performance evolution and degradation mechanisms were investigated after 12 wet-dry cycles in 0%-11% NaCl solutions. The results indicate that the chloride-salt corrosion resistance threshold of the PRFQ system was 4%, and the recommended PG content in the PRFQ system was 40-70 wt%. At a PG content of 50 wt% and an RM/FA/QL ratio of 5:1:2, after 12 wet-dry cycles in an 11% NaCl solution, the residual compressive strength was 1.82 MPa, the mass loss was 13.12%, and the heavy metal leaching concentrations met the Class III limits of the groundwater quality standards. Low-concentration Cl - promotes Fe/Al gel formation and particle bonding, compensating for microstructural defects. A higher Cl - concentration leads to Na + -induced decalcification, Friedel's salt expansion and NaCl crystallization stress, causing pore expansion and degradation. Wet-dry cycles accelerate Cl - migration and the dissolution of hydrates, but some decomposed products bond with Cl - , providing filling and passivation and slowing degradation. This study supports the safe, high-value utilization of PG, RM, and FA in chloride-rich environments.

title: Integrated human and natural regulation of carbon concentrations and fluxes dynamics in the Yangtze River mainstream over the past two decades
abstract: Rivers play a key role in the global carbon cycle, yet the long-term spatiotemporal dynamics of dissolved organic carbon (DOC), particulate organic carbon (POC), and dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) in large rivers remain uncertain, particularly for large Asian rivers where simultaneous assessments of all three forms are scarce. We compiled a monthly database (2000-2022) of DOC, POC, and DIC concentrations at 10 sites along the Yangtze River mainstream by integrating 2022 field campaigns with a systematic literature synthesis, and applied three machine learning algorithms to reconstruct continuous monthly concentrations. Fluxes were derived by combining the best-performing concentration estimates with discharge. From headwaters to estuaries, all three fluxes increased, driven by precipitation-controlled runoff growth, whereas concentrations diverged: DOC increased downstream through elevated COD Mn (permanganate index) from runoff flushing; POC declined via vegetation interception and reservoir retention; and DIC decreased through runoff dilution. Over the past two decades, DOC and DIC fluxes were primarily regulated by precipitation-driven discharge, but DOC flux also rose with increasing DOC concentration, while POC flux declined synchronously with POC concentration, and DIC flux showed no significant trend. The corresponding concentration changes-a rise in DOC and declines in POC and DIC-were primarily driven by cascade reservoir construction and climate warming. Consequently, the Yangtze River mainstream is transitioning from a system historically dominated by POC and DIC export toward one increasingly characterized by DOC export. This transition has important implications for carbon burial efficiency and greenhouse gas emissions.

title: Hole-oriented interface engineering for sensitive photoelectrochemical detection of tetracycline
abstract: High-performance photoelectrochemical (PEC) sensors require efficient utilization of photogenerated holes at the semiconductor/electrolyte interface. However, the rational design of an efficient interlayer for directed hole transport remains challenging. Herein, a CoMn-layered double hydroxide (CoMn-LDH) hole transport layer is integrated with a BiVO 4 photoelectrode to regulate interfacial charge transfer. Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) and in situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveal that CoMn-LDH efficiently promotes hole extraction from BiVO 4 while markedly suppressing both interfacial and bulk charge recombination. Coupled with target-specific molecular recognition, the resulting PEC sensor enables highly sensitive and selective detection of tetracycline, affording a low detection limit of 8.4 nM and a wide linear range of 0.01-20 μM. The enhanced sensing performance originates from the built-in electric field at the CoMn-LDH/BiVO 4 heterojunction, which facilitates hole extraction and interfacial oxidation of tetracycline while suppressing electron-hole recombination. In addition, the sensor exhibits good repeatability, robust operational stability, and satisfactory recoveries in tap water, Chaohu lake water, and aquaculture water. This work establishes hole-oriented interfacial engineering as an effective strategy for developing high-performance PEC platforms for antibiotic monitoring.

title: Retraction notice to “Spotlighting of microbial electrodeionization cells for sustainable wastewater treatment: Application of machine learning” [Environ. Res. 219 (2023) 115113]
Retraction notice to “Green sporopollenin supported cyanocalixarene based magnetic adsorbent for pesticides removal from water: Kinetic and equilibrium studies” [Environ. Res. 201 (2021) 111588]
Comprehensive characterization of bioaerosol microbial communities, ARG, and occupational exposure risks in WWTP and comprehensive landfill
abstract: In the sewage treatment plant and landfill in the same area, the differences in transmission characteristics of potential pathogenic microorganisms and antibiotic resistance genes/movable genetic elements (ARGs/MGEs) mediated by bioaerosols have not been fully studied. Therefore, we integrated 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing, high-throughput quantitative PCR, quantitative microbial risk assessment, exposure-dose estimation, and machine learning to compare microbial communities, antibiotic resistance genes and mobile genetic elements (ARGs/MGEs), and estimated occupational exposure levels at a wastewater treatment plant (XQ) and an integrated solid waste treatment facility (DP) in Central China. The mean culturable bacterial concentration was 3.4-fold higher at DP than at XQ (1726 CFU/m 3 , 502 CFU/m 3 ), and proportion of fine biogenic particles was also higher at DP (27%, 15%). In contrast, mean airborne concentration of ARGs/MGEs was substantially higher at XQ than at DP (5462 copies/m 3 , 584 copies/m 3 ), resulting in a higher estimated inhalation exposure dose at XQ. The dominant resistance determinants were ermC, dhps, and intI1 at XQ, and cmxA, tnpA-05, and lnuA-01 at DP. Machine learning analysis identified Faecalibacterium as an important microbial feature distinguishing solid waste bioaerosols, whereas blaPAO was among most influential ARG features associated with XQ bioaerosols. Partial least squares regression revealed extensive covariation between bacterial genera and resistance determinants. Achromobacter was positively associated with ermX at XQ and with intI1 at DP, although these associations do not establish direct host-gene relationships. Overall, two facilities showed contrasting bioaerosol exposure profiles, characterized by higher bacterial and fine-particle levels at DP and higher ARG/MGE exposure estimates at XQ. These findings support facility-specific occupational aerosol control and monitoring strategies.

title: High-throughput transcriptomics for mechanism-informed mixture risk assessment of perfluoroalkyl substances using human biomonitoring data
abstract: Widespread human exposure to mixtures of perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) presents a challenge for risk assessment, as toxicological data for many PFAS are limited and mixture risk assessment requires insight into their shared toxicological mechanisms. In this study, we reanalyzed publicly available high-throughput transcriptomic (HTTr) datasets from human liver spheroids by integrating benchmark dose modeling with pathway enrichment analysis to identify shared pathway perturbations that served as the basis for deriving mechanistically informed transcriptomic points of departure (tPODs) for nine PFAS, including legacy, long-chain, and short-chain substitute compounds. Three shared pathways, namely PPAR signaling, PPARα-regulated lipid metabolism, and fatty acid, triglyceride, and ketone body metabolism, were identified as consistently perturbed across all nine PFAS. Using these shared pathways, PFAS were further prioritized using the Toxicological Prioritization Index, and long-chain PFAS showed greater overall perturbations than short-chain PFAS. For PFAS with available animal-derived PODs, the resulting tPODs were generally consistent with or more conservative than apical PODs. The combined margin of exposure estimates, calculated by integrating tPODs with population-level serum concentrations from different countries/regions, indicated potential concern for some populations under central-tendency conditions, whereas conservative lower-bound estimates suggested potential concern for all populations and high concern for a small fraction of individuals. Overall, the findings indicate that mechanistically informed tPODs derived from HTTr data, together with human biomonitoring measurements, can support early-tier mixture risk assessment of chemicals.

title: Understanding the complexity of microplastics, antibiotic resistance, and their interaction with human health and ecosystems: a review towards global environmental sustainability
abstract: Microplastics (MPs), defined as particles with a diameter <5 mm, are increasingly recognized as important global environmental stressors due to their ubiquity and harmful effects on organisms. Although most studies have investigated the direct biological effects of MPs, their role in the spread of pathogens and antibiotic resistance remains less explored. Thanks to their hydrophobic surfaces, MPs act as substrates for microbial colonization, giving rise to the plastisphere-a microenvironment that hosts opportunistic and clinically relevant bacteria, including Escherichia coli, Vibrio spp., and Aeromonas spp., some of which are multidrug-resistant. The plastisphere has emerged as a hotspot for antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), promoting horizontal gene transfer (HGT) and contributing to the environmental spread of resistance. Human exposure to MPs is widespread, as MPs have been detected in water, food, and air. Once ingested or inhaled, they can accumulate in tissues, cross biological barriers, and cause gastrointestinal irritation, dysbiosis of the microbiota, endocrine disruptions, oxidative stress, and immunotoxicity. MPs carrying biofilms containing resistant bacteria and ARGs represent a direct route of exposure for the introduction of resistance factors into the human body, increasing the risk of untreatable infections. Despite growing evidence, significant knowledge gaps remain regarding the role of MPs in the spread of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and associated health risks. To date, no legislation specifically considers MPs as vectors of pathogens and ARGs. This review aims to clarify the concept of the plastisphere, its implications for AMR, and the urgent need for interdisciplinary approaches to address this emerging global threat.

title: Spatial and seasonal dynamics of microbial and phytoplankton communities and factors influencing the surface water and sediments of the Ponjavica River in the Ponjavica nature park
abstract: Microorganisms are key bioindicators of changes in biogeochemical cycles and the ecological status of aquatic ecosystems. In this paper, seasonal changes in culturable microbial groups, phytoplankton, and physicochemical water characteristics were examined as integrated indicators of environmental status in the Ponjavica River (Ponjavica Nature Park, Serbia). Sampling was conducted at six sites (P2-P7) in 2021, with two campaigns carried out in spring (May) and autumn (November). At all sites, the number of microorganisms was higher in sediment than in water, confirming the importance of sediment as a reservoir of microbial activity and a potential biomonitoring matrix. In autumn, the number of microorganisms in the water was higher than in spring, with anaerobic bacteria predominating. Phytoplankton communities exhibited pronounced seasonal dynamics. In autumn, Cyanobacteria dominated, accounting for 59-99% of total biomass, while in spring, Chlorophyta (26-97%) and Cryptophyta (2-37%) were more prevalent. The increased number and biomass of phytoplankton in autumn were accompanied by higher concentrations of phosphorus and nitrogen, which may reflect increased nutrient uptake and conditions favorable to phytoplankton development. Higher concentrations of iron, manganese, arsenic (except at P7), zinc, chromium, lead, and copper were recorded. These spatial and seasonal differences may be related to variations in nutrient inputs from the surrounding watershed, with agricultural activities as one potential source. Spatial analysis identified site P7, where higher conductivity, increased suspended matter, nitrate, calcium, sulfate, and greater phytoplankton abundance were recorded in autumn. The results confirm that seasonal nutrient input and local physicochemical conditions significantly shape culturable microbial groups and phytoplankton communities, highlighting their potential for biomonitoring pollution and assessing the ecological status of river ecosystems in protected areas.

title: Mutation-induced conformational remodeling of dihydropteroate synthase governs sulfonamide resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae
abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a major bacterial pathogen, and dihydropteroate synthase (DHPS) is the primary target of sulfonamides (SAs). Environmental exposure to SAs promotes the emergence and spread of antibiotic resistance. However, the molecular basis of DHPS mutation-mediated resistance remains unclear. Derived from the folP sequences of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole-resistant clinical isolates, six clinically relevant DHPS mutants were constructed to investigate the molecular basis of resistance and to clarify how structure-activity relationships influence ligand recognition and binding modes. The results showed that the mutations altered the structural characteristics of the catalytic cavity and the substrate tunnel but exerted limited effects on the entry or binding of 6-hydroxymethyl-7,8-dihydropterin pyrophosphate (DHPPP). DHPPP binding induced conformational remodeling, including expansion of loop 2 or loop 5 and rotation of HIE153. Compared with the wild type, sulfamethoxazole (SMX) exhibited reduced binding affinities across all mutants, with loop 2 expansion and impaired loop closure identified as the primary structural determinants of resistance. Additionally, HIE153 indirectly contributed to SMX recognition by maintaining the local microenvironment, binding pocket conformation, and neighboring interaction networks. Structure-activity relationship analysis showed that fused-ring sulfonamides exhibited the strongest tolerance to resistance-associated mutations. These findings reveal how DHPS mutations preserve natural-substrate recognition while selectively weakening SA binding, providing molecular-level insight into SA resistance and its implications for environmental antimicrobial resistance.

title: Mechanisms of POM-mediated Hg immobilization and MeHg suppression in paddy soil: a perspective of coupled geochemical and microbial processes under water management
abstract: Particulate organic matter (POM) plays a critical role in Hg biogeochemistry, yet its immobilization mechanisms and interactions with water management remain unclear. This study investigated POM-mediated Hg immobilization under non-flooded and flooded conditions through a 120-day incubation experiment, combined with batch adsorption, multi-technique characterization, and microbial community analysis. POM addition significantly reduced soil available Hg and promoted the redistribution of Hg to operationally defined less-labile or residual fractions, with available Hg reduction reaching 82% under flooded conditions, compared to 61% under non-flooded. Mechanistically, POM immobilized Hg 2+ through physical entrapment within its porous structure and chemisorption-dominated surface complexation via sulfur and oxygen-containing functional groups, with reactive organic sulfur as the most active binding site. Indirectly, POM addition increased SOC, and structural equation modeling (SEM) supported a statistical pathway consistent with SOC contributing to Hg transformation under flooding (path coefficients: 0.872-0.902). Additionally, POM dose-dependently suppressed MeHg accumulation by reducing bioavailable Hg pools and decreasing hgcA gene abundance, with microbial community restructuring further contributing to this suppression through enrichment of keystone taxa such as Vicinamibacter. Overall, POM amendment combined with flooding may mitigate Hg bioavailability in contaminated agricultural soils under controlled conditions, but field validation is required before recommending this as a practical strategy.

title: Neighborhood walkability, green space, and incident hip fracture among older U.S. adults: The cardiovascular health study
abstract: PURPOSE: Neighborhood walkability and green space are associated with walking behavior and physical activity, but evidence linking them to fracture is limited and inconsistent, and potential sex differences remain understudied. We evaluated associations of neighborhood walkability and green space with incident hip fracture in older, community-dwelling U.S. adults. METHODS: We conducted a prospective cohort study of adults aged ≥65 years from the Cardiovascular Health Study (CHS). Neighborhood exposures were defined using 1-km radial buffers around geocoded residential addresses from 1992 to 1993 (baseline). Walkability was the sum of standardized population and walkable destination densities. Green space was the proportion of satellite-derived green land cover. Hip fractures were prospectively ascertained over 12 years using International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Revision (ICD-9) codes from hospital discharge abstracts. Cox hazard models adjusted for individual-level (age, sex, race, weight, height, smoking status, current heavy alcohol use, medication use, diabetes, renal function, marital status, education level, annual household income) and neighborhood-level (median household income, median value of owner-occupied housing, proportion of persons in managerial/professional occupations) covariates evaluated associations, overall and by sex. RESULTS: Among 3676 participants (58% women), 359 experienced hip fracture over a median 10-years observation. Greater neighborhood walkability was significantly associated with lower hip fracture incidence among women (hazard ratio per 1 standard deviation increase of 0.72 [95% confidence interval, 0.53-0.98]), but not overall or among men. Neighborhood green space was not significantly associated with hip fracture. CONCLUSION: Greater neighborhood walkability, but not green space, was associated with lower hip fracture risk among older women.

title: Integrating empirical ecotoxicology and predictive modelling to assess ecological and human health risks from heavy metals in Malaysia's Chini Lake UNESCO biosphere reserve
abstract: Chini Lake, Malaysia's first UNESCO-designated biosphere reserve, exemplifies the growing challenge of safeguarding freshwater ecosystems exposed to legacy mining activities and ongoing land-use disturbance. Mining and other anthropogenic activities have contributed to persistent heavy metal contamination in freshwater ecosystems, underscoring the need for robust and reliable risk assessment frameworks to inform conservation and policy. This study applies an integrated approach combining empirical (ECOTOX) and predictive (ECOSAR) toxicity data to evaluate ecological and human health risks across 18 surface water sampling stations within Chini Lake tropical freshwater ecosystem. The study determines the abundance and distribution of heavy metals, heavy metal pollution index (HPI), risk quotient (RQ) and hazard quotient (HQ). The RQ derived from the empirical ECOTOX database revealed high ecological risks (RQ ≥ 1) from mean concentrations of aluminium, zinc, copper, nickel, and lead. This level of threat was underestimated by several orders of magnitude when using the ECOSAR model. This finding highlights a significant potential for the underestimation of ecological threats in freshwater bodies if predictive models are used in isolation for metals. For human health, all HQ values for direct water ingestion were below the risk threshold (HQ < 1), though arsenic and cadmium were the primary risk drivers, with children being 2-4 times more vulnerable than adults. This research provides a critical methodological framework for reconciling different risk assessment paradigms. It underscores the paramount importance of leveraging field-relevant, empirical ecotoxicological data over predictive models for metals to accurately characterise ecological threats and guide sustainable water governance in mining-impacted and climate-sensitive tropical environments.

title: The divergent roles of humic- and fulvic-acid DOM in regulating Hg methylation/demethylation in paddy soils
abstract: Understanding mercury (Hg) methylation and demethylation processes in paddy soils is crucial for controlling food contamination and health risks, yet the roles of dissolved organic matter (DOM) fractions remain unclear. A year-long field study, followed by an incubation experiment using Hg isotope tracers ( 202 Hg II and Me 200 Hg), was conducted to investigate how the humic acid (HA) and fulvic acid (FA) fractions regulate these processes. Field correlation results showed significant relationships between DOM properties and MeHg levels (p m - 202 Hg II ) for Hg-bound FA (Hg-FA) and Hg-bound HA (Hg-HA) treatments were 0.91 ± 0.22 and 0.40 ± 0.06 10 -3 d -1 , respectively, and the average demethylation rate constants (K d -Me 200 Hg) were 0.28 ± 0.07 and 0.36 ± 0.11 d -1 . Incubation results revealed that Hg-FA, with low aromaticity and molecular weight, had significantly higher methylation rates than Hg-HA (p < 0.05), suggesting greater bioavailability. Conversely, high-molecular-weight HA, with greater aromaticity and humic character, reduced net methylation potential and promoted MeHg degradation. Hg methylation and demethylation in response to the same DOM fraction varied across the studied sites, highlighting the distinct roles of each fraction's properties in paddy soils. This study broadens the understanding of DOM's roles in Hg fate in rice paddies, demonstrating that net MeHg production is governed by the balance between FA-promoted methylation and HA-promoted demethylation, challenging the traditional view that total DOM concentration is the primary controlling factor.

title: Bromophenols, pentachlorophenol, and chlorinated benzenes in pooled human serum samples from Australia
abstract: ABSTRACT Through various routes humans are constantly exposed to polyhalogenated compounds which are ubiquitous in the environment. Evidence of their harmful environmental and toxic properties led to many of them being classified and regulated as persistent organic pollutants (POPs) under the Stockholm Convention. The analysis of human serum samples enables the assessment of human exposure to these compounds. However, such biomonitoring should not only cover POPs but also halogenated natural products (HNPs) which have very similar structures, and can also be present in humans. The marine environment of Australia is known for its high abundance of HNPs including bromophenols. To consider and compare both classes of polyhalogenated compounds, human serum samples from three general areas in Australia were purposefully pooled using de-identified surplus pathology samples as well as pooled de-identified samples from an occupational cohort (typically 25 donors), i.e. urban areas, coastal areas as well as islands. Overall, 26 serum pools were analyzed for three bromophenols as well as chlorinated phenols, penta- (PeCB) and hexachlorobenzene (HCB). Pentachlorophenol (PCP) showed the highest levels in all serum pools. One serum sample with donors from a remote island showed exceptionally high levels of PCP (10,500 pg/mL serum) and 2,6-dibromophenol (2,6-DBP, 1,500 pg/mL serum). Typically, 2,4,6-tribromophenol was the 2 nd most abundant analyte (up to 140 pg/mL serum). However, the determined wide ranges of concentrations in the pools from the three general areas were overlapping. Significant differences between urban-dominated regions and islands as well as the coast were only found for 2,4-DBP, 2,6-DBP and HCB.

title: Composition-controlled NaOH/Na2CO3 fusion activation of coal gasification slag: Structural reconstruction, cementitious reactivity, and environmental performance
abstract: Coal gasification slag (CGS) contains potentially reactive aluminosilicate phases, but its use in cement-based materials is limited by the low accessibility of Si- and Al-bearing species within its highly connected network. To overcome this limitation, a composition-controlled NaOH/Na 2 CO 3 fusion strategy was adopted, in which the total alkali addition was fixed at 8 wt% of CGS for all alkali-containing formulations while the NaOH/Na 2 CO 3 ratio was systematically varied to investigate the composition-dependent activation of CGS. The resulting changes were evaluated through strength activity index measurements, R 3 calorimetry, elemental dissolution, phase evolution, structural characterization, and environmental and economic assessment. Among the investigated formulations, H6-C2 exhibited the highest activation efficiency. Its 28 d strength activity index reached 94.1%, representing an increase of 10.4% over H0-C0, while the cumulative heat release in the R 3 test reached 285.39 J/g SCM. After 48 h of dissolution, the released Si and Al concentrations increased to 47.9292 and 26.7225 mg/L, respectively. Spectroscopic and phase analyses showed a decrease in the FTIR-derived polymerization degree to 0.5148 together with substantial phase redistribution toward Na-bearing silicate and aluminosilicate phases. These changes are consistent with reduced Si-O-T network connectivity and greater accessibility of Si- and Al-bearing constituents after fusion. The dissolution kinetic fitting further suggested contributions from both interfacial reaction and diffusion-related resistance to the observed Si and Al release. H6-C2 also reduced embodied energy, global warming potential, and production cost by 27.1%, 75.0%, and 46.5%, respectively, relative to ordinary Portland cement. Overall, the optimized NaOH/Na 2 CO 3 ratio enhanced CGS reactivity while limiting environmental and economic burdens, supporting its value-added utilization as a lower-impact supplementary cementitious material.

title: Multifunctional MoS2/CNTs/chitosan hybrid hydrogel sponge for efficient solar-driven seawater desalination and wastewater purification
abstract: Solar-driven interfacial evaporation provides an eco-friendly and potentially effective method to address global freshwater shortages. However, designing multifunctional solar evaporators capable of high-efficiency evaporation and effective wastewater purification remains significant technical challenges. Herein, we have fabricated a scalable and self-cleaning solar evaporator (MoS 2 /CNTs/CS@MS, abbreviated as MCCM) via strategic integration of MoS 2 , chitosan (CS), carbon nanotubes (CNTs), and melamine sponge (MS) into a hybrid materials system. The chitosan-modified melamine sponge immobilized MoS 2 /CNTs through robust electrostatic interactions, while simultaneously constructing hydrophilic pathways to facilitate mass and water transport. With a remarkable evaporation rate of 1.82 kg·m -2 ·h -1 (about 7.9 times that of natural evaporation, 0.23 kg·m -2 ·h -1 ), the MCCM evaporator also exhibited exceptional salt tolerance in 20 wt% NaCl brine, owing to synergistic capillary forces, porous structure, and hydrophilicity. MoS 2 /CNTs in MCCM improved light absorption property and promoted photoinduced charge separation, achieving 98.27 % of CR degradation under solar irradiation. With 22.45 kg·m -2 freshwater output in 9 h of natural solar light, desalinated water by MCCM not only meets WHO and EPA drinking water standards, but also effectively supports plant germination. By integrating solar evaporation with photocatalysis, this MCCM offers a viable solution for sustainable water purification in marine and industrial settings.

title: Application of food waste digestates and digestate-derived biochar for mitigating antibiotic, Pb, and ARGs pollution in soil containing biodegradable microplastics: The key role of exogenous dissolved organic carbon and organic nitrogen
abstract: The widespread use of biodegradable plastic mulch films and organic manure in agriculture has led to the accumulation of biodegradable microplastics (BMPs), heavy metals, and antibiotics in soil. In this study, three food waste-derived soil amendments, including digestion liquid (DL), digested food waste (DFW), and DFW-derived biochar (DFW-BC), were evaluated for their ability to mitigate co-pollution of Pb, sulfamethazine (SM2), and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in soil containing poly(butylene succinate) microplastics (PBS-MPs). All amendments enhanced SM2 dissipation, and DFW and DFW-BC facilitated the transformation of acid-soluble Pb into less mobile fractions, whereas DL exhibited a more modest effect on Pb immobilization. Regarding ARGs, DL amendment reduced the relative abundances of intl1 and sul1 by 21.6% and 35.0%, respectively. DFW amendment achieved reductions of 77.6% for intl1 and 57.1% for sul2, while DFW-BC amendment reduced them by 17.8% and 28.6%, respectively. Correlation network analysis suggested that Bacillaceae was identified as a potential host of sul1 and intl1, whereas sul2 potential hosts mainly belonged to the phylum Proteobacteria. Mechanistically, these amendments primarily drove changes in the soil bacterial community by increasing soil dissolved organic matter (DOM) and total dissolved nitrogen (TDN) contents, while reducing water-soluble SM2 concentration, thereby suppressing the proliferation of potential ARGs hosts such as Bacillaceae and mitigating soil ARGs contamination. This study demonstrates that food waste-derived amendments, as value-added reutilization resources, offer a promising strategy for the remediation of soils co-contaminated with BMPs and multiple pollutants.

title: In situ mechanochemical carbonation enables carbon-negative detoxification and upcycling of municipal solid waste incineration fly ash
abstract: Municipal solid waste incineration fly ash (MSWI FA) as a hazardous waste in many countries is characterized by strong alkalinity, enrichment of multiple heavy metals, and high chloride content, making its detoxification and utilization a major global challenge. Herein, we propose an in situ mechanochemical carbonation (MC) that simultaneously couples ball milling with wet carbonation, thereby accelerating CO 2 absorption and enabling rapid detoxification (under the evaluated leaching conditions) and resource-oriented upcycling of FA. Additive-free MC substantially enhanced FA reactivity, likely through increased exposure of reactive surfaces and enhanced access to unreacted reactive phases during milling, achieving a CO 2 absorption of 124 g/kg-FA in 40 min (twice that of conventional wet carbonation) and 83% of theoretical CO 2 absorption potential. Net CO 2 balance assessment considering energy- and reagent-related carbon emissions within the defined process boundary indicated the carbon-negative potential of MC treatment (e.g., -95.6 kg CO 2 /t-FA after 40 min treatment). MC-induced deep carbonation reduced Cl content in FA by ∼67% compared with conventional carbonation, yielding a final Cl content of 0.223%. Introduction of additives (NaOH, NaH 2 PO 4 , and/or trimercapto-s-triazine trisodium salt) into MC treatment further increased CO 2 absorption by up to 68% and simultaneously decreased the short-term leaching concentration of multiple heavy metals (i.e., Pb, Cd, Cu, Cr, Zn, Ni) by >94%, with the immobilization effects attributable to pH regulation and additive-induced mineral formation and complexation.

title: Biochemical responses of Mytilus galloprovincialis to individual and binary exposures to PFDoA, bisphenol A and tricresyl phosphate: Exposure and post-exposure dynamics
abstract: This study investigated the biochemical responses of the mussel Mytilus galloprovincialis both immediately after exposure (14 days) and following a subsequent recovery period (14 days) in uncontaminated conditions. Mussels were exposed to bisphenol A (BPA), perfluorododecanoic acid (PFDoA), and tricresyl phosphate (TCP), either individually at a nominal concentration of 20 ng/L or in binary mixtures containing 20 ng/L of each compound (40 ng/L total nominal concentration). Biomarkers of aerobic metabolism, energy reserves, antioxidant defenses, esterase-mediated biotransformation, oxidative damage, and cholinergic function were assessed at the end of both periods. At the end of exposure, BPA was associated mainly with reduced electron transport system activity, PFDoA with modulation of antioxidant responses, and TCP with increased lipid peroxidation and altered acetylcholinesterase activity. After transfer to clean seawater, some responses approached period-specific control values, whereas others persisted or became more evident. BPA-exposed mussels retained lower aerobic metabolic capacity; PFDoA-exposed mussels showed continued modulation of glutathione peroxidase and total antioxidant capacity; TCP-exposed mussels retained elevated lipid peroxidation and incomplete restoration of acetylcholinesterase activity; and the TCP/PFDoA treatment showed increased metabolic, carboxylesterase and antioxidant responses. Binary exposures modified the biochemical profiles in an endpoint-dependent manner, but the experimental design does not permit formal classification as additive, synergistic, or antagonistic. Because exposure concentrations and tissue burdens were not analytically verified, the mechanistic interpretation of persistence and recovery is limited. Overall, post-exposure responses were only partially reversible and differed among endpoints, supporting the inclusion of post-exposure periods and period-specific controls in ecotoxicological assessments.

title: Spatio-temporal trends in wildfire smoke exposures at schools and childcare centers in the United States and implications for child and adolescent health
abstract: Background Wildfires are on the rise in the Unites States. Epidemiological evidence demonstrates that wildfire smoke exposure is harmful to health, especially for children and adolescents. We quantified temporal and regional trends in wildfire smoke exposure at United States public schools and childcare centers to inform risk assessment, mitigation strategies, and policy. Methods We derived annual smoke days (binary indicator of wildfire “smoke day” versus “non-smoke day” determined using smoke plume identification from satellite imagery and simulated air trajectories from fire locations), and student-smoke-days for public schools (n=115,612) and childcare centers (n=131,372) across the United States from 2006-2023 using national daily wildfire PM 2.5 products. Indoor/outdoor PM 2 . 5 mass concentration ratios were derived for West Coast facilities (n=71) with nearby PurpleAir monitors. Results Mean annual smoke days increased from 6.8 to 54.4 at schools (during the academic year) and from 9.4 to 112.2 at childcare centers (year-round) between 2006 and 2023, totaling 2.64 and 1.02 billion student-smoke-days in 2023, respectively. Smoke-day counts were highest in the South and Midwest, while the West experienced the most severe days. Median (IQR) indoor/outdoor PM 2 . 5 ratios for schools across working-hours was 0.86 (0.54, 1.39), indicating substantial but variable building protection. Conclusions Exposure to wildfire smoke days at youth educational facilities increased rapidly over time, especially between 2019 and 2023, with substantial regional differences in magnitude and severity. Schools and childcare centers can play a pivotal role in wildfire smoke preparedness through implementation of clean-air strategies and exposure mitigation plans to protect child and adolescent health.

title: Transgenerational effects of paternal in utero arsenic exposure on MASLD-like phenotypes
abstract: Previous study indicated that early-life arsenic (As) exposure caused adulthood metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD)-like phenotypes. This study aimed to investigate the impacts of paternal in utero As exposure on MASLD-like phenotypes in offspring. Pregnant dams received NaAsO 2 (15 mg/L) through drinking water. In utero As-exposed male pups were designated as F0 mice and mated with untreated females to produce F1 offspring. F1 males were subsequently mated with untreated females to generate F2 offspring, both without further As exposure. MASLD-like phenotypes were evaluated in F1 and F2 offspring. On PNW28, As-exposed F1 offspring exhibited hepatic steatosis, glucose intolerance, insulin resistance, and obesity, accompanied by altered metabolic hormones, such as GLP-1, GIP, insulin, leptin, and ADPN. The core MASLD-like phenotypes, including hepatic steatosis, glucose intolerance and insulin resistance, exhibited transgenerational transmission from F1 to F2 generations. In F2 offspring, these metabolic abnormalities were detected at PNW45 but not at PNW28, predominantly in male offspring. In contrast, As-induced obesity and metabolic hormone alterations exhibited transgenerational attenuation. F2 offspring retained only adipocyte hypertrophy, with no significant changes in white or brown adipose tissue weight. Furthermore, hormonal alterations in F2 mice were limited to reduced GLP-1 levels in females and elevated insulin and ADPN levels in males, while other altered hormones normalized. This study is the first to confirm that paternal in utero As exposure causes MASLD-like phenotypes in F1 offspring and transgenerational transmission to F2 generation.

title: Synergistic Ce-Ov-Mn and Cu-Ov-Mn asymmetric centers in CeCu-MnO2 for efficient toluene oxidation by facilitating key oxygen species cycling
abstract: MnO 2 -based materials have been extensively investigated for the elimination of aromatic volatile organic compounds (VOCs). Nevertheless, their practical performance is limited by sluggish activation-consumption-replenishment kinetics of key oxygen species. Here, we have successfully engineered Cu-O-Mn and Ce-O-Mn asymmetric centers within MnO 2 . Their successful construction not only gives rise to Cu-O v -Mn and Ce-O v -Mn defect sites but also refines the electron transfer efficiency between metal and oxygen species in CeCu-MnO 2 . The Cu-O v -Mn or Ce-O v -Mn defect sites promote the adsorption of gaseous oxygen onto the CeCu-MnO 2 surface while simultaneously facilitating the migration of lattice oxygen, thereby substantially accelerating the activation-consumption-replenishment cycle of reactive oxygen species. Consequently, CeCu-MnO 2 exhibits catalytic activity markedly superior to that of Ce-MnO 2 and Cu-MnO 2 . Its T 90 is lowered by 25 °C and 33 °C relative to Cu-MnO 2 and Ce-MnO 2 , respectively, and its low-temperature reaction rate is nearly twice as high as that of the latter two. Moreover, CeCu-MnO 2 demonstrates excellent catalytic stability and water resistance, confirming its immense potential for industrial application.

title: Cellular toxicity and apoptosis-related responses to individual and combined exposure to microplastics and perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) in Hediste diversicolor coelomocytes
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are emerging contaminants of increasing concern in marine ecosystems due to their widespread occurrence and ability to adsorb and transport hazardous chemicals such as perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS). PFOS is a persistent per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) with high environmental stability, bioaccumulative potential, and well-documented toxicity to aquatic organisms. However, the combined effects of MPs and PFOS on marine invertebrates remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the individual and combined effects of environmentally relevant concentrations of MPs (50 mg kg -1 sediment) and PFOS (0.1, 0.5, and 1 μg kg -1 sediment) on the coelomic fluid of the benthic polychaete Hediste diversicolor after 7 days of sediment exposure. The MPs consisted of particles <30 μm composed of PVC, PET, PS, HDPE, LDPE, and PE with heterogeneous morphologies. PFOS accumulated in the coelomic fluid in a dose-dependent manner, with higher concentrations observed under co-exposure, suggesting that the presence of MPs may influence PFOS bioavailability and uptake. This increased accumulation was accompanied by pronounced cytotoxic and genotoxic effects, including lysosomal membrane destabilization, increased micronucleus frequency, and DNA fragmentation. Co-exposure also upregulated the pro-apoptotic genes p53, Bax, and Casp-3, while downregulating the anti-apoptotic gene Bcl-2, indicating activation of apoptotic pathways. Overall, the effects of combined exposure varied according to the endpoint and PFOS concentration, with co-exposure producing greater responses for some endpoints but not consistently across all treatments. These findings highlight the increased hazard posed by the co-occurrence of MPs and PFOS and emphasize the need to consider contaminant mixtures in marine environmental risk assessment.

title: Enhanced remediation of wastewater impacted by acid mine drainage at low temperature using sulfate-reducing bacteria immobilized in biomass-amended PVA-SA beads
abstract: Acid mine drainage (AMD) is a severe environmental threat owing to its high acidity, sulfate, and heavy metal content with devastating effects on watershed ecosystems.
