In cold-climate mining regions, water temperature below 15 °C severely limits conventional bioremediation, as most functional bacteria are mesophilic. In this study, we tested the hypothesis that sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) capable of AMD remediation persist in cold mine environments and that their activity can be enhanced via gradient cold acclimation. Indigenous functional consortia were enriched and acclimated from AMD-contaminated sediments collected in the Shandi River basin, China. Metagenomic analysis confirmed the dominance of Desulfovibrio, the presence of complete dissimilatory sulfate reduction pathways, alongside cold-adaptation and acid-tolerance genes. Free-living cells were then immobilized in polyvinyl alcohol-sodium alginate (PVA-SA) beads containing corn straw pretreated with raw AMD. The results demonstrated that the beads possessed a porous network structure and enabled sustained carbon source release, attaining a sulfate removal efficiency of 98.5% in synthetic mining wastewater (SMW) at 12 °C. Solid-phase characterization verified that sulfate and heavy metals were transformed into stable crystalline phases. Furthermore, Microbial community profiling revealed that fermentative bacteria dominated the consortium, which could convert straw into bioavailable substrates that sustained SRB metabolism. These results demonstrated that immobilized bacteria were potentially and practically applied to AMD-impacted wastewater remediation despite the cold climate.

title: Early-life exposure to environmental pollutants and endocrine disruptors: emerging risks and mechanistic insights in maternal, fetal, and child health
abstract: Exposure to environmental pollutants and endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) in early life is a critical public health issue because it can alter developmental programming that impacts susceptibility to disease throughout life. The prenatal and early postnatal periods are times of vulnerability when exposure to environmental stressors may impact endocrine signalling, placental function, epigenetic regulation, and metabolic homeostasis. There is increasing evidence that exposure to bisphenols, phthalates, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), pesticides, heavy metals, and air pollutants has been associated with pregnancy outcomes, neurodevelopmental disorders, metabolic dysfunction, endocrine abnormalities and reproductive impairments. Exposomics, high-resolution mass spectrometry, biomonitoring, and passive sampling technologies have made crucial advances in characterising complex environmental exposures. At the same time, novel methods such as multi-omics, single-cell sequencing, spatial biology and microbiome studies have yielded more detailed mechanistic understanding of how environmental factors can impact developmental processes via epigenetic, inflammatory, oxidative stress, and endocrine pathways. The placenta has emerged as a valuable biomarker matrix for assessing fetal exposure and developmental programming. Exposure routes, biomonitoring methods, placental processes, molecular and epigenetic modifications, and the impacts of early-life environmental exposures on neurodevelopment, metabolism, endocrine function, and reproduction are all summarised in this review. It also emphasises current advancements in exposure assessment, preventive measures, and policy frameworks, highlighting the importance of life-course perspectives and environmental justice. To identify important windows of susceptibility, improve risk assessment, and develop strategies to safeguard maternal and child health, exposomics in conjunction with systems biology and longitudinal epidemiological approaches will be essential.

title: Retraction notice to “Development of zinc ferrite nanoparticles with enhanced photocatalytic performance for remediation of environmentally toxic pharmaceutical waste diclofenac sodium from wastewater” [Environ. Res. 216 (2023) 114500]
Retraction notice to “Artificial neural networks modeling for lead removal from aqueous solutions using iron oxide nanocomposites from bio-waste mass” [Environ. Res. 199 (2021) 111370]
Quantifying the drivers of ozone formation using localized photochemical reactivity and double machine learning
abstract: Surface ozone (O 3 ) pollution remains severe in many Chinese cities despite declining precursor emissions, reflecting nonlinear interactions among emissions, meteorology, chemistry, and transport. Here, we integrated hourly observations from Yuncheng in the Fenwei Plain during 2020-2022 with a localized observation-constrained box model to develop a photochemically constrained double machine learning (DML) framework. From 2020 to 2022, the annual mean O 3 concentration in Yuncheng increased from 76.2 to 79.9μg m -3 . Compared with clean days, O 3 -polluted days had stronger southeasterly winds, higher temperatures, lower humidity. Box-model calculations indicated that O 3 formation in Yuncheng was VOC-limited during the pollution season. Using MCM v3.3.1, we derived a localized maximum incremental reactivity scale for Yuncheng (MIR-YC), with reactivity decreasing in the order isoprene > anthropogenic alkenes > aromatics > oxygenated VOCs > alkanes. The resulting localized ozone formation potentials were subsequently used in place of measured VOC concentrations to constrain the machine-learning analysis. The optimized random forest model achieved a test R 2 of 0.923, and SHAP analysis attributed 44.6% and 26.4% of predictive importance to local precursors and photochemical drivers, respectively. DML then quantified conditional marginal responses beyond predictive attribution, associating a 1 °C temperature increase with a 4.04μg m -3 increase in O 3 after adjustment for observed covariates. This integrated framework links localized chemical sensitivity with observation-based atmospheric responses, providing a quantitative basis for locally tailored VOC-NOx control strategies.

title: Biomimetic design of glutamic acid-functionalized polyacrylonitrile fiber: Advanced phosphate capture via intermolecular weak interactions
abstract: Excessive phosphorus discharge is a primary driver of aquatic eutrophication, highlighting the need for efficient and sustainable phosphate removal technologies. In phosphate-binding protein PstS, amino acid residues construct multiple hydrogen-bonding networks with phosphate ions, facilitating high-affinity phosphate sequestration. Inspired by this mechanism, glutamic acid was employed as a functional monomer and was introduced onto polyacrylonitrile fiber to mimic the intermolecular weak interaction environment of the active site of PstS, generating the glutamic acid-functionalized polyacrylonitrile fiber (PANF-Glu). It exhibits desirable adsorption performance (maximized at 123.69 mg P/g) over a wide pH range (3-11). It also showed outstanding regeneration performance. >91% adsorption capacity was retained after 5 adsorption-desorption cycles. Characterization and theoretical calculations indicate that abundant carboxyl and amine groups on the surface of PANF-Glu allowed the formation of a stable hydrogen-bonding network with phosphate ions. The enhanced hydrophilicity of the adsorption interface further facilitates the diffusion and mass transfer of phosphate ions towards the adsorbent surface. Electrostatic attractions from protonated amine groups and van der Waals forces rendered an enhanced phosphate capture. By establishing a synergy between hydrogen bonding and electrostatic attraction, this material achieves efficient phosphate adsorption and regeneration, offering a valuable example for the development of phosphate adsorbents based on multiple intermolecular weak interactions. Furthermore, this biomimetic design involves no metal, avoiding the risk of secondary pollution caused by potential metal leaching. Consequently, PANF-Glu holds theoretical and practical promise for advanced phosphate removal from water and wastewater, which may have important implications for the development of advanced phosphate adsorption materials.

title: Integrated evidence-based assessment of in vitro and in vivo data supports that the effects of phenmedipham in Xenopus laevis are consistent with generalised toxicity rather than thyroid disruption
abstract: Phenmedipham (PMP), an herbicide registered for various crops across different geographies, is under re-approval in Europe and should be evaluated for potential endocrine-disrupting properties according to the current legislation on pesticide active substances. This paper describes an evidence-based assessment of potential thyroid-mediated effects of PMP in Xenopus laevis as model species for thyroid modality. As an indication of thyroid activity, rat thyroperoxidase inhibition was reported in a single in vitro assay in the US-EPA ToxCast database. The results of a 27-day Extended Amphibian Metamorphosis Assay with X. laevis showed very little evidence of the consequences of potential thyroperoxidase inhibition in vivo. A minor non-statistically significant delay of 0.76 days in the mean time to reach metamorphic climax was estimated for tadpoles from the highest treatment group (0.5 mg/L) which reached the metamorphic climax at a significantly lower rate over time compared to control. As it is within the historical control data variability (±2.72 days), the estimated developmental delay of 0.76 days is not adverse for individuals, and no population-level impact is therefore expected in field. Other statistically significant low-magnitude effects (e.g. ≤ 4.2% for reduced survival and growth) were observed at the highest PMP concentration at study termination. Minor statistically significant histopathological changes in the thyroid of tadpoles from the highest treatment group could be explained by the effects on developmental timing. Overall, the response pattern observed in X. laevis was consistent with generalised toxicity and thus, PMP does not meet the endocrine disruption identification criteria for thyroid modality.

title: Functionalized hierarchical cellulose aerogel for simultaneous removal of Pb(II), Cd(II), and Cr(VI): performance enhancement and adsorption mechanisms
abstract: To address the combined pollution of Pb(II), Cd(II), and Cr(VI) in water, this study successfully fabricated aldehyde-functionalized aerogels (ACK) and thiol-functionalized aerogels (BCK) with hierarchical structures via periodate oxidation and L-cysteine grafting modification using α-cellulose as raw material, and systematically evaluated their synchronous adsorption performance toward the ternary heavy metal system. The results showed that both BCK and ACK could simultaneously remove Pb(II), Cd(II), and Cr(VI), and the adsorption capacity of BCK was significantly superior to that of ACK. The adsorption process involved both chemisorption and multilayer adsorption. The adsorption of Cd(II) and Cr(VI) onto BCK was endothermic and spontaneous, whereas that of Pb(II) was exothermic. Functional groups on the aerogel, including thiol, amino, hydroxyl, and carboxyl groups, collectively promoted the efficient removal of Pb(II), Cd(II), and Cr(VI) through complexation, chelation, electrostatic interactions, and redox reactions. After five regeneration cycles, the adsorption capacities of BCK for Pb(II), Cd(II), and Cr(VI) remained above 82%, indicating good reusability. This study provides a new strategy for developing green, efficient, and renewable biomass-based adsorbent materials for Pb(II), Cd(II), and Cr(VI) removal.

title: Ecological partitioning and functional specialization of Thermoproteota across multiple trench sediments
abstract: Thermoproteota (formerly referred to as Thaumarchaeota) are phylogenetically divided into ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA) affiliated with Nitrososphaeria and basal non-ammonia-oxidizing archaea (non-AOA). While both groups co-existed in the hadal trenches, their differentiations across multiple trenches remain poorly understood. Here, 25 medium- and high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), including 18 AOA and 7 non-AOA representatives, were generated from metagenomics of Diamantina, Kermadec, Mariana-Yap trench sediments. AOA MAGs of Nitrosopumilales encompassing CSP1-1, DRGT01 and Nitrosopumilus exhibited chemoautotrophic potential with broader niche widths and higher diversity across trenches. Potential nitrification rates (PNR) were predominantly associated with AOA activity and exhibited clear depth-/trench-dependent patterns, driven by NH 4 + availability. In contrast, the non-AOA lineage diverged approximately earlier (∼2.66 Ga), whereas the divergence between B1T1B5 and JAPUIC01 was estimated at ∼1.91 Ga during the Paleoproterozoic. B1T1B5 harbored auto/mixotrophic traits, whereas JAPUIC01 exhibited a metabolically flexible, heterotrophic strategy potentially suited to anaerobic niches. The pronounced niche partitioning and functional specialization of AOA and non-AOA Thermoproteota across geographically isolated trenches were based on their genomic traits, likely an integrated consequence of microbial ecological adaptation and strong purifying selection of the local environmental condition. The findings provide a unified ecological and evolutionary framework for understanding Thermoproteota diversification in the deep ocean and reveals how functional specialization and genomic adaptive evolution shape nitrogen cycling in Earth’s deepest ecosystems.

title: Hemihydrate phosphogypsum as a waste-derived sulfate source for low-carbon supersulfated cement: Hydration regulation and strength-normalized environmental performance
abstract: Hemihydrate phosphogypsum (HPG) can serve as a waste-derived sulfate source in low-clinker supersulfated cement (SSC), expanding phosphogypsum utilization while reducing demand for natural gypsum. This study examines how HPG content governs the temporal evolution of sulfate supply and how this evolution relates to hydration, pore structure, and long-term strength in SSC co-activated with ferroaluminate clinker (FAC), carbide slag (CS), and sodium silicate (SS). Mixtures containing 5-25 wt% HPG were evaluated for compressive strength. The 10, 15, and 20 wt% HPG mixtures were further analyzed by hydration kinetics, pore-solution chemistry, quantitative phase analysis, and microstructural characterization. Composite-activated SSC developed 10.23-14.36 MPa at 1 d, corresponding to a 205.4-328.7% increase over the CS-activated reference. The 15 and 20 wt% HPG mixtures reached 65.54 and 63.76 MPa at 28 d and continued to increase to 81.56 and 78.79 MPa at 270 d, respectively. At 10 wt% HPG, sulfate depletion after early hydration constrained continued ettringite formation and late-age pore refinement. At 20 wt% HPG, sustained reaction of ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBS) generated slightly more ettringite and C-(A)-S-H, but a larger fraction of pores >50 nm remained, diminishing the strength efficiency of the additional hydration products. The 15 wt% HPG mixture provided the most favorable coupling of sulfate supply, hydrate accumulation, pore refinement, and strength, and achieved the lowest 28 d energy- and carbon-intensity indices among the investigated mixtures.

title: Thermophilic pig manure compost as an additive for sewage sludge composting: humification efficiency and changes in heavy metals, antibiotics, and antibiotic resistance genes
abstract: Thermophilic livestock manure compost harbors microbes with vigorous metabolic activity, making it a promising natural inoculant for composting systems. However, there has been no documented application of thermophilic livestock manure compost as an additive in sewage sludge composting. The impacts of this strategy on shifts in heavy metal speciation and the removal of antibiotics and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) during sludge composting remain poorly understood. In this study, thermophilic pig manure compost materials (TM) were used as additives and incorporated into sewage sludge composting to evaluate its effects and underlying mechanisms on humification efficiency, heavy metal immobilization, and the removal of antibiotics and ARGs. Results indicate that TM significantly improved organic matter degradation rate, germination index, and humification index by 26.9%, 18.9%, and 35.8%, respectively, while reduced the composting maturation period by at least five days. TM significantly decreased both the concentrations and exchangeable fractions of Zn, Pb, As, and Ni in sludge compost, as well as their accumulation in corn seedlings (P < 0.05), by modulating key environmental factors (moisture content, carbon-to-nitrogen ratio, and pH) and influencing the microbial community structure. TM facilitated the removal of tetracycline, sulfonamide, and quinolone antibiotics, and reduced the prevalence of ermA, ermF, sul1, sul2, tetM, and tetX by decreasing the abundance of ARGs-hosting microorganisms (e.g., Pseudomonas, Streptomyces, Flavobacterium, Bordetella, Escherichia, and Klebsiella) and mobile genetic elements (e.g., intl1, intI2, and Tn916/1545). These results offer a scientific basis for the resource recovery and utilization of sewage sludge.

title: Association between organophosphate esters and incident type 2 diabetes risk: modification by genetic risk and lifestyle
abstract: People are widely exposed to organophosphate esters (OPEs) as flame retardants and plasticizers. OPEs may affect type 2 diabetes (T2D) risk, but prospective evidence is limited and inconsistent, and the modifying effects of genetic and lifestyle factors remain unclear. The present nested case-control study within the Dongfeng-Tongji cohort of retired adults (median age: 62 years; mean follow-up: 4.6 years) included 981 pairs of incident T2D cases and controls matched by age and sex. We measured 10 plasma OPEs in baseline blood samples and used conditional logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, quantile g-computation, and Bayesian kernel machine regression to examine their association with T2D risk. We examined effect modification by lifestyle and polygenic risk score. Each twofold increase in plasma triphenyl phosphate (TPHP) was associated with 6% higher odds of T2D (odds ratio, OR = 1.06; 95% confidence interval, CI: 1.01-1.11). The odds were 49% higher in the highest tertile versus the lowest (OR = 1.49, 95% CI: 1.04-2.14). Tri-isobutyl phosphate and tri-n-butyl phosphate (TiBP + TnBP) in the highest tertile showed an inverse association versus the lowest (OR = 0.75, 95% CI: 0.58-0.99). Detectable tri(1-chloro-2-propyl) phosphate (TCPP) was associated with 75% higher odds of T2D versus undetectable levels (OR = 1.75, 95% CI: 1.30-2.36). The overall mixture effect was not significant, with TPHP positive and TiBP + TnBP negative as main contributors. Interaction analysis using relative excess risk (RERI) showed additive synergy for high TPHP combined with an unhealthy lifestyle (RERI = 0.88, 95% CI: 0.09-1.52), low TiBP + TnBP combined with an unhealthy lifestyle (RERI = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.02-1.32), and low TiBP + TnBP combined with high genetic risk (RERI = 0.88, 95% CI: 0.03-1.74). The highest odds of T2D were for high PRS, unhealthy lifestyle, and high TPHP (OR = 7.16, 95%CI: 4.06-12.62) or low TiBP + TnBP (OR = 6.63, 95%CI: 3.83-11.47). Healthy lifestyle may offset OPEs and genetic effects.

title: Fly ash-assisted low-temperature hydrothermal treatment enables deep sludge dewatering by restoring sludge cake water seepage capacity
abstract: Low-temperature hydrothermal treatment (LHT) is an important pretreatment technology for sludge stabilization and resource recovery; however, the associated deterioration in mechanical dewaterability remains a major barrier to its wider application. To alleviate this limitation, this study developed a fly ash (FA)-assisted LHT process and evaluated its effects on sludge dewatering performance and filter cake structure. LHT alone at 120 °C markedly worsened sludge dewatering, whereas FA addition effectively improved the dewatering of LHT-treated sludge, with performance progressively improving as the FA dosages increased within the tested range. For example, compared with LHT alone, FA addition at 25% of sludge dry solids decreased the filter-cake water content (W c ) after pressure filtration from 83.19% to 58.30% and reduced the capillary suction time (CST) by 68.12%. Mechanistic analysis revealed that FA caused an obvious additional release of soluble components and left the net bound-water fraction estimated by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) nearly unchanged. In contrast, the cake compressibility coefficient decreased from 1.10 to 0.50 and the total porosity resolved by X-ray computed tomography (X-CT) increased from 7.34% to 21.07%, while the proportion of connected pores within the identified pore volume increased from 0% to 52.46%. These findings associate the dewatering improvement with reduced cake compressibility and increased pore connectivity, without a corresponding decrease in the DSC-estimated net bound-water fraction. This study highlights the importance of restoring filter-cake structure of LHT-treated sludge and provides a practical route for integrating sludge conditioning with industrial solid-waste utilization.

title: Field trial of all-solid-waste stabilized soda residue for roadway subgrades: mechanical performance and environmental behavior
abstract: Soda residue (SR), a highly alkaline and saline by-product of the ammonia-soda process, remains difficult to reuse at high dosage because of its high water content and soluble-salt release. In this study, an all-solid-waste stabilized soda residue (S-SR) containing 70 wt% SR was validated in a full-scale roadway subgrade to assess field constructability, engineering performance, and environmental behavior under natural exposure. Under low-temperature natural curing, mean California bearing ratio (CBR) increased from 38.6% at 1 d to 164.6% at 28 d, resilient modulus from 260.8 to 388.6 MPa, and dynamic deformation modulus from 65.6 to 199.9 MPa, while rebound deflection decreased from 0.374 to 0.190 mm. Degree of compaction and initial water content jointly controlled spatial variability. Leached Cl - decreased from 3028 mg/L at 1 d to 268 mg/L at 60 d and SO 4 2- from 286 to 15 mg/L. Over five months, lysimeter leachate pH decreased from 10.87 to 8.32 and electrical conductivity from 15,469 to 4236 μS/cm (a 72.6% reduction), indicating gradual decreases in leachate alkalinity and overall dissolved-ion level during the middle-to-late monitoring period. The dynamic cone penetration index (DCPI) showed strong power-law relationships with field mechanical indices (R 2 = 0.94-0.99) and evolved consistently with anion leaching. Compared with reported SR-based systems, S-SR achieved higher SR utilization and 7-d CBR, together with lower material-related cost and production-stage carbon emissions. The study provides field-scale evidence for high-content SR reuse while documenting age-dependent leaching attenuation and field environmental responses under natural exposure.

title: Chitosan-derived carbon/chain-like CoNi composite aerogels for efficient electromagnetic absorption, radar stealth and thermal insulation
abstract: With the increasingly severe problem of electromagnetic radiation pollution, pure carbon aerogels struggle to achieve a wide absorption bandwidth, strong absorption intensity and multifunctional integration at a low filler loading ratio. In this work, chitosan-derived carbon/chain-like CoNi composite aerogels with low bulk density (0.0949 ∼ 0.1019 g/cm 3 ) were prepared by using biomass chitosan as carbon source through solvothermal reaction, solution blending and high-temperature carbonization. The introduction of the chain-like magnetic component not only optimized the impedance matching, but also constructed a dielectric-magnetic cooperative loss system, breaking through the performance limitations of pure carbon aerogels in terms of loss mechanism and structural design. When the content of CoNi alloy was 13.3 wt%, the binary composite aerogel exhibited the best electromagnetic wave absorption performance under the filler loading ratio of only 10 wt% in the paraffin matrix. Specifically, when the matching thickness was 2.75 mm, the minimum reflection loss reached -62.45 dB; when the thickness was 3.07 mm, the maximum absorption bandwidth of 8.08 GHz was achieved. Furthermore, the electromagnetic absorption mechanism of the prepared composite aerogels was clarified. Additionally, the binary composite aerogels possessed excellent thermal insulation performance and good simulated radar stealth performance, demonstrating its potential in various application scenarios. This work provides a new idea for the development of lightweight and multifunctional carbon-based electromagnetic wave absorbers derived from biomass sources.

title: Organ type governs macrophyte decomposition while inundation status drives the decoupling of carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus release in lake wetlands
abstract: Macrophyte-derived organic carbon potentially contributes 66-85% of carbon turnover in lake wetlands. However, the carbon and nutrient fate of its debris decomposition remain elusive, particularly under extreme hydrological regimes. Here, we conducted a 150-day aquatic mesocosm experiment simulating the decomposition of Phragmites australis debris to explore how organ-specific structural traits (leaves, stems, and roots) interact with inundation conditions (Floating, Submerged) to affect debris decomposition and aquatic C release, as well as nutrient dynamics. Our results demonstrate that debris decomposition is associated with organ-specific structural traits rather than inundation conditions. Notably, roots (70.3%-82.7% mass loss) decomposed at a rate comparable to that of leaves (74.2%-80.2% mass loss). Conversely, stems (38.6%-52.4% mass loss), characterized by recalcitrant lignin matrices, degraded at approximately half the foliar rate. Correspondingly, the rapid initial leaching of aboveground tissues generated aquatic carbon peaks within the first 15 days, reaching up to 684 mg/L for dissolved organic carbon and 72 mg/L for particulate organic carbon. Furthermore, inundation conditions drove a stoichiometric decoupling among carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus release. While the submerged condition significantly decelerated structural carbon losses, it significantly facilitated nitrogen losses and near-complete phosphorus leaching (lost 88.2%-95.3%). These findings elucidate that current models basing aboveground aquatic carbon inputs on foliar decomposition or treating fibrous root pools as generalized, homogeneous carbon pools potentially miscalculate overall debris decomposition and C release in littoral wetlands. Our findings provide an empirical basis for balancing carbon preservation against potential nitrogen and phosphorus leaching risk in lake wetland management.

title: Engineered Escherichia coli nrfA reduces cadmium accumulation in rice by modulating bacterial-driven nitrogen cycling and root iron plaque formation
abstract: Nitrogen supply in the rhizosphere affects cadmium (Cd) accumulation in rice. To study bacterial nitrogen transformation effects on Cd uptake in rice, Escherichia coli MG1655 overexpressing nrfA, which encodes cytochrome c nitrite reductase involved in dissimilatory nitrite reduction to ammonium (DNRA), was constructed using a Tn5 transposon system. The nrfA genomic copy number in the engineered strain was approximately 3-fold that in wild-type, and RNA-seq analysis confirmed significantly increased nrfA transcript. Transcriptomics showed enrichment of ribosomes, oxidative phosphorylation, and carbon metabolism pathways. In pot experiments, inoculation with the nrfA-overexpressing strain selectively enriched nitrogen-transformation and iron-cycling taxa, including Actinobacteria and Flavobacterium. Organic nitrogen metabolism gene abundances increased following strain inoculation, particularly in the nrfA-overexpressing treatment; in contrast, denitrification gene abundances decreased, with the greatest reduction in the nrfA-overexpressing treatment. Consistent with these results, soil ammonium nitrogen was 79.4% and 34.1% higher in the nrfA-overexpressing treatment than in uninoculated control and wild-type treatment, respectively. The nrfA-overexpressing strain also promoted iron plaque formation on rice root surfaces, enhancing root Cd interception Cd by >20% versus both other groups. Consequently, compared with uninoculated control, inoculation with nrfA-overexpressing E. coli significantly reduced Cd concentration in rice roots, stems, and grains by 36.2%, 61.0%, and 57.4%, respectively. Collectively, nrfA-overexpressing E. coli reshaped rhizosphere nitrogen cycling toward sustained ammonium nitrogen enrichment, potentially suppressing root Cd uptake through cation competition and strengthening root-surface Cd retention, achieving simultaneous nitrogen enrichment and Cd reduction in paddy soil. This study may offer theoretical support for microbial remediation of Cd-contaminated farmland.

title: Environmental factors associated with long COVID severity: A lifelines cohort analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Environmental components of the external exposome may influence the severity of long COVID, but population-based studies integrating multiple exposures remain scarce. OBJECTIVES: To identify specific environmental factors most strongly associated with long COVID severity, measured as fatigue, quality of life (QoL), and number of symptoms, within a population-based sample of individuals with self-reported long COVID, and to compare results across multiple statistical approaches. METHODS: We analyzed data from 1108 participants in the Lifelines COVID-19 cohort who had self-reported long COVID and had complete covariate information. Outcome information was obtained through questionnaires, and environmental exposures were estimated by geocoded linkage to participant's residential addresses. Analyses were stratified by sex due to large differences in outcome distribution. Exposure-outcome associations were estimated using traditional regression models, horseshoe regression, Bayesian Model Averaging, and Random Forest, with adjustment for age, BMI, and education level. In secondary analyses we further stratified for urbanicity and severity of complaints. RESULTS: Findings varied across analytical methods. The most consistent associations were observed in men: higher neighborhood prevalence of low-income residents was associated with greater fatigue, represented by lower scores (B = -2.09), and greater distance to blue space was associated with lower QoL, represented by higher scores (B = 0.26). We did not find any associations in females, or the number of present symptoms in either males or females. The secondary analyses showed differences between urban and rural populations for all outcomes, and when comparing the most fatigued and worst QoL (75th percentile and above) to less diseased participants. CONCLUSION: In this study, we found modest and context-dependent associations between certain urban features of the external exposome, particularly neighborhood socioeconomic status and access to blue space, and dimensions of long COVID severity. The heterogeneity of results across sex, urbanicity, and analytical methods highlights the need for targeted follow-up studies in diverse populations.

title: Reshaping of PD/A-PN/A cross-feeding and functional complementarity denitrification network by nitrogen load increase: A pilot study on mature landfill leachate treatment
abstract: To address the challenge of low-carbon nitrogen removal from mature landfill leachate, a pilot-scale coupled partial denitrification/anammox-partial nitritation/anammox (PD/A-PN/A) system was operated under two sequential influent NH 4 + -N conditions. Compared with Phase I, Phase II was characterized by a higher influent NH 4 + -N concentration (604.2 ± 54.1 versus 404.0 ± 45.9 mg/L) and coincided with an increase in average total nitrogen (TN) removal efficiency from 52.7 ± 9.2% to 72.3 ± 14.9%, reaching 85.3 ± 7.3% during late Phase II. Meanwhile, the PN/A-unit effluent NO 3 - -N concentration decreased from 73.4 ± 22.4 to 20.2 ± 5.7 mg/L. Activity assays and late-phase microbial profiles were consistent with clearer functional differentiation in Phase II. PN/A flocs showed ammonium-oxidation and nitrite-supply potential. Carrier biofilms provided the major assay-based anammox potential, with SAA increasing from 0.23 to 0.70 g N/(g VSS·d). The relative abundance of Candidatus Brocadia in the carrier biofilm was 2.0% in the Phase I sample and 35.6% in the Phase II sample. PD/A granules retained partial-denitrification potential for residual NO 3 - -N conversion and additional NO 2 - -N supply. Apparent nitrogen balance and stoichiometric estimation indicated that the apparent contribution of the PN/A unit to TN removal increased from 41.0% to 70.8%, while the anammox contribution was estimated at up to 91.3% in Phase II. Collectively, the agreement among nitrogen-species profiles, activity assays, apparent nitrogen balance, and microbial community and functional-gene data was consistent with a putative reciprocal cross-feeding network. In this network, nitrate generated in the PN/A unit was returned to the PD/A unit through recirculation and served as a substrate for partial denitrification, while the resulting nitrite could in turn support anammox-enriched carrier biofilms in the PN/A unit; ammonium-oxidizing flocs within the PN/A unit provided an additional internal nitrite supply. These reciprocal nitrate and nitrite exchanges reinforced cross-unit and cross-biomass functional complementarity.

title: Molecular insights into microbial transformation of dissolved organic matter from a wastewater treatment plant
abstract: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) in treated wastewater influences effluent reactivity and ecological risks. How biological treatment configurations reshape DOM at the molecular level remains unclear. This study integrated molecular characterization, metagenomic microbial community analysis and metatranscriptomic functional profiling, machine-learning interpretation, and dynamic Partial Mantel Distance network analysis to compare DOM transformation in full-scale anaerobic-anoxic-oxic process (A2O) and oxidation ditch process (OD). The A2O exhibited a stronger redox-stage-dependent DOM remodeling than the OD. In the A2O, the final aerobic effluent showed a reduced mean molecular weight of 411.45, higher O/C, and lower H/C, with lipid-like and protein-like compounds decreasing from 35.13% to 15.39% and from 35.70% to 21.44%, respectively, whereas the lignin/CRAM-like fractions increased to 47.64%, indicating preferential removal of labile aliphatic and proteinaceous molecules and enrichment of refractory DOM. The OD retained a higher final molecular weight of 451.43 and a lipid-like fraction of 33.94%, suggesting gradual stabilization under continuous circulation and mixed redox microenvironments. The microbial communities differed significantly between the processes, whereas the enzyme profiles showed weaker separation, indicating functional redundancy. The Random Forest models effectively predicted the DOM molecular fate in both processes, with macro AUC values of 0.8913 and 0.8923 for the A2O and OD, respectively. The dPMD networks revealed intermediate-mediated cascade transformations. The treatment configuration governed DOM persistence, microbial ecological control, and the refractory character of the residual effluent DOM. This study provides a molecular-level theoretical basis for optimizing biological wastewater treatment processes, regulating refractory DOM, and reducing the ecological risks associated with treated wastewater discharge.

title: Rescue of herbicide-suppressed soil bacterial communities by metallic micronutrients links to improved soil aggregate stability
abstract: Metallic micronutrients have the potential to alleviate herbicide-induced impairment of soil bacterial communities and then improve aggregate stability. A survey of maize-producing regions across China was executed to reveal the relationships among typical herbicides, metallic micronutrients, bacterial communities, and soil aggregate stability. Subsequent field trials were conducted to assess the impacts of atrazine, acetochlor, thiencarbazone-methyl·isoxaflutole (TMI), and metallic micronutrients on functional genes. The survey showed that atrazine and acetochlor were negatively correlated with the abundance of the denitrification gene nirS and the proportion of macroaggregates. Structural equation modeling (SEM) demonstrated that atrazine and acetochlor suppressed the proportion of macroaggregates, mainly via reduced nirS abundance, lower soil pH, and decreased microbial diversity. Geodetector analysis further identified joint effects between atrazine and acetochlor, suggesting stronger combined associations with reduced nirS abundance and macroaggregate proportions. SEM analysis indicated that zinc mitigated the impairment of atrazine and acetochlor on the soil aggregate stability by enhancing nirS abundance. Iron exhibited a positive direct path coefficient to macroaggregate proportions. Controlled field trials further verified that atrazine, acetochlor, and TMI significantly reduced nirS abundance relative to the herbicide-free control, whereas zinc amendment significantly increased nirS abundance under TMI exposure, as supported by variance analysis. Consequently, metallic micronutrients can alleviate the inhibitory impacts of herbicides on the abundance of genes involved in essential bacterial functions, and exhibit potential in maintaining soil aggregate stability.

title: Unraveling the microbial mechanisms and electron transfer networks of Cr(VI) driven anaerobic methane oxidation
abstract: Anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM) plays a critical role in mitigating methane emissions, while hexavalent chromium [Cr(VI)] contamination remains a significant challenge in environmental remediation. The coupling of AOM with Cr(VI) reduction offers a promising strategy to simultaneously address heavy metal pollution and methane emissions reduction. However, the exact contribution of Cr(VI)-dependent AOM (Cr-AOM) to methane mitigation, the key functional microorganisms involved, and the underlying methane metabolic pathways and electron transfer mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, we systematically investigated these aspects using a combination of 13 C-labeled methane microcosm experiments, DNA-stable isotope probing (DNA-SIP), meta-omics, electrochemical analysis, and molecular docking simulations. Our findings indicated that Cr-AOM enables concurrent Cr(VI) removal and methane emission reduction, with the AOM potential showing a positive correlation with the isotopic fractionation factor. 13 CH 4 -DNA-SIP analysis identified Methyloceanibacter, Methylocystis, and Candidatus Bathyarchaeia as the key genera mediating Cr-AOM, which synergistically facilitate efficient methane metabolism through inter-microbial cooperation. Metatranscriptomic analysis revealed the presence of an active reverse methanogenesis pathway. Meanwhile, Actinomycetota harbored genes such as norB, narB/G/H, and nirK, indicating a potential nitrogen metabolic capacity that may be linked to AOM through bacterial cross-feeding, thereby coupling methane oxidation with the nitrogen cycle. Furthermore, electron transfer in Cr-AOM was primarily mediated by chromate reductases from Pseudomonadota, cytochrome c, PilA-encoded proteins, and riboflavin, supplemented by a chemical reduction pathway (involving H 2 S). The presence of trace amounts of sulfate was found to enhance the electron transfer process in Cr-AOM, thereby coupling methane oxidation with the sulfur cycle. This study elucidates the metabolic pathways and electron transfer mechanisms of Cr-AOM, providing a theoretical foundation for controlling methane emissions and remediating heavy metal pollution, advancing the conceptual framework of Metal-AOM, and furthering our understanding of the coupling between metal oxide reduction and the biogeochemical cycles of C, N, and S.

title: Interspecific difference in seasonal change of stomatal O3 uptake and annual cumulative stomatal O3 uptake estimated by species-specific Jarvis-type models for 10 Japanese urban greening tree species
abstract: Tropospheric ozone (O 3 ) is a detrimental gaseous air pollutant for human health. Urban greening trees can reduce the atmospheric O 3 concentration in urban areas by absorbing it through the stomata into the leaves, but the most effective species for this purpose remain unclear. This study addresses this gap by developing new species-specific Jarvis-type stomatal conductance (g s ) models for 10 typical Japanese urban tree species. Using these models, we examined the seasonal changes in stomatal O 3 uptake, the annual cumulative stomatal O 3 uptake (COU), and their determining factors in the 10 species. Firstly, developing species-specific g s models is imperative for accurately quantifying O 3 uptake, because the optimal g s models for all the species incorporated limiting functions due to photosynthetic photon flux density (f light ) and leaf phenology (f phen ), while other environmental functions were not necessarily included. Secondly, evergreen trees generally showed greater annual O 3 uptake due to longer leaf duration, whereas deciduous trees had potential for greater O 3 removal in early spring, when atmospheric O 3 concentrations peak. Thirdly, within the five evergreen broad-leaved tree species, Osmanthus fragrans exhibited relatively high physiological activity over a prolonged period, resulting in the highest COU. Within the five deciduous tree species, Styrax japonicus exhibited the highest COU, due to the highest g max and tolerance to relatively high air temperature and vapor pressure deficit, some of which differ from previously reported findings. These insights provide a scientific basis for optimizing urban tree selection to improve air quality.

title: Microbial degradation of 1,2-bis(2,4,6-tribromophenoxy)ethane by a novel bacterial isolate: transformation mechanism and bioaugmentation
abstract: To date, reports on the microbial degradation of 1,2-bis(2,4,6-tribromophenoxy)-ethane (BTBPE) by pure strains remain limited. Herein, a BTBPE-degrading strain--FX-1--affiliated with Bacillus velezensis was isolated for the first time. After 5 days of reaction, a maximum biodegradation efficiency of 72.6% was achieved for 1.0 mg/L BTBPE in the presence of 1.0 g/L glucose as a co-substrate at an initial pH of 7.2 and a temperature of 30°C. Eight identified biodegradation products indicated that debromination, ether bond cleavage and aromatic ring cleavage were the primary biotransformation pathways for BTBPE. Biodegradation by strain FX-1 was shown to reduce the biotoxicity of BTBPE. Integrated analysis of proteomics and RT-qPCR suggested that chemotaxis proteins, ABC transporters, and lipoproteins might facilitate the transmembrane transport of BTBPE. Haloacid dehalogenase, nitrate reductase, and cytochrome P450 enzymes were potentially involved in the biotransformation of BTBPE. Histidine kinase, response regulator, general stress proteins, antioxidant proteins, and chaperone proteins might support the survival of strain FX-1 under BTBPE stress. The addition of 1.0-g/L glucose enhanced the expression of BTBPE-degrading enzymes and stress-responsive proteins. Microcosm experiments suggested that strain FX-1 was a promising candidate for the bioaugmentation of BTBPE-contaminated water, sediment, and soil. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to illuminate the mechanisms of BTBPE transformation by a bacterial strain and propose its potential use in bioremediation.

title: A multimodal fusion framework for predicting the life cycle of aerobic granular sludge: Integration of fluorescence spectra and physicochemical parameters
abstract: Aerobic granular sludge (AGS) undergoes four stages throughout its life cycle, namely Adaptation, Growth, Maturation, and Disintegration. The dynamic evolution of these stages alters granule morphology and structural integrity, thereby affecting wastewater treatment performance and system stability. Therefore, early identification of potential stage transitions in AGS is important for operational management. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have provided new opportunities for predicting the states of complex biological treatment systems. In this study, a multimodal machine learning (MML) model for AGS full life cycle evolution analysis was constructed by integrating three-dimensional excitation-emission matrix (3D-EEM) spectral images with operational physicochemical parameters, achieving life cycle stage identification and short-term prediction. The results showed that the MML model achieved an accuracy of 0.95, outperforming the spectral image-based model (0.72) and the numerical-based model (0.90). Multi-time-span prediction further demonstrated stable short-term performance (Δt ≤ 7 days) with F1-scores above 0.85. In addition, improved SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and guided backpropagation (GBP) were used to analyze feature contributions. Overall, the proposed MML modeling strategy was further extended into a framework for AGS life cycle monitoring, providing early indications of phase evolution and supporting process assessment.

title: Spatial heterogeneity and seasonal dynamics of vegetation–soil carbon storage in shallow lake wetlands of eastern China
abstract: Shallow lake wetlands have important vegetation and soil carbon pools; yet, habitat-level differences in carbon storage among lake types have been insufficiently quantified. In this study, we compared three representative shallow lake wetlands in eastern China, Qin Lake, Changdang Lake, and Hongze Lake, during low- and high-water periods. We combined Sentinel-2-based land-cover classification with field measurements to distinguish aquatic vegetation functional types and to estimate vegetation carbon density, surface soil organic carbon density, and combined vegetation-surface soil organic carbon storage. The three lakes showed distinct habitat composition and carbon-storage structures. Qin Lake had the highest proportion of emergent vegetation, Changdang Lake had the highest proportion of floating-leaved vegetation, and Hongze Lake was dominated by open water with relatively strong aquaculture disturbance. Under the biomass-accounting scheme adopted in this study, emergent vegetation showed the highest estimated vegetation carbon density and generally made a relatively high contribution to the estimated vegetation carbon pool, whereas surface soil carbon dominated the combined carbon pool, accounting for 69.82%-93.93% of total estimated storage. Period-averaged combined carbon storage was 8.75, 85.70, and 1023 kt C in Qin Lake, Changdang Lake, and Hongze Lake, respectively. Between the low- and high-water periods, the combined carbon storage was estimated to be lower in Qin Lake and Hongze Lake but higher in Changdang Lake, reflecting differences in habitat composition and habitat-specific carbon density. These results illustrate the value of habitat-level and functional-type-based carbon accounting for interpreting carbon-storage heterogeneity in shallow lake wetlands.

title: Low-to-moderate arsenic exposure and DNA methylation: A review of life-course evidence and mechanistic insights
abstract: Arsenic exposure affects an estimated 94 to 220 million people worldwide, yet most research has centered on high-dose endemic settings, leaving the epigenetic effects of environmentally relevant exposures undercharacterized. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from 68 studies on DNA methylation alterations associated with low-to-moderate arsenic exposure, integrating human epidemiological, animal, and in vitro data. Gene-specific findings were stage-patterned across the life course, whereas global and repetitive-element methylation findings were heterogeneous. Prenatal exposure perturbs mitochondrial biogenesis, growth and endocrine regulation, vascular development and neurodevelopment. Childhood evidence rests on two studies, implicating mitochondrial, growth-regulatory and mismatch repair genes. In adults, oxidative stress response, cancer and cardiovascular pathways, and metabolic dysfunction are most often affected. Experimental models corroborate several of these processes and show that methylation alterations can persist after exposure ceases. Although CpG-site replication across cohorts remains limited, pathway convergence across independent populations supports biological plausibility. Notably, methylation alterations are detectable at or below the WHO guideline of 10 μg/L, particularly during sensitive developmental windows, although whether these changes lead to disease has not been established. Beyond the nuclear genome, mitochondria are a plausible target for arsenic-induced epigenetic disruption through their roles in one-carbon metabolism and redox regulation. This review critically evaluates mitochondrial DNA methylation findings against five methodological quality criteria and proposes a framework for future investigations, addressing a field where biological rationale has outpaced technical validation. Research priorities include longitudinal designs that link methylation biomarkers to clinical outcomes and intervention trials that assess reversibility to inform regulation.

title: Manganese-crosslinked porous carbon for phosphorus recovery and soil remediation: A sustainable strategy featuring fast adsorption and controlled release
abstract: Developing efficient systems to recover phosphorus (P) from water is critical for mitigating aquatic eutrophication and advancing sustainable P cycling. Herein, a porous carbon skeleton was synthesized via pyrolysis of manganese-crosslinked sodium alginate (Mn/SA-C-S) for efficient P adsorption and subsequent soil remediation. Mn/SA-C-S exhibited rapid P adsorption (14.61 mg/g within 200 min) and controlled release (∼10% desorption over 500 min) via precipitation and surface complexation. The P-rich Mn/SA-C-S (Mn/SA-C-S-P) sustains soil available P (∼109 mg/kg), enhances plant P uptake, and reduces P loss. Crucially, Mn/SA-C-S-P application significantly reshaped the soil microbial community, enriching key functional groups involved in nutrient cycling. Life cycle assessment revealed that Mn/SA-C-S production emits 9.19 kg CO 2 eq, which is 1.9 to 17.62 times lower than values reported in the literature for biochar-based materials. Producing one ton of Mn/SA-C-S-P yields a net benefit of $487.48. This study provides a proof of concept for recovering P from wastewater and reusing it as a resource toward sustainable P management.

title: Impact of cold excess on pregnancy outcomes in women undergoing assisted reproductive technology: A large retrospective cohort study in Anhui, China
abstract: To investigate the association between cold exposure and implantation failure or pregnancy loss during different assisted reproductive technology (ART) exposure windows. This retrospective cohort study included 5905 embryo transfer cycles from the First Affiliated Hospital of the University of Science and Technology of China between 2018 and 2022. Individual cold exposure was quantified using a novel daily mean cold excess (DMCE) metric, calculated based on the 5th, 7.5th, and 10th percentile thresholds of historical temperature distributions. Associations between cold exposure across eight defined windows with implantation failure or pregnancy loss were assessed using logistic regression to estimate odds ratio (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI), adjusting for demographic, clinical, and environmental confounders. Subgroup analyses were performed to explore potential heterogeneity and sensitivity analyses were conducted to test the robustness of our findings. A total of 5905 participants (mean age 30.7 ± 4.6 years) were included, 2543 (43.1%) achieved a live birth. Significant increases in implantation failure or pregnancy loss risk were identified during the window from embryo transfer to the end of the first trimester, each 0.1-unit increase of DMCE was associated with elevated odds of implantation failure or early pregnancy loss, with ORs of 1.07 (95% CI: 1.03-1.11) for severe (DMCE_P5), 1.04 (95% CI: 1.02-1.07) for moderate (DMCE_P7.5), and 1.03 (95% CI: 1.01-1.05) for mild (DMCE_P10) cold definitions. Subgroup analyses revealed greater vulnerability among women with lower education levels and those undergoing fresh embryo transfer during the window from embryo transfer to the end of the first trimester. Results remained consistent across sensitivity analyses. High-intensity cold exposure during the first trimester represents a critical exposure period and independent risk factor for implantation failure or early pregnancy loss in ART pregnancies. These findings underscore the necessity of implementing thermal protection measures from embryo transfer to the first trimester, especially for vulnerable groups during winter months.

title: From atmosphere to surface: The dynamics of urban rainfall chemical pollutants and their determinants at south foot of Qinling Mountain, the geographical boundary between north-south of China
abstract: The Qinling Mountains (QLM) form an important geographic boundary between northern and southern China, resulting in distinct climatic conditions and atmospheric environments. However, the chemical characteristics, controlling factors, and sources of rainfall-related pollutants in urban areas influenced by QLM topography remain poorly understood. The typical urban rainfall observation was carried out at the southern foot of the QLM to explain these issues. Alkaline ions, particularly NH 4 + and Ca 2+ , dominated ion deposition and substantially neutralized rainwater acidity. Ion concentrations and muliti-factors analysis indicated that the variations of precipitation amount and source emissions are primary factors affecting rainwater ion chemistry. Source apportionment showed that marine inputs contributed 68% of Na + and 58% of Cl - , urban dust accounted for 55% of Ca 2+ and 75% of Mg 2+ , and anthropogenic emissions and secondary aerosols were the major sources of NO 3 - , NH 4 + , and SO 4 2- . Compared with the southern QLM region, the northern urban area exhibited lower rainfall but higher pollutant deposition, especially for Ca 2+ and NH 4 + , likely due to stronger anthropogenic emissions such as vehicle activities. This study highlights significant north-south differences in rainfall chemistry across the Qinling Mountains and provides insight into regional atmospheric pollution control.

title: Molecular characteristics and formation mechanisms of chlorinated disinfection byproducts from diatomaceous organic matter: Deciphering intracellular vs. extracellular contributions via FT-ICR MS and machine learning
abstract: Diatom-derived algal organic matter (AOM), including intracellular organic matter (IOM) and extracellular organic matter (EOM), is an important precursor of disinfection byproducts (DBPs) in drinking water sources during diatom blooms. Clarifying the differences in the toxicity and formation mechanisms of chlorinated DBPs between IOM and EOM is crucial for identifying priority removal targets and optimizing drinking water treatment. However, these differences remain poorly understood. In this study, the toxicity, formation characteristics, and underlying mechanisms of IOM-derived DBPs and EOM-derived DBPs were systematically investigated and compared, with a focus on molecular-level interactions. At the same dissolved organic carbon (DOC) concentration (1.135 mgC/L), chlorinated IOM showed higher cytotoxicity than chlorinated EOM. IOM preferentially formed more nitrogenous DBPs, including (semi-)volatile and macromolecular species, whereas EOM produced more carbonaceous DBPs. Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry combined with machine learning revealed distinct molecular signatures of DBP precursors in IOM and EOM. Precursors of high-molecular-weight carbonaceous DBPs had lower unsaturation and oxidation degrees but higher aromaticity, whereas precursors of macromolecular nitrogenous DBPs showed the opposite pattern. Given the substantially higher DOC concentration of IOM than EOM at the same diatom density, IOM should be prioritized for removal. These findings provide molecular-level insight for controlling diatom-related DBP risks in drinking water treatment.

title: Kinetics, radical chemistry and machine-learning-optimized abatement of capecitabine by UV/peroxymonosulfate: simultaneous micropollutant removal and attenuation of disinfection by-products formation potential
abstract: As a widely used anticancer prodrug, capecitabine (CAPT) is poorly removed by conventional treatment and may generate toxic transformation products and disinfection by-products (DBPs). This study systematically evaluated CAPT abatement by UV/peroxymonosulfate (UV/PMS), integrating reaction kinetics, energy analysis, reactive species quantification, machine learning, transformation products identification and subsequent disinfection assessment. UV/PMS reduced CAPT below the quantification limit within 4 min, with the pseudo-first-order rate constant (k obs ) of 0.7854 min -1 and the lowest electrical energy per order (EE/O) among the tested processes. SO 4 • - dominated CAPT oxidation, contributing 65.20% of the overall degradation. HO• contributed 23.92%, while direct UV photolysis and PMS oxidation accounted for 9.94% and 0.94%. The contribution of singlet oxygen was negligible. The second-order rate constants of CAPT with SO 4 • - and HO• were 4.02 × 10 9 and 7.48 × 10 9 M -1 s -1 , and UV/PMS exhibited strong process synergy effect. The PMS dose of approximately 200 μM under mildly alkaline conditions provided a favorable balance between degradation kinetics and energy consumption, whereas natural organic matter exerted the strongest matrix inhibition. XGBoost accurately predicted k obs and EE/O, and Pareto optimization identified a balanced operating point with k obs ≈5.5 min -1 and EE/O ≈ 1.88 kWh m -3 order -1 . Transformation products were tentatively identified and evaluated using DFT calculations, Fukui functions, frontier molecular orbital analysis and elemental ratio analysis. The results suggested that oxidation likely involved the fluoropyrimidine moiety and the aliphatic side chain, followed by hydroxylation, defluorination, deamination, hydrolysis and C-N bond cleavage. UV photodegradation alone increased the halogen reactivity of residual precursors, whereas UV/PMS minimized both total and toxicity-weighted levels of the four targeted DBPs during chlorination and chloramination. In conclusion, UV/PMS combined rapid, energy-efficient CAPT abatement with reduced DBPs formation and the related-toxicity burden.

title: Revealing spatiotemporal NOx emission dynamics in the Yangtze River Delta using physics-informed neural networks and TROPOMI observations
abstract: Accurate estimation of nitrogen oxide (NO x ) emissions is essential for characterizing their impacts on atmospheric environment and supporting air pollution management. This study introduces an innovative inversion framework based on a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN), designed to derive NO x emissions from TROPOspheric Monitoring Instrument (TROPOMI) satellite observations. By embedding the physical laws governing atmospheric processes, this method effectively bridges traditional data assimilation techniques with the computational efficiency of deep learning. Unlike purely data-driven models, it directly integrates physical constraints from atmospheric mass continuity equation into the model training process, thereby avoiding the computational burden associated with chemical transport models (CTMs) and removing the need for CTM simulations for supervision. Application to the Yangtze River Delta region in China (2018-2023) revealed clear spatiotemporal variations in NO x emissions, capturing the reduction during the COVID-19 pandemic and the subsequent recovery. Emission uncertainties were quantified using Monte Carlo dropout, providing robust error estimates alongside the inversion results. The proposed framework provides a computationally efficient and physically grounded basis for NO x emission inversion, with broad applicability to air quality assessment and environmental management.

title: Hierarchical porous flower-like NiO/NiS with S-type heterojunction for deep mineralization of antibiotics
abstract: A 3D flower-like NiO/NiS S-scheme photocatalyst (MNOS-3) was constructed via Ni-MOF calcination and in-situ solvothermal sulfurization. Assembled from 2D ultrathin nanosheets with local topological mesoporous channels, MNOS-3 exhibited broadened visible-light absorption and significantly reduced charge transfer resistance. Under visible light, MNOS-3 achieved an order-of-magnitude kinetic leap compared to pure phases, with rate constants for tetracycline (TC) and oxytetracycline (OTC) reaching 3.85 × 10 -2 min -1 and 3.61 × 10 -2 min -1 , respectively. Radical trapping tests established the ROS contribution level as ·O 2 - > h + > ·OH. XPS and Mott-Schottky analyses confirmed that an interfacial built-in electric field drives an S-scheme charge transfer mechanism, recombining weak carriers while retaining the strongly reducing NiS conduction band (-1.34 V) and oxidizing NiO valence band (+1.59 V). Synergistic ROS attack induced defunctionalization and ring-opening fragmentation of the tetraphenyl skeleton. LC-MS and ECOSAR evaluations confirmed deep mineralization of intermediates into harmless CO 2 and H 2 O with effective toxicity elimination. This work provides a universal strategy for developing highly active, durable S-scheme heterojunctions for environmental remediation.

title: Characterisation of particle-bound PAHs emitted from a residential wood-burning stove and their dependence on combustion phases
abstract: Residential wood combustion is a major global source of air pollution linked to respiratory illness, yet the real-time shifts in emission profiles during a single burn cycle remain poorly understood. This study investigates the phase-resolved dynamics and size distributions of particle-bound polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) from three widespread Central European temperate wood species (beech, black locust, and spruce) burned under nominal conditions in a standard residential stove. Aerosol emissions were separated using a cascade impactor across five distinct combustion phases, with PAH masses quantified via GC-MS/MS. Particulate emission peaked sharply during initial ignition and flaming (intervals #1-#3) for all fuels. PAH emissions followed the same pattern for spruce and black locust, whereas beech showed a delayed PAH maximum in interval #4. These peaks coincided with intense devolatilisation and low flue-gas oxygen, consistent with localised oxygen-deficient combustion. Across all fuels and phases, the PM size distribution remained monomodal, peaking at an aerodynamic diameter of ∼0.1 μm, with the highly respirable fine fraction (PM1) representing 70-89% of the total PM mass. While particle size did not determine specific PAH profiles, chemical composition was influenced by fuel type and combustion stage. Hardwoods (beech and black locust) consistently emitted low-molecular-weight (LMW) PAHs. Softwood (spruce), however, generated an intense initial release of high-molecular-weight (HMW) PAHs, before shifting to LMW species during the burnout phase (intervals #4-#5). These findings indicate that, under the tested conditions, PAHs are predominantly bound to the fine (PM1) particle fraction during the flaming phase, with a shift towards coarser particles observed during burnout, suggesting a potential relevance to health risk.

title: Facilitating non-radical peroxymonosulfate oxidation of tetracyclines driven by struvite crystallization
abstract: Eliminating residual antibiotics during struvite recovery from livestock wastewater is essential to prevent the spread of antibiotic resistance. In this work, the effects of in-situ struvite crystallization on the degradation of typical veterinary antibiotics, tetracyclines (TCs), by non-radical peroxymonosulfate (PMS) oxidation were investigated. Results revealed that the process of struvite crystallization enhanced PMS oxidation of TCs with k obs values reaching 1.95-2.15 times those of PMS alone. 1 O 2 and electron transfer processes were identified as the dominant non-radical pathways. Electrochemical analyses indicated that electron transfer processes would be more active through crystallization than pre-formed crystals in PMS oxidation due to the higher interfacial reactivity. Mg:P molar ratio and pH affected TCs degradation through regulating struvite crystallization and altering the speciation of TCs and PMS, with Mg:P ratio of 1.0 and pH 9.2-9.8 being optimal for facilitating 1 O 2 generation and PMS oxidation. In the presence of humic acid (HA), HA-TCs complexes caused an inhibitory effect on TCs degradation, and excess Mg 2+ mitigated this inhibition by reducing the direct association between TCs and HA. Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR-MS) and fluorescence spectroscopy analyses revealed that HA underwent selective molecular restructuring, with nitrogen-containing and highly condensed aromatic components being converted into more oxygenated and less aromatic products through oxygenation, which could further favor electron transfer pathways. This study highlights that struvite crystallization enhances non-radical oxidation and provides new insights into antibiotic removal with simultaneous phosphorus recovery in livestock wastewater.

title: Privileged in-situ deposited MnOx mediates efficient inorganic nitrogen removal during the treatment of actual mine-tailing wastewater in single-chamber microbial electrolysis cells
abstract: Sustainable, cost-effective and stable single-chamber microbial electrolysis cells (MECs) for the treatment of typical actual mine-tailing wastewater (MTW) containing ternary components of dissolved manganese, inorganic nitrogen (NH 4 + -N and NO 3 - -N) meeting the China national discharge standards of pollutants from the rare earths industry are demonstrated over 100 days fed-batch operation. The MECs inoculated with anammox granular sludge initially induced Mn removal and privileged the in-situ deposition of oxygen vacancies (O v ) rich nanoscale manganese oxides (MnO x ) over the graphite felt electrodes. The deposited MnO x mediated, more preferentially, the biotic (rather than the electrochemical) conversion of inorganic nitrogen (NH 4 + -N: 91.3%; NO 3 - -N: 92.3%; total N: 93.6%) with a 100% selectivity to N 2 , achieving appreciable increments (NH 4 + -N: 54.5-fold and 1.3-time; NO 3 - -N: 3.4-time and 5.1-fold; total N: 8.7-fold and 1.9-time) over the abiotic controls and the open circuital conditions, respectively. The nitrogen removal processes were driven more influentially by bioanodic oxidation due to the greater variety of nanoscale MnO x deposited over the bioanodes presenting greater O v . Moreover, the harboring of higher cytochrome b and riboflavin within the bioanodic extracellular polymeric substances with more exoproteins contributed to these processes, besides the properties of specific bioanodic and biocathodic microbial communities. The calcination of the MnO x deposited bioelectrodes and their reuse, confirmed a solid framework for further system development. Overall, this study explores new cost-effective and stable processes for treating actual MTW (containing dissolved manganese, NH 4 + -N and NO 3 - -N) with simultaneous recovery/reuse of manganese, contributing to the sustainability of mineral mining and processing industries.

title: Synergistic bioremediation of metolachlor-contaminated soil by Penicillium oxalicum MetF1 and earthworms: Enhanced degradation, microbial community restructuring, and ring-opening metabolic activation
abstract: The chloroacetamide herbicide metolachlor (MET) is a widespread environmental contaminant posing risks to aquatic and soil ecosystems. Although the fungal strain Penicillium oxalicum MetF1 efficiently degrades MET in liquid culture, its performance in complex soil environments remains unexplored. Recognizing the multifunctional roles of earthworms as soil ecosystem engineers-including their capacity to modulate microbial activity and pollutant bioavailability-we incorporated Eisenia fetida into a synergistic bioremediation system with P. oxalicum MetF1 in MET-contaminated soil. The synergistic treatment achieved 93.88% MET removal within 14 days, significantly outperforming treatments with the fungus (81.75%) or earthworms (30.10%) alone. Metabolite dynamics revealed that earthworms accelerated the transformation of MET intermediates (M2H, MESA, MDES), with a unique enrichment of genes encoding key ring-opening enzymes (3-hydroxyphenylacetate 6-hydroxylase, tyrosine aminotransferase). Earthworms also decreased soil pH toward neutrality, mobilization of available phosphorus, and stabilization of organic carbon, and may partially offset microbial alkali-hydrolyzable nitrogen consumption. High-throughput sequencing demonstrated that the synergistic system alleviated pesticide-induced stress, increased microbial alpha diversity, enriched beneficial degraders (Sphingomonas, Flavobacterium, Fusarium), suppressed pathogenic Blumeria, and fostered tighter co-occurrence networks with more positive interactions. Functional prediction revealed upregulation of carbohydrate and amino acid metabolism pathways as well as the xenobiotics biodegradation pathway, with phenylacetate and tyrosine degradation pathways providing an efficient metabolic route for MET ring-opening. Earthworms exhibited low MET bioaccumulation (BAF < 1) and net weight gain, indicating limited bioaccumulation potential and the absence of obvious lethal effects. However, sublethal effects and the toxicity of MET metabolites (M2H, MESA, and MDES) require further investigation. Collectively, this study demonstrates a powerful earthworm-fungus synergistic system for MET remediation, unravels its microbial and biochemical regulatory networks governing enhanced performance, and offers a mechanistic framework for deploying multi-organism strategies in the remediation of persistently contaminated soils.

title: Mechanical properties and micromechanisms of solid waste stabilized aeolian sand improved by nano- CaCO3 and fibers
abstract: Aiming to address the dual problems of industrial solid waste storage pollution and insufficient performance of aeolian sand subgrades in cold and arid regions, this study uses industrial solid wastes (blast furnace slag and fly ash) as an alkali-activated matrix to prepare stabilized aeolian sand. On the basis of realizing the utilization of bulk solid waste, a synergistic modification system with nano-CaCO 3 (NC) and basalt fiber (BF) is constructed. Through macroscopic mechanics and freeze-thaw cycle tests, combined with DIC technology, mesoscopic simulation and microscopic analysis, the reinforcement mechanism of composite materials was explored. The results demonstrate that Nano-CaCO 3 optimizes matrix compactness through the micro-aggregate filling effect and nucleation effect, and synergizes with the three-dimensional bridging crack-resistance effect of basalt fiber to improve material performance. After hybrid modification, the compressive strength increases by 23.8%, and the splitting tensile strength increases by 28.8%. The strength loss rate can be controlled within 65% after 20 freeze-thaw cycles. DIC analysis reveals the differential characteristics that nano-modification induces strain localization while fiber modification induces strain dispersion: the shear bandwidth reaches 200-300 px, and the peak shear strain γ max is controlled between 0.08 and 0.10. Microscopic observations further elucidate the synergistic mechanisms: nanoparticles induce a transition from tensile to shear debonding, while fibers dissipate energy through pull-out and bridging actions. This multi-scale synergy achieves a significant improvement in the "strength-toughness-stability" of the composite. This study provides a theoretical basis for the utilization of solid waste resources in cold and arid areas and the freeze-thaw resistance design of aeolian sand subgrade engineering.

title: Lignosulfonate-derived sulfur functionalization of bimetallic Ni/Co-MOF for effective removal of Hg(II) from wastewater
abstract: The high toxicity and persistence of mercury (Hg(II)) severely threaten the safety of aquatic environments. In this study, a strategy based on sodium lignosulfonate (Na-LS) functionalized Ni/Co-MOF was proposed, successfully constructing a series of sulfur-doped lignin-MOF composite adsorbents (LS-Ni/Co-MOF). The introduction of Na-LS enabled efficient sulfur doping, which significantly enhanced the Hg(II) adsorption performance of the resulting composites. Batch adsorption experiments at 298 K showed that the Langmuir model calculated the maximum Hg(II) adsorption capacity of 0.5-LS-Ni/Co-MOF, 0.75-LS-Ni/Co-MOF, and 1-LS-Ni/Co-MOF to be 781.7, 799.7, and 802.1 mg g -1 , respectively, with equilibrium attained within 60 min at an initial concentration of 100 mg L -1 . Furthermore, LS-Ni/Co-MOF exhibited highly selective adsorption toward Hg(II) over various competing ions, including Ca(II), Al(III), Pb(II), Cd(II), Mg(II), Co(II), Ni(II), Zn(II), and Mn(II). The K d values for Hg(II) reached 349237.3, 450760.9 and 471704.5 L g -1 for 0.5-LS-Ni/Co-MOF, 0.75-LS-Ni/Co-MOF, and 1-LS-Ni/Co-MOF, respectively. After five consecutive adsorption-desorption cycles, the Hg(II) removal efficiency remained above 70%. Dynamic column tests showed a 50% breakthrough time of 3120 min, demonstrating great potential for practical application. In real wastewater, the materials achieved a removal efficiency of 90% for Hg(II). Finally, Spectroscopic analysis and DFT calculations revealed that the adsorption mechanism involves a coordination interaction between the surface hydroxyl and sulfonate groups and Hg(II). This work provides a promising materials design pathway for the functional utilization of lignin and the purification of heavy metal-contaminated wastewater.

title: Experimental evaluation, backpropagation neural network prediction and bibliometric analysis of bioelectricity production from agricultural wastes by microbial fuel cell
abstract: In this study, a two-stage bioprocess combining enzymatic hydrolysis and a microbial fuel cell (MFC) was established to evaluate electricity generation from three agricultural wastes (mushroom sticks, rice husks and bamboo shavings). The highest glucose concentration of 4 g/L was obtained in the mushroom sticks hydrolysate. However, rice husk hydrolysate produced the highest power density of 26.02 mW/m 2 at a current density of 29.45 mA/m 2 . The calorific value of the rice-husk hydrolysis residue (18.662 MJ/kg) was comparable to that of the original rice husks (19.424 MJ/kg), suggesting potential for further energy recovery through combustion. The backpropagation (BP) neural network model could be used to predict the MFC power density with the mean square error (MSE) of 0.0166 and the correlation coefficient (R) of 0.8917. Bibliometric analysis revealed that the volume of publications and citation frequency in the field of biomass-MFC technology exhibited distinct phased growth from 2006 to 2025, indicating that research outcomes continued to attract significant academic attention and the influence of core literature accumulated steadily. The research focus shifted from a singular emphasis on power generation to the resource-oriented and environmentally synergistic utilization centered on biomass. The results obtained from this study could contribute to renewable energy and circular economy by recycling agricultural wastes.

title: Dioxin-like contaminants (PCDD/Fs, PBDD/Fs, PXDD/Fs, PCBs, PCNs) & PBDEs in edible avian eggs other than chickens
abstract: The occurrence of dioxin-like environmental contaminants, polybrominated diphenylethers (PBDEs) and polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) was investigated in eggs of eleven avian species excluding chickens. The majority were duck and quail eggs, but smaller numbers of goose, turkey, guinea-fowl, pheasant, pea-fowl, gull, ostrich, emu and rhea eggs from retail outlets were also analysed using high-resolution sector-field mass spectrometry. Polychlorinated/brominated dibenzo-p-dioxins/dibenzofurans (PCDD/Fs, PBDD/Fs), PCBs and PBDEs were measured in 104 samples. Mixed halogenated dioxins, furans, biphenyls (PXDD/Fs & PXBs), and polychlorinated naphthalenes (PCNs) were investigated in ∼1/5th of samples. These environmental contaminants were detected in all species at lipid weight maxima of 26 pg TEQ/g, 465 ng/g NDL-PCBs and 227 ng/g PBDEs. Except for PCDD/Fs and PBDD/Fs (detected in 90% of samples), gull eggs showed highest contaminant levels. PBDD/F TEQ (max. 7.98 pg/g lipid) exceeded PCDD/F TEQ in 26% of duck eggs and elevated contaminant levels were recorded for other species. Different husbandry practices, access to soil and herbage under free-range conditions, seasonality and lower periodicity of egg laying may promote elevated contaminant levels. Dietary intakes of PCDD/F and PCB TEQ through consumption of duck eggs ranged from 0.04 to 0.44 pg TEQ/kg bw/week for adult consumers, and approximately doubled (0.08 - 0.94 pg TEQ/kg bw/week) when all measured DL-TEQ was included. Indicative intakes from eggs of other species were considerably higher, with corresponding values ranging from 0.44 to 5.3 and 0.51 to 6.2 pg TEQ/kg bw/week, respectively. Uniquely, the study provides baseline levels of emerging environmental contaminant occurrence and dietary exposure through eggs of hitherto unstudied avian species. The results emphasise the significance of non-regulated TEQ inputs. The doubling of TEQ intake through duck egg consumption when these emerging contaminants are included, suggests that the current limited focus on chlorinated congeners may provide an inadequate reflection of dietary exposure.

title: Microplastics in commercially important marine fish from Giresun Province, Türkiye: A baseline assessment of tissue distribution, polymer composition, spatial patterns, and potential environmental and ecological risk
abstract: This study investigated the occurrence, characteristics, and spatial distribution of microplastics in muscle tissues and guts of commercially important fish species with different feeding habits (Pomatomus saltatrix, Mullus barbatus, Trachurus trachurus, Engraulis encrasicolus, Mugil cephalus, Merlangius merlangus, and Sarda sarda) from Giresun coast of the Black Sea. Microplastic contamination and polymer-associated hazard characteristics were evaluated using the contamination factor (CF), pollution load index (PLI), polymer hazard index (PHI), and potential ecological risk index (PERI). Microplastics were detected in both muscle tissue and gut, with substantial variation among species and tissues.
