The highest microplastic abundance was observed in the muscle of P. saltatrix (41.3 ± 19.3 particles/g-dw) and in the gut of M. cephalus (230.7 ± 8.2 particles/g-dw). Fibers (FBs) were the predominant morphotype in both muscle tissue and gut, accounting for 92.7% and 97.1% of the detected particles, respectively. Polyethylene terephthalate predominated in muscle tissue (53.4%), whereas polypropylene predominated in the gut (68.7%). The calculated CF, PLI, PHI, and PERI values revealed marked differences in relative microplastic contamination and polymer-associated hazard among species, tissues, and sampling locations. These differences suggest that feeding behaviour, habitat use, and polymer composition may contribute to species- and tissue-specific microplastic exposure patterns. The detection of microplastics in muscle tissue, together with their variable polymer composition, highlights the ecological relevance of microplastic contamination in commercially important fish and the need for continued monitoring of microplastic occurrence and characteristics in the south-eastern Black Sea.

title: Single biochar application enhances soil methane sink and underlying microbial mechanisms in a subtropical forest after twelve years of treatments
abstract: Biochar is an effective amendment for enhancing soil carbon sequestration and regulating soil greenhouse gas emissions, such as methane (CH 4 ), yet its decadal-scale effects in forest ecosystems remain unclear. Here, based on a 12-year field experiment in a subtropical forest where biochar was applied once at rates of 0 (CK), 10 (Bio10), and 30 t ha -1 (Bio30), we monitored in-situ CH 4 fluxes over one year and simulated daily soil CH 4 fluxes using a Soil Methanotrophy Model (MeMo). Combined with laboratory incubations and metagenomic absolute quantification sequencing, we found that a single biochar application enhanced the soil CH 4 sink even after twelve years, in a dose-dependent manner. Compared with CK, Bio10 increased the annual cumulative CH 4 uptake by 24.9% (P 4 uptake flux showed no statistically significant increase (10.3%). In contrast, Bio30 significantly increased both the mean annual flux and annual cumulative uptake by 56.0% and 76.4%, respectively. Biochar addition significantly increased soil extractable organic carbon (EOC) contents, but significantly decreased ammonium nitrogen (NH 4 + -N) content (P 4 uptake (total effect = 0.60). In summary, a single application of 30 t ha -1 biochar still exerts a significant enhancement of the soil CH 4 sink in subtropical forest soils twelve years after application. These findings provide critical scientific evidence for evaluating the long-term climate mitigation benefits of biochar in forest ecosystems and offer theoretical support for nature-based strategies to enhance forest soil CH 4 sinks.

title: Multi-city study of the joint effects of ozone and temperature exposure on violent crime during warm months in the United States
abstract: High temperatures have been associated with increased violent crime, but evidence regarding whether air pollution modifies this relationship remains limited. We conducted a multi-city time-series analysis to examine joint impacts of acute temperature and ozone (O 3 ) exposure on violent crime during warm months (May-October) in 62 cities from 2005 to 2023 across the continental US. Daily violent crime counts were derived from the National Incident-Based Reporting System. City-specific two-day moving average temperature and O 3 were used as exposures. We conducted single-exposure quasi-Poisson regression models to estimate city-specific relative risk (RR) of violent crime comparing the risk at the 90th and 10th percentile exposures of temperature and O 3 , separately. Then, we conducted joint-exposure quasi-Poisson models using a smooth non-linear interaction term. Effect modification by O 3 on temperature-related risk was assessed by comparing risk at the 90th versus 10th percentile temperatures under low (5th), medium (50th), and high (95th percentile) O 3 concentrations, using city-specific temperature and O 3 values. Meta-regression analyses were used to combine city-specific risk estimates. The estimated city-specific RRs ranged from 0.73 to 2.31 across study cities. Across the cities, the risk of violent crime at the 90th versus 10th percentile of temperature and O 3 exposure was 1.09-fold and 1.05-fold higher, respectively. The pooled RRs of violent crime comparing the 90th and 10th temperature percentiles were 1.08 (95% CI: 1.05-1.10), 1.04 (1.02-1.07), and 1.00 (0.98-1.03) at the 5th, 50th, and 95th percentile O 3 concentrations, respectively. Overall, we found more pronounced temperature-related risks of violent crime at low O 3 concentrations and attenuated risks at high O 3 concentrations. These findings highlight the importance of considering the complex joint effects of temperature and O 3 in public health strategies for violent behaviors.

title: Projected burden of cold spell-attributable Parkinson's disease mortality among older adults in China under climate change and population ageing
abstract: Population ageing may amplify cold-related health risks under climate change, particularly for older adults with Parkinson's disease (PD). We developed a climate-ageing projection framework to estimate the burden of cold spell-attributable PD mortality in China by integrating national mortality data, climate projections, and demographic forecasts. We analyzed 59,384 PD deaths among adults aged 60 years and older in China mainland during 2013-2020 using a time-stratified case-crossover design. Cold spells were associated with an increase in mortality, with effects concentrated within lags 0-4; the cumulative odds ratio was 1.109 (95% CI: 1.036, 1.187), with an attributable fraction (AF) of 9.83% (95% CI: 3.48%, 15.75%). AF point estimates were descriptively higher in southern than in northern China. Across the six administrative regions, AF point estimates ranged from -8.81% in Northwest China to 25.87% in Northeast China, with no statistical evidence of cross-region heterogeneity. Projections showed that cold spell-attributable PD mortality remained substantial across all scenarios in the 2030s, despite climate warming. Thereafter, trajectories diverged. Under SSP1-RCP2.6, projected nationwide attributable deaths were 744 (95% CI: -391, 1659) in the 2030s, 988 (95% CI: -608, 2277) in the 2050s, and 867 (95% CI: -589, 2042) in the 2080s, with East and Southwest China contributing the largest shares and being the only regional estimates whose 95% CIs excluded zero. Under SSP2-RCP4.5, the nationwide burden rose modestly in the 2050s and then declined by the 2080s, whereas under SSP5-RCP8.5 it declined more steeply over time. These scenario-specific patterns occurred alongside substantial differences in projected cold spell occurrence, highlighting that future cold-related PD mortality cannot be inferred from mean warming alone. Under the modeled scenarios, climate warming did not necessarily translate into uniformly lower cold-related PD mortality in an ageing society. This persistence may warrant continued attention to cold-related risks in near-term climate-health adaptation for ageing populations.

title: Facile surface hydrophobic modification of rice husk for efficient crude oil emulsion separation
abstract: Commercial demulsifiers are mainly polyethers derived from ethylene oxide and propylene oxide, with hazardous and complex production routes. Rice husk (RH), a renewable agricultural by-product with abundant cellulose, lignin and surface oxygen-containing groups, is a promising hydrophilic substrate for biomass demulsifiers. However, the reported RH-based demulsifiers generally need harsh synthesis conditions, and investigations into their interfacial mechanisms are still superficial. In this work, an RH-based demulsifier (RHPB) was prepared via a relatively mild one-step surface hydrophobic modification of RH with 1-bromooctadecane (C18Br). Its structure and surface morphology were characterized by FT-IR, XRD, 13 C NMR, SEM, and N 2 adsorption-desorption analysis. Bottle test results revealed that RHPB attained a demulsification efficiency (DE) of 89.7% within 40 min and 95.2% after 180 min at a dosage of 600 mg/L. In addition, RHPB exhibited good salt and pH tolerance, achieving 99.7% of DE, particularly under strongly alkaline conditions. Combined with density functional theory (DFT) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, the critical role of RHPB in regulating intermolecular non-covalent forces (dominated by hydrogen bonding) at the interface was revealed. RHPB forms HBs with water molecules through its oxygen-containing functional groups, competitively displacing water molecules originally bound to asphaltenes. Meanwhile, the hydrophobic long chains create steric hindrance effects that assist interfacial reconstruction, thereby effectively weakening the strength of the asphaltene-constructed oil-water interface (OWI) film. Owing to the low cost, naturally abundant feedstock, RHPB represents a sustainable alternative to traditional polyether demulsifiers for W/O emulsion remediation. This study provides a valuable strategy for designing demulsifiers by tuning the amphiphilicity of modified rice husk.

title: Feasibility of self-sustaining smoldering for the preparation of constructed technosols from acidic mine tailings
abstract: Self-sustaining smoldering has been widely investigated for treating organic solid waste, whereas its potential to transform acidic mine tailings into constructed Technosols (CTs) for rehabilitation remains unclear. Here, self-sustaining smoldering was evaluated as a method for preparing CTs from acidic mine tailings, with a focus on smoldering behavior, acid-generation potential, arsenic (As) risk, physicochemical properties, dissolved organic matter (DOM) characteristics, revegetation potential, and mineralogical transformation. At tailings/wheat straw ratios of 3:1-6:1 and airflow rates of 0.2-0.9 m 3 /h, smoldering was self-sustaining, increasing the net neutralization ratio from 1.65 to values in the range 3.06-6.32 and indicating a transition to nonacid-generating behavior. Smoldering increased pH and nutrient availability, with the contents of organic matter and available nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium increased by 2.02-3.97, 1.29-3.56, 1.87-45.08, and 50.62-85.69 times their respective initial levels. Smoldering also promoted DOM humification; increased condensed aromatic and tannin-like compounds; depleted sulfur-containing DOM; induced pyrite depletion, goethite-to-hematite transformation, and kaolinite dehydroxylation; and increased surface roughness. Although total As concentrations decreased from 64.50 to 52.87-64.14 mg/kg and the optimal treatment met the relevant landscaping-soil limit, smoldering increased As bioavailability and leachability in several treatments, necessitating subsequent risk management. However, plant tests of the resulting loamy-sand CTs confirmed improved revegetation potential, with greater ryegrass germination, shoot growth, and dry biomass compared with untreated tailings, particularly under tailings/wheat straw ratios of 3:1. This study advances the application of smoldering and provides a low-cost and energy-efficient method for preparing CTs for widespread acidic mine-tailings rehabilitation.

title: Humin-accelerated microbial dechlorination of polychlorinated biphenyls in Taihu Lake sediment microcosms: Insights into congener and microbe shifts and the role of subsequently supplemented sulfidated nanoscale zero-valent iron
abstract: Microbial dechlorination is a promising route for the in situ detoxification of PCB-contaminated sediments, yet this is often limited by slow electron transfer and the progressive depletion of electron donors. Humin acts as a naturally occurring solid-phase redox mediator, whereas sulfidated nanoscale zero-valent iron (S-nZVI) can provide extra electrons. Both of them hold the potential to enhance PCB dechlorination. Herein, this study investigated the long-term (66 weeks) effect of humin (20 g ·kg -1 slurry basis) on dechlorinating the most toxic commercial PCB mixture Aroclor 1254 in Taihu Lake sediment microcosms. Moreover, the triggering potential of supplemented S-nZVI (0.1% slurry basis) was examined after Week 30, when initial dechlorination slowed down. The results showed that humin significantly accelerated PCB dechlorination during the rapid phase (Weeks 12-30), without altering the predominant meta- and para-dechlorination preferences. Total PCB mass decreased by approximately 32% while toxic equivalents declined by >99% by Week 66. Congener-specific analysis inferred three predominant humin-enhanced meta-dechlorination pathways of PCB110 (236-34) → PCB71 (26-34) → PCB32 (26-4), PCB99 (245-24) → PCB47 (24-24), and PCB92 (235-25) → PCB52 (25-25). Microbial analyses by multiple molecular biology tools suggest that humin was associated with closer co-occurrence between putative dechlorinating and supporting anaerobic populations. Dehalococcoides abundance increased from ∼10 7 to ∼10 8 copies·mL -1 , accompanied by pronounced increases in the reductive dehalogenase (RDase) genes pcbA4 and pcbA5, which reached 1.00 × 10 8 ± 1.47 × 10 6 and 4.81 × 10 8 ± 2.04 × 10 7 copies·mL -1 , respectively. Supplementation with S-nZVI at Week 30 triggered further dechlorination and total PCB mass decreased by 44% at the end of Week 66. S-nZVI drove apparent increases in the abundances of Dehalococcoides, Dehalogenimonas, as well as iron- and sulfate-reducing populations. Predicted functional changes further displayed a wide community response accompanying sustained PCB dechlorination. Combining humin-enhanced rapid-phase dechlorination with S-nZVI-supported further dechlorination after dechlorination slows may provide a viable strategy for sustaining long-term PCB bioremediation.

title: Behavior and toxicity of Buckminsterfullerene (C60) in aquatic environments: A 30-year review
abstract: Buckminsterfullerene (C 60 ) is widely applied in various fields due to its unique physicochemical properties and has been increasingly detected in aquatic environments. This review examines the current knowledge of C 60 behavior and toxicity in aquatic environments over the past 30 years. Once released into aquatic systems, C 60 undergoes complex processes, including dispersion, aggregation, sedimentation, transformation, and interactions with co-pollutants. These processes influence its mobility, bioavailability, and toxicity, affecting organisms from algae to benthos. Mechanisms for these toxicities involve solvent-related effects, reactive oxygen species generation, physical contact, and carrier effects with co-pollutants. Furthermore, current evidence suggests that the ecological risks of C 60 are likely underestimated, particularly in sediment-associated, food-web, and multi-pollutant exposure scenarios. This review also identifies critical knowledge gaps, including the fate of sediment-associated C 60 , the limited diversity of test organisms, the lack of environmental realism in exposure conditions, and challenges in maintaining C 60 purity during preparation.

title: Enantiomer-specific effects of metconazole disrupt soil microbiota, gut homeostasis, and genomic responses of Eisenia fetida
abstract: The selective use of highly active, low-risk enantiomers in place of racemic fungicides represents a sustainable approach to balancing agricultural productivity with environmental safety. Little is known about the enantioselective toxicity and environmental disturbances of the chiral triazole fungicide metconazole (MEZ) on the soil ecosystem. This study revealed that rac-MEZ dissipated faster than cis-MEZs in soil, but rac-MEZ induced a greater decrease in bacterial diversity and network complexity. The longer persistence of cis-MEZs possibly led to greater bioaccumulation in earthworms (Eisenia fetida). Enantioselectivity was observed for two cis-MEZs; cis-1R,5S-MEZ exhibited more severe acute toxicity in earthworms than cis-1S,5R-MEZ. This may be attributed to the potential detoxifying protein (CYP4V), which binds weakly with cis-1R, 5S-MEZ. This weaker detoxification capacity potentially resulted in oxidative stress response system collapse in earthworms, leading to excess reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and disturbance of antioxidant and detoxification enzymes (such as CAT, SOD, and GST). The ROS dysregulation caused by cis-1R, 5S-MEZ induced severe ecotoxicity, including DNA damage, heme metabolism disruption, and downregulation of transcriptional ovo-spermathecal apparatus development and genomic diversification, possibly resulting in higher cytotoxicity, genotoxicity, and reproductive toxicity. Therefore, cis-1R,5S-MEZ is more toxic to earthworms and their ecological functions, suggesting a less favorable environmental risk profile for potential agricultural use.

title: Waste sludge-derived humic acid alters metallic nanoparticle-bacteria interactions during denitrification via amide-mediated transformation and metabolic regulation
abstract: Silver nanoparticles (Ag NPs) are increasingly recognized to disrupt bacterial denitrification, a process responsible for over 70% of global nitrogen removal, yet cost-effective and sustainable mitigation strategies remain largely limited. This work systematically reveals the interactions between waste sludge-derived humic acid (WSHA) and Ag NPs, providing WSHA as a scalable alternative that achieves near-complete denitrification recovery (98.4% vs. 70.6% for natural analogs) through amide-mediated silver transformation and metabolic regulation. Structural characterization reveals WSHA's distinctive lower α-helix/(β-sheet + random coil) ratio (0.31 vs. 0.83 for natural analogs) exposes abundant amide groups that exhibit superior Ag NPs binding affinity (-6.53 eV vs. -5.41 eV for carboxyl groups). Notably, nitrogen atoms in amide groups serve as primary electron-donating centers (carrying -0.70 e), driving preferential Ag surfaces binding that promotes Ag NPs aggregation (from 10 to 50.8 nm) and surface oxidation to low-toxicity Ag 2 O and Ag 2 S species, thereby reducing bioavailable Ag + release by 80%. Furthermore, transcriptomic analysis reveals a dual-protection mechanism beyond physicochemical transformation. WSHA simultaneously upregulates key denitrification enzymes (e.g., nitrate and nitrite reductases) and central carbon metabolism pathways (e.g., glycolysis and TCA cycle), while activating comprehensive stress-response systems (e.g., DNA replication, SOS response, and oxidative stress defense). This integrated physicochemical-biological protection establishes waste-derived humic substances as scalable, economically viable solutions for mitigating metallic nanoparticle contamination in both engineered and natural microbial ecosystems.

title: Moisture-induced pore restriction reveals a lower initial moisture window for aerobic composting of aquaculture-derived particulates
abstract: Aerobic composting offers a sustainable route for recycling aquaculture-derived particulates, but appropriate moisture conditions for these fine and adhesive materials remain unclear because conventional criteria are mainly derived from terrestrial wastes. Aquaculture-derived particulates were composted for 28 d at initial moisture contents of 40%, 45%, and 50%. The 40% treatment maintained the highest porosity and more favorable oxygen conditions, entered the thermophilic phase (>50 °C) on day 8, and remained thermophilic for 13 d. In contrast, the 45% treatment sustained thermophilic conditions for only 6 d, whereas the 50% treatment never exceeded 50 °C and reached a minimum O 2 concentration of 5.3%. The 40% treatment achieved a 52.47% decrease in C/N ratio, a final germination index of 81.7 ± 6.3%, and an HA/FA ratio of 1.87 ± 0.06, indicating enhanced organic matter stabilization and humification. Higher moisture caused persistent oxygen limitation, prolonged NH 4 + -N accumulation, ammonia loss, and increased greenhouse gas emissions. Microbial and metagenomic analysis were consistent with faster succession toward thermotolerant and aerobic degraders under 40% moisture, whereas higher moisture favored oxygen-limited metabolic potentials. Aquaculture-derived particulates also contained higher mucin-equivalent levels than that in terrestrial substrates examined, suggesting that mucin may increase moisture-dependent adhesion and pore restriction. These findings demonstrate that aquaculture particulate-based composting requires a lower initial moisture level than commonly applied to terrestrial substrates, highlighting the importance of balancing water availability and pore aeration to improve compost stability and mitigate greenhouse gas emissions.

title: Interfacial electron transfer and surface dual-sites on Fe-Mn bimetallic catalyst for synergistic peroxymonosulfate activation and reactive oxygen species generation
abstract: The remediation of persistent chlorophenolic contaminants in aquatic environments remains a formidable challenge, necessitating the development of highly efficient and sustainable advanced oxidation technologies. Peroxymonosulfate-based advanced oxidation processes (PMS-AOPs) have been recognized as a significant approach, yet their catalytic performance is often limited by insufficient active sites, sluggish electron transfer kinetics, and poor catalyst stability. To overcome these limitations, a novel biochar-supported Fe-Mn bimetallic catalyst (Fe-Mn@BC) was rationally designed and synthesized as an efficient peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activator for the removal of 2,4,6-trichlorophenol (TCP). Under optimal parameters, the Fe-Mn@BC/PMS system realized complete TCP degradation within 150 min. Mechanism studies revealed that reactive oxygen species (ROSs), including SO 4 ·- , O·H, O 2 - ·, and O 2 1, were the dominant active species responsible for TCP degradation. Characterization results and electrochemical analysis demonstrated that the synergistic Fe(II)/Fe(III) and Mn(II)/Mn(III)/Mn(IV) redox cycles not only facilitated electron transfer but also promoted O-O bond cleavage within the PMS molecule, thereby sustaining continuous ROSs generation. Furthermore, surface functional groups (e.g., C=O) on the catalyst contributed to ROSs formation via a non-radical pathway, further enhancing the oxidative capacity. This work provided a robust bimetallic catalyst system with enhanced PMS activation capability, offering an sustainable and effective solution for the treatment of chlorophenolic contaminants.

title: Association of occupational noise exposure with hypertension and the mediating role of metabolic dysregulation: A combined cross-sectional and longitudinal study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Evidence linking occupational noise to hypertension remains inconsistent, and potential metabolic pathways are insufficiently characterised. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 70,759 workers in Jiangsu Province and a retrospective five-year cohort analysis of 2188 workers. We combined multivariable regression, machine-learning prediction, mediation analysis, and longitudinal modelling to examine associations and potential pathways. RESULTS: Hypertension prevalence was 28.19%. Compared with unexposed workers, noise exposure of 70-< 85 dB(A) and 85-< 90 dB(A) was associated with higher hypertension odds (OR = 1.16 and 1.21, p < 0.001), whereas the association at ≥ 90 dB(A) was not significant after adjustment. XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance (AUC = 0.84), with metabolic indicators including triglycerides, glucose, and γ-glutamyl transferase ranking among the important predictors, while noise exposure also contributed to prediction. Mediation analyses identified potential indirect pathways involving γ-glutamyl transferase, glucose, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the association between occupational noise exposure and systolic blood pressure. Longitudinal analyses showed delayed divergence in metabolic markers and larger systolic blood pressure differences during the later follow-up period. CONCLUSIONS: Occupational noise exposure was associated with elevated blood pressure even at levels below the Chinese occupational noise exposure limit of 85 dB(A) for an 8-h working day, which is primarily intended to prevent noise-induced hearing loss. The findings are consistent with a potential role of oxidative stress-related glucose and lipid metabolic dysregulation in this association. Future occupational health strategies should incorporate longitudinal metabolic surveillance to mitigate noise-induced risks in exposed populations.

title: Adsorption behavior of nanoplastics from water onto magnetic biochar in single and binary heavy metal systems: A combined experimental and DFT study
abstract: Coexisting metals can alter the removal of nanoplastics by magnetic biochar, but comparisons between single- and mixed-metal treatments depend on the concentrations used. We evaluated the apparent uptake of dispersed polystyrene (PS) nanoplastics by magnetic biochar (MBC) under metal-free, Pb(II), Zn(II), and binary Pb(II)/Zn(II) conditions. Each metal was added at 50 mg L -1 in the corresponding treatment. At an initial PS concentration of 100 mg L -1 , the apparent uptake capacities were 24.25, 19.40, 14.48, and 21.14 mg g -1 , respectively. The binary value was numerically higher than either single-metal value but remained below the metal-free control. Because the binary treatment contained twice the total metal concentration of each single-metal treatment, the observed binary response reflects the combined influence of metal composition and total loading. Control measurements showed metal-associated changes in PS aggregation, while SEM-EDS and XPS analyses detected Pb and Zn on recovered MBC and indicated changes in the surface chemical environment. Selected finite-cluster calculations further illustrated configuration-dependent local metal arrangements and electronic redistribution at the modeled PS-MBC interface. Together, these results establish a treatment-dependent adsorption response under defined batch conditions and indicate that metal identity, total loading, and local interfacial configuration jointly influence dispersed PS removal.

title: Effects of calcium-based amendments on carbon and nitrogen emissions from soil and composting systems: a meta-analysis
abstract: Nitrogen (N) and carbon (C) losses from cropping and livestock systems contribute significantly to global warming and other ecological crises. Calcium-based materials, such as lime, gypsum, phosphogypsum (PG), and single superphosphate (SSP), are widely used in agriculture because of their affordability and multifunctional benefits; however, their overall efficacy in mitigating C and N losses across soil and compost systems remains insufficiently quantified. Therefore, this study conducted a comprehensive meta-analysis of 279 published studies (200 on soil and 79 on compost) to evaluate the effects of Calcium-based amendments on C and N emissions. The results showed that liming significantly reduced N 2 O emissions by 27.9% in soil and 36.5% in composting systems. However, liming significantly increased soil NH 3 emissions by 68.4% and CO 2 emissions by 26%. Gypsum, SSP, and PG reduced NH 3 emissions by 15.0%, 49.6%, and 64.6% in soil, and by 39.5%, 39.9%, and 54.8%, respectively, in compost. Gypsum and PG reduced CH 4 emissions by 52.7% and 29.2% in soil, and by 23.2% and 71.8%, respectively, in compost. PG reduced soil N 2 O and CO 2 emissions by 17.9% and 20.5%, respectively, but increased N 2 O emissions from compost by 101.9%. SSP increased soil CO 2 emissions by 5.4%, whereas it reduced N 2 O, CO 2 , and CH 4 emissions from compost by 25.2%, 14.1%, and 36.9%, respectively. Soil N 2 O emissions decreased with increasing liming rates, whereas C emissions showed the opposite trend. Increasing the N application rate stimulated both N 2 O and NH 3 emissions. In composting systems, the effects of SSP were governed by the application rate, C/N ratio, and initial pH. This study provides a comprehensive assessment of the effects of Calcium-based amendments and identifies key factors influencing their efficacy and differences in their effects across soil and compost systems. These findings provide a scientific basis for developing targeted strategies to mitigate greenhouse gas and NH 3 emissions while delivering co-benefits for agriculture and the environment.

title: Traffic-related air pollution links with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder in Denmark: Developmental periods of susceptibility and sex-specificity
abstract: Literature supports that higher early life exposure to air pollution arising from combustion, e.g., traffic exhaust and electric power generation, is associated with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). However, little is known about whether certain periods of exposure during fetal or childhood brain development are more important, i.e. whether there are critical windows of exposure, or whether associations differ by child sex. To address these gaps, we performed a population-based case-cohort study including singletons born 1981-2008 using Danish national registry data resources. We included 21,860 persons diagnosed with ADHD (ICD10 F90.0) and 32,041 persons randomly selected from the eligible population. Daily fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) and elemental carbon (EC) exposure corresponded to complete residential addresses from pre-conception through the 12th year of life, using the multi-level Danish air model, DEHM/UBM/AirGIS, at the address level. We estimated hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals for pollutants and ADHD, adjusting for urbanicity, Danish region, birth year, sex assigned at birth, socio-demographic factors, and polygenic scores for ADHD. To account for correlation structure of pollutants across time, we adjusted pollutant exposure in one time period for other periods, finding that HRs in the second-year of life were larger than during pregnancy or other postnatal years: EC > 1.13 vs. EC 3 HR: 1.24 (1.12, 1.36); these associations were not attenuated after adjusting for PM 2.5 . For females, the EC HR in the 2 nd year of life: 1.44 (1.21, 1.72) was larger than for males: 1.18 (1.00, 1.40) (modification test p = 0.000), suggesting increased vulnerability in females. Critical period and sex modification results were similar for PM 2.5 . These results add to growing literature that major air pollutants increase ADHD risk and add important new insights that early childhood may be an important period of exposure and links may be stronger in females.

title: Molecular-weight-dependent responses of DOM to hydrological seasonality and nutrient ratios
abstract: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) plays a central role in aquatic biogeochemical processes, yet seasonal differences in its carbon concentration, fluorescence composition, and environmental associations among operational size fractions remain insufficiently characterized. Here, water samples collected during dry and wet seasons were fractionated into three cumulative filtrates (<0.45 μm, <10 kDa, and <1 kDa). DOC measurements, UV-vis spectroscopy, excitation-emission matrix fluorescence coupled with parallel factor analysis (PARAFAC), and multivariate analyses were combined to characterize seasonal variation and component-specific environmental associations. DOC concentrations were higher in the wet season in the <0.45 μm and <10 kDa permeates but similar between seasons in the <1 kDa permeate. In the smallest filtrate, similar DOC concentrations contrasted with differences in fluorescence composition: the dry-season PARAFAC model was dominated by tryptophan-like fluorescence, whereas the wet-season model was dominated by humic-like fluorescence. PARAFAC models fitted to pooled seasonal data resolved four, three, and two components in the <0.45 μm, <10 kDa, and <1 kDa permeates, respectively, with both protein-like and humic-like fluorescence were identified in the model for each fraction. Environmental associations differed among filtrates and within broad fluorescence classes. Notably, two <10 kDa protein-like components shared an emission maximum at 340 nm but exhibited opposing associations with the physicochemical and nutrient constructs in partial least squares path modeling. Overall, operational fractionation revealed filtrate-specific seasonal DOC patterns not captured by bulk measurements alone, while component-resolved fluorescence analysis exposed environmental associations obscured by broad fluorescence classifications. These findings highlight the complementary roles of DOC concentration measurements and fluorescence characterization in interpreting aquatic DOM dynamics.

title: Impact of extreme rainstorm-induced flooding on emergency healthcare demands in a mountainous district: a multi-group interrupted time-series analysis
abstract: Floods have severe impacts on human health and emergency healthcare systems; however, research on their short-term acute health effects remains insufficient, particularly in vulnerable mountainous regions. The severe floods that occurred in Beijing from July 29 to August 2, 2023, had a substantial significant impact on remote mountainous districts. Utilizing daily emergency department (ED) visit data from a hospital in these remote areas, this study employed a difference-in-differences interrupted time series design to compare the 2023 disaster period with the corresponding periods in 2024 and 2025. We assessed temporal trends in all-cause ED visits, as well as cause-specific visits for cardiovascular disease (CVD), respiratory diseases, and physical trauma, across the acute blockade, and short-term recovery phases. During the acute blockade phase, all-cause ED visits (relative risk [RR] = 0.74, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.58-0.96) and CVD visits (RR = 0.50, 95% CI: 0.28-0.91) exhibited significant immediate declines. This reduction may reflect decreased healthcare accessibility resulting from physical isolation caused by extreme rainfall and road disruptions. Moreover, the daily slope of CVD visits showed an increasing trend (RR = 1.26, 95% CI: 1.04-1.54). Upon entering the short-term recovery phase, there was an immediate compensatory surge in all-cause ED visits (RR = 1.28, 95% CI: 1.13-1.44), particularly in visits for physical trauma (RR = 2.23, 95% CI: 1.82-2.75). This rebound was primarily driven by males and adults aged 18-64 years. These findings suggest that acute physical blockades in mountainous regions may temporarily suppress healthcare utilization by limiting access to emergency services, followed by a substantial delayed compensatory surge in ED visits, predominantly for physical trauma. Accordingly, primary healthcare capacity for the management of physical trauma and CVD should be strengthened at the grassroots level to enhance the resilience of emergency medical systems.

title: Microbial community shifts accompany divergent soil carbon recovery after aquaculture-pond restoration across China's coastal wetlands
abstract: Aquaculture-pond restoration may rebuild coastal soil carbon, but gains in soil organic carbon (SOC) do not necessarily indicate lower lability or uniform microbial responses. We compared aquaculture ponds and adjacent restored wetlands at 10 sites across temperate, subtropical, and tropical China. SOC, microbial biomass carbon (MBC), dissolved organic carbon (DOC), and easily oxidizable carbon (EOC) were measured at 0-15 and 15-30 cm in 160 samples, and carbon pool management index (CPMI) components were calculated. Surface-soil bacterial communities and FAPROTAX-inferred functions were characterized at three sites. Restoration increased SOC at most sites and surface MBC at five, but carbon-pool responses differed among regions. Operationally non-labile carbon (C SS = SOC - EOC), an operational estimate of less-labile carbon rather than a directly measured persistent carbon pool, increased at Yancheng, Minjiang River Estuary, Zhanjiang, and Dongzhai Port. Caofeidian, Hangzhou Bay, Zhangjiang River Estuary, and Beilun River Estuary had high carbon pool activity indices, producing CPMI values of 239.78-363.74% and indicating labile-carbon enrichment rather than uniform stabilization. Bacterial community structure was dominated by geographic separation: pond and restored samples remained close within sites, whereas alpha diversity decreased at Caofeidian, changed little at Minjiang River Estuary, and increased at Dongzhai Port. Restoration also altered dominant genera and inferred functions, including greater representation of plant-polymer degradation functions in some restored soils. DOC accounted for 46.25% of the fitted variation in the 10 dominant genera and was positively associated with Sulfurimonas, SOC, and C SS . Pond-to-wetland restoration therefore followed multiple carbon-recovery trajectories, ranging from labile-carbon pulses to accumulation of a less labile fraction. Assessments should integrate SOC quantity, carbon lability, and microbial associations.

title: Retraction notice to “Application of lipid and polymeric-based nanoparticles for treatment of inner ear infections via XGBoost” [Environ. Res. 239 (2023) 117115]
Corrigendum to “Ambient ozone exposure and depressive symptoms in adolescents: Results of the GINIplus and LISA birth cohorts” [Environ. Res. 170 (2019) 73-81]
Retraction notice to “Zinc oxide nanoflakes supported copper oxide nanosheets as a bifunctional electrocatalyst for OER and HER in an alkaline medium” [Environ. Res. 252 (2024) 119030]
Reconciling competing objectives in carbonated MSWI fly ash washing: Dechlorination, calcium retention, and heavy metal stabilization
abstract: The resource utilization of MSW incineration fly ash is constrained by its high chloride content, calcium loss during washing, and the environmental risk of residual heavy metals. This study proposes a multistage pretreatment integrating carbonation, ball milling, ultrasonication, and CO 2 -coupled washing to balance dechlorination, calcium retention, and heavy metal stabilization. Citric acid (CA), ammonium bisulfate (AB), and ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) were selected as washing agents and evaluated on carbonated fly ash. For the investigated fly ash, results demonstrated that carbonation provided the foundational calcium fixation, while ball milling physically disrupted particle agglomerates to expose encapsulated chlorides, with 60 min selected as the milling duration. Ultrasonication for 10 min further reduced soluble chloride contents in heavily carbonated fly ash residues to 0.72%, 0.79%, and 0.81%, respectively, with calcium loss rates of 14.30%, 10.81%, and 12.08%. However, EDTA washing caused severe remobilization of Pb, Zn, Cu, and Cd. Further coupling ball milling and ultrasonication with in-situ CO 2 sparging (20 min for CA and 10 min for AB) improved the overall treatment performance. The lowest soluble chloride content (0.71%) was obtained with CA, whereas AB achieved the lowest calcium loss (8.87%). All heavy metal leaching concentrations in CA and AB residues met the regulatory limits. Risk assessment code analysis indicated that AB generally resulted in lower environmental risks than CA, although Cd remained the primary residual concern. Overall, the coupled treatment alleviated the trade-offs among chloride removal, calcium retention, and heavy metal stabilization, thereby improving the resource recovery potential of treated fly ash.

title: Root-applied taurine reduces grain cadmium and improves rice yield by decreasing Cd transport and increasing Cd retention in roots
abstract: Taurine (TAU) can improve plant stress tolerance, but its effect on cadmium (Cd) accumulation in rice remains poorly understood. Here, we compared seed soaking, root application, and foliar spraying of TAU using hydroponic and full-season pot experiments with rice (Oryza sativa L. cv. Kitaake). The results showed that root application of TAU was the optimal approach, which can significantly promote rice growth and reduce Cd accumulation. In the hydroponic experiment, 10 mg L -1 TAU increased shoot and root dry weights by 37.3% and 63.3%, respectively, and decreased shoot Cd concentration by 29.0%. In the pot experiment, root-applied TAU decreased brown-rice Cd concentration by 23.3% and increased grain yield by 14.7%. Root application of TAU reduced expression of OsNRAMP1, OsNRAMP5, OsIRT1, and OsIRT2 genes associated with Cd uptake and the OsHMA2 gene in charge of xylem loading by 29.7%, 11.4%, 48.8%, 11.1%, and 22.0%, respectively, whereas increased expression of the OsHMA3 gene involved in Cd vacuolar sequestration by 27.5%. Integrated transcriptomic, metabolomic, and physiological analyses showed that TAU activated the jasmonic acid signaling and phenylpropanoid pathway and promoted root cell-wall lignification, thereby increasing Cd retention in the cell wall by 20.2%. These results suggest that root-applied TAU decreases Cd accumulation in rice grain through coordinated changes in Cd uptake, translocation, and root retention while increasing grain production, offering a potential strategy for the safe utilization of Cd-contaminated paddy fields.

title: Tissue-specific uptake, depuration kinetics, and metabolite formation of decabromodiphenyl ether (BDE-209) in Chinese mitten crab (Eriocheir sinensis)
abstract: Extremely high levels of decabromodiphenyl ether (BDE-209) are frequently detected in Chinese mitten crabs (Eriocheir sinensis), which raises dietary concerns for humans. However, the tissue-specific toxicokinetics of BDE-209 in crabs have rarely been reported. In this study, the short-term tissue-specific uptake, depuration, and debromination of BDE-209 were investigated in Chinese mitten crabs during a 28-day dietary exposure period followed by a 28-day depuration period. Hemolymph and viscera were the major accumulation compartments, together accounting for over 84.7% of the combined BDE-209 burden in the four examined tissues. The uptake rate constants followed the order: hemolymph > viscera > gill > muscle, while elimination half-lives showed the reverse order (hemolymph: 3.93 d < viscera: 8.48 d < muscle: 11.22 d < gill: 11.86 d). Males generally exhibited higher BDE-209 uptake rates and higher whole-body concentrations than females. However, sex-related differences in depuration were tissue- and dose-dependent, with significant differences mainly observed at the low dose. Tissue-distribution patterns and metabolite profiles were broadly similar between sexes. Three possible lower-brominated products (BDE-207, BDE-206, and BDE-197) were detected in both viscera and hemolymph, consistent with stepwise reductive debromination of BDE-209. Their metabolite-to-parent concentration ratios were low (<1.03%), indicating limited formation of the detected debromination products under the present experimental conditions. A significant positive correlation was observed between the concentrations of BDE-209 and its metabolites in hemolymph and viscera. These findings provide useful information for BDE-209 risk assessment and may contribute to the establishment of limit standards in crab, while also giving recommendations to ensure the chemical safety of crab products.

title: Interfacial assembly of PBAs/ZIF-8 composites for ultrahigh-capacity and selective thallium capture with exceptional alkaline tolerance
abstract: Effective Tl + elimination under extreme alkaline pH remains challenging, as alkali triggers decomposition of Prussian blue analogs (PBAs), lowering adsorption efficiency and generating secondary pollutants. Furthermore, conventional PBAs nanocrystals ( + adsorption capacity of 629.03 mg/g and a removal efficiency of 97.78%, significantly surpassing most reported adsorbents, with over 90% removal within 10 min. The micron-sized particles enable convenient separation by simple filtration, while the ZIF-8 shell confers stable Tl + removal across pH 2-12, a tolerance unattainable by bare PBAs, through a complementary protection mechanism. In actual industrial leachate and in the presence of competing ions, the material reduces residual Tl + to below 5 μg/L with a distribution coefficient K d > 10 4 mL/g. Mechanistic studies confirm a near-equimolar K + /Tl + ion-exchange pathway. This work offers a promising stabilization strategy for structurally vulnerable adsorbents and a viable candidate for deep Tl + removal from hazardous wastewater.

title: Feedstock-dependent biochar properties shape short-term soil CO2 emissions through microbial enzyme-associated processes beyond the effect of soil pH in black soil
abstract: Black soils represent globally important reservoirs of soil organic carbon (SOC), yet the mechanisms regulating short-term carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions following biochar amendment remain poorly understood. Although biochar-induced alkalization has been widely proposed as a key mechanism influencing soil carbon mineralization, whether increased soil pH alone can explain feedstock-dependent CO 2 responses remain unresolved. Here, we investigated the effects of biochars derived from six feedstocks on CO 2 emissions, soil chemical properties, microbial functional traits, and extracellular enzyme activities in a short-term incubation experiment using black soil. Biochar application increased cumulative CO 2 emissions by 9.1%-44.6%, with substantial variation among feedstocks. Biochars increased soil pH, nutrient availability, and the activities of carbon-, nitrogen-, and phosphorus-acquiring enzymes, but the magnitude of these responses varied substantially with feedstock-dependent biochar properties. Cumulative CO 2 emissions were positively associated with β-glucosidase (BG), leucine aminopeptidase (LAP), and acid phosphatase (ACP) activities. Random forest and regression analyses identified soil pH and extracellular enzyme activities as major predictors of CO 2 emissions, with extracellular enzyme activities collectively contributing 52.9% of the relative importance and exhibiting stronger relationships with CO 2 emissions (R = 0.68-0.72) than soil chemical properties alone. Importantly, pH manipulation using NaOH in the absence of biochar failed to reproduce the enhanced enzyme activities and CO 2 emissions observed following biochar amendment, demonstrating that alkalization alone was insufficient to explain the contrasting CO 2 responses among different biochar treatments. These findings indicate that short-term CO 2 emissions following biochar application are shaped by feedstock-dependent biochar properties in association with microbial enzyme-mediated carbon turnover beyond the effect of soil pH. Our results highlight the importance of integrating biochar properties and microbial functional responses when evaluating short-term soil carbon mineralization and the environmental implications of biochar amendment.

title: Evaluating municipal solid waste-derived vermicompost for soil improvement, plant performance, and associated health risk in spinach
abstract: The management of municipal solid waste (MSW) is a global challenge, and composting provides a sustainable solution for converting organic fractions into compost. This study investigated the effects of municipal solid waste vermicompost (MSW VC ) on soil properties, morphological, biochemical and HM accumulation in spinach, along with associated human health risks. Pot experiments were conducted with six treatments: 20% (T1), 40% (T2), 60% (T3), 80% (T4) MSW VC doses, inorganic fertilizer (IF), and control (T0). Soil analyses revealed significant (p VC amendments. Biochemical parameters, including chlorophyll, carotenoids, protein, ascorbic, phenolics, and proline, were enhanced at moderate doses (20-40%) (p 60%) elevated lipid peroxidation and stress responses to HM. BCF indicated that Pb and Cu accumulation decreased with increasing MSW VC (p > 0.05), whereas Zn and Ni exhibited higher root and shoot uptake (p VC enhances soil properties, application must be carefully controlled to balance agricultural benefits against toxicity and food safety risks.

title: Enhanced nitrogen and manganese removal in a manganese redox-driven moving bed biofilm reactor: Role of extracellular polymeric substances
abstract: In this study, the continuous flow moving bed biofilm reactor (MBBR) was developed for conversion of nitrogen and manganese including MBBR1 (R1, with manganese redox cycling function) and MBBR2 (R2, control group). The result suggested that NH 4 + -N removal reached 95 ± 2% and 78 ± 1% by R1 and R2 with NO 3 - -N effluent concentrations of 2.1 ± 0.4 and 7.1 ± 0.6 mg L -1 , and TN removal through R1 increased compared with R2. Fluorescence characteristics and concentration of extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) were explored, and reactive oxygen species, apoptosis and enzyme activity of biofilm including the correlation between enzyme activity and EPS were analyzed. These results showed that protein decreased in R1 at 0-10 h, and it decreased in R2, and manganese addition promoted the development of an EPS-rich biofilm matrix. β-sheet content of EPS proteins increased from 29.9% in R2 to 34.6% in R1, and EPS mediated manganese redox might stimulate EPS production and simultaneously modified the chemical properties of EPS. Morphology, electrochemistry, and electron transport system activity of EPS/biofilm were investigated, and transcriptomic characteristics of biofilm were elaborated. These representations demonstrated that manganese redox cycling intensified the redox stress signal within biofilm. EPS mediated manganese redox might trigger oxidative stress, but the manganese-amended biofilm in R1 maintained the stronger antioxidant capacity and cell viability. Furthermore, manganese-amended biofilm from R1 had a strong response for protein synthesis and cellular machinery. This study deepens the application of EPS mediated manganese redox for nutrient removal.

title: Green synthesis of SnO2 nanoparticles using Calophyllum inophyllum seed shell extract and their biological and environmental applications
abstract: In this research, tin oxide nanoparticles (SnO 2 NPs) were green synthesized using Calophyllum inophyllum seed shell extract (CISSE) as both the stabilizing and capping agent, providing an ecologically friendly, sustainable, and cost-efficient synthesis route. The synthesized nanoparticles were comprehensively characterized to determine their optical properties, crystalline structure, functional groups, morphology, particle size, elemental composition, surface chemistry, and colloidal stability. The most prominent absorption peak (λ max ) in the UV-visible spectrum was found at 280 nm. FESEM and HR-TEM examination indicated that the synthesized nanoparticles had quasi spherical to spherical shape with an average size of 19.29 ± 5.25 nm. According to DLS analysis, the polydispersity index (PDI) was 0.389, and the mean hydrodynamic size was 85 nm. The zeta potential value of -27.9 mV suggested notable colloidal stability. Raman spectroscopy revealed a unique vibrational peak at 631 cm -1 , indicating the effective production of crystalline SnO 2 NPs. XPS analysis confirmed the presence of Sn and O, with Sn 3d peaks consistent with Sn 4+ in SnO 2 and C 1s signals indicating oxygen-containing carbonaceous species associated with the nanoparticle surface. The biosynthesized SnO 2 NPs exhibited potent larvicidal, antibacterial, antibiofilm, antiproliferative, and photocatalytic activities. They showed effective larvicidal activity against Aedes aegypti (LC 50 = 9.0 mg/L) and Culex quinquefasciatus (LC 50 = 7.5 mg/L) with minimal toxicity toward non-target organisms. The nanoparticles demonstrated strong antibacterial activity, with maximum inhibition zones of 23 mm against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, and pronounced antibiofilm activity, achieving 91.08% biofilm inhibition against Acinetobacter baumannii. Furthermore, SnO 2 NPs exhibited enhanced antiproliferative activity against SiHa cervical cancer cells (IC 50 = 57.81 μg/mL) compared with the crude extract (IC 50 = 233.56 μg/mL). Also, the synthesized SnO 2 NPs efficiently photocatalytically degraded ibuprofen under UV irradiation, highlighting its prospects for therapeutic and environmental uses.

title: Nocturnal road traffic noise and sleep during mid-adulthood in urban settings: Examining sex and socioeconomic differences within the DAS-EP project
abstract: Sleep is essential for physical and mental health but tends to deteriorate from mid adulthood, particularly among women. Nocturnal road traffic noise is a major environmental stressor that can disrupt sleep. This study aimed to examine the association between nocturnal road traffic noise and sleep health during mid-adulthood and explore potential sex-based differences. We conducted a cross sectional analysis using data from population health surveys (2021–2023) including 1,898 adults aged 40–60 living in urban areas of the Basque Autonomous Community, the Valencian Community, and Barcelona. Nocturnal road traffic noise was assessed using L night indicator, defined as the long-term average noise level during the night-time period (23:00-07:00), and estimated using official noise maps. Sleep health was assessed through self-reported measures of sleep duration, overall sleep satisfaction, and sleep quality using the SATED scale, a multidimensional measure of sleep health (Satisfaction, Alertness, Timing, Efficiency, and Duration). A Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) was used to identify covariate adjustment sets and associations were estimated using linear models accounting for the complex survey design. Women generally reported poorer sleep health than men, with lower sleep satisfaction and poorer sleep quality, and sleep quality increased with area-level household income. Noise exposure increased with income at lower levels, while different patterns were observed across regions after €50,000. The association between noise exposure and sleep health varied across regions and sleep health dimensions. In Barcelona, higher noise exposure was associated with greater sleep satisfaction, but this association was not significant in pooled meta analyses. In contrast, higher noise exposure was associated with poorer sleep quality in the Basque Country, with the pooled meta-analysis showing a similar overall pattern. These findings highlight the context-dependent nature of noise–sleep relationships and support the need for targeted public health strategies.

title: Independent and interactive effects of traffic-related noise and air pollution on lung function: A randomized crossover study in healthy young adults
abstract: Traffic noise and air pollution are major environmental stressors linked to adverse respiratory outcomes. We conducted a randomized crossover study in 51 healthy adults during evening rush hour beside a busy urban road to explore the independent and interactive effects of traffic noise and air pollution on lung function. Participants underwent four different interventions. For each intervention, noise levels and concentrations of ozone (O 3 ), nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ), PM 1 , PM 2.5 , and PM 10 were monitored, and lung function parameters of participants were measured, including forced vital capacity (FVC), forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV 1 ), FEV 1 /FVC, and forced expiratory flows (FEF 25 , FEF 50 , FEF 75 , FEF 25-75 ). Linear mixed-effects models (adjusted for age, sex, and BMI) were used to evaluate associations of traffic noise and/or air pollution with lung function. We found that after adjustment, higher traffic noise exposure was associated with declines in indicators reflecting dynamic ventilatory function. Regarding air pollutants, O 3 and PM 10 exhibited independent adverse effects on distal airways. Specifically, a 10 μg/m 3 increase of O 3 was associated with a 0.224 L/s reduction in FEF 75 , and the value is 0.215 L/s for a 10 μg/m 3 increase of PM 10 . More importantly, exploratory analyses identified potential synergistic interactions: noise co-exposure amplified declines in FEV 1 and small-airway flow associated with PM 1 and PM 2.5 , and enhanced the adverse effects of O 3 on mid-to-small airway flow. Therefore, to better protect respiratory health, especially during peak traffic hours, interventions should simultaneously target reductions in both traffic noise and air pollution levels, for vulnerable populations and healthy young adults.

title: Fates and characteristics of antibiotic resistance genes carried by viruses during a full-scale anaerobic sludge digestion
abstract: The transmission of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) mediated by viruses in sludge represents an emerging concern for antibiotic resistance dissemination. This study investigated the virus-carried ARGs (vARGs) profiles and potential risks in sludges collected from an entire anaerobic sludge digestion plant. A total of 79 unique vARGs spanning 10 antibiotic resistance classes were identified, with trimethoprim resistance genes being the most diverse. Although most vARGs (94.9%) exhibited low sequence similarity ( 5 - 10 6 VLPs/g) still remained in the final sludges. In the metagenomes, the levels of vARGs increased approximately 7-fold, suggesting that vARGs were more difficult to be moved than plasmid-associated ARGs and chromosome-associated ARGs. The host prediction suggested associations between some vARG-carrying viruses and potential pathogenic bacteria, which are worth further experimental validation. In summary, the persistence of vARGs in sludge remains a concern, even after the implementation of sludge treatment processes.

title: Synthesis and application of quaternized biomass cellulose microspheres for high-efficiency removal of water pollutants
abstract: The development of environmentally friendly, efficient and low-cost adsorbents for water purification is of great importance. In this study, cellulose microspheres (CM) with controllable size were prepared by a phase separation method and successfully modified with 3-chloro-2-hydroxypropyltrimethyl ammonium chloride (CHPTAC) to obtain positively charged functionalized cellulose microspheres (QCM). The QCM can adsorb typical anionic pollutants (Cr(VI)) and cationic pollutants (RhB). The maximum adsorption capacity of QCM for Cr(VI) was 3.97 mg g -1 (pH = 5, 45 °C), which conformed to the pseudo-secondary kinetics and Langmuir model, indicating that the process was a spontaneous heat-absorbing on a single molecular layer. The maximum adsorption capacity of RhB was 33.32 mg g -1 (pH = 7, 15 °C), which conformed to the pseudo-primary kinetics and Langmuir model, and the adsorption process was a spontaneous exothermic monolayer. The adsorption mechanism demonstrated the key role of quaternary ammonium groups in enhancing the adsorption performance. In addition, QCM was renewable and retained more than 95% of adsorption efficiency after three cycles. The above results indicated that QCM had good adsorption performance and structural stability for the removal of heavy metals and dyes from wastewater.

title: Biodegradation of oxidized lignite by Pseudomonas sp. TX1: Degradation products and metabolomic characterization
abstract: Microbial degradation offers a green pathway for resource recovery and clean conversion of low-rank coal. However, the mechanisms governing the extracellular depolymerization of coal macromolecules and intracellular metabolic regulation remain poorly understood. This study integrated solid-phase structural characterization, liquid-phase product analysis, and untargeted metabolomics to investigate lignite biodegradation by an indigenous isolate, Pseudomonas sp. TX1. During TX1 treatment of oxidized lignite, the culture supernatant reached an absorbance at 450 nm (A 450 ) of 2.67 after 10 days, indicating the accumulation of colored soluble components. The strain preferentially cleaves methylene bridges and alkyl side chains in lignite, followed by biological funneling of highly substituted aromatic rings into ring-opened intermediates. GC-MS analysis demonstrated that lignite was successfully depolymerized into high-value liquid-phase small molecules with broad industrial applications, including long-chain alkanes, fatty acid methyl esters, phenolic derivatives, and nitrogen-containing heterocycles. Metabolomic analysis revealed that aromatic monomers undergo ring-opening metabolism via the homogentisate and β-ketoadipate pathways. Concurrently, the pentose phosphate pathway is activated to supply reducing power, while ascorbic acid and melatonin cycles are regulated to counteract oxidative stress. This study elucidates the multi-scale molecular mechanism of coal biotransformation, providing a theoretical basis for developing low-rank coal bioconversion technologies.

title: CuS-Cu2S/γ-Fe2O3 for efficient Cr(VI) elimination from electroplating wastewater: The role of surface-active Cu-based sulfide phase regulation
abstract: Conventional adsorbents for Cr(VI) elimination from electroplating wastewater are constrained by limited uptake capacity, poor recyclability, and inadequate management of retained chromium. To tackle these issues, a magnetically recoverable CuS/γ-Fe 2 O 3 composite was developed as a reusable adsorbent. Upon thermal annealing, a partial phase transformation from CuS to Cu 2 S occurred, yielding a mixed CuS-Cu 2 S/γ-Fe 2 O 3 hybrid. This hybrid exhibited enhanced Cr(VI) capture, achieving 87.2 mg g -1 at pH 4.0, 25 °C, 0.5 g L -1 adsorbent dosage, and 50 mg L -1 initial Cr(VI). Elimination process proceeded via the adsorption-reduction route, governed by surface reductant availability and affinity aqueous Cr(VI) and H + . Although the CuS-to-Cu 2 S transformation reduced total reductant sites, it improved Cr(VI) and H + adsorption, likely due to the unique surface properties of Cu 2 S; hence, the CuS-Cu 2 S/γ-Fe 2 O 3 composite outperformed its single-phase counterpart. Moreover, this composite also showed good stability and reusability, maintaining 100% Cr(VI) removal over fifteen cycles while retaining magnetic recoverability. Furthermore, repeated adsorption enabled efficient Cr(VI) enrichment from electroplating wastewater onto CuS-Cu 2 S/γ-Fe 2 O 3 , allowing the spent adsorbent to serve as a potential substitute for chromium ore. In summary, these findings highlighted CuS-Cu 2 S/γ-Fe 2 O 3 as a highly promising adsorbent for treating Cr(VI)-bearing electroplating wastewater.

title: Aging-driven mobilization of endogenous phthalate esters from microplastics and the ecotoxicity of PAEs toward soil microbiota and plants
abstract: Microplastics are long-term sources of hazardous endogenous additives; however, the release behavior and ecological impacts of phthalate esters (PAEs) during environmental aging remain poorly understood. This study systematically examined the release of dibutyl phthalate (DBP) and di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) from microplastics under mechanical abrasion, accelerated H 2 O 2 oxidation, and prolonged exposure to mildly acidic conditions. We evaluated the concentration-dependent effects of DBP and DEHP on Escherichia coli, a culturable environmental microorganism, pak choi, and soil bacterial communities. Accelerated H 2 O 2 oxidation produced the greatest release, reaching 95.6% for DBP and 31.9% for DEHP, whereas release under mildly acidic exposure remained below 4%. Mechanical abrasion further increased PAE migration during chemical treatments. DBP and DEHP had limited effects on E. coli under the experimental conditions but inhibited culturable water- and soil-derived microorganisms in nutrient-limited media. Higher PAE concentrations significantly inhibited seed germination and plant growth, reducing biomass by up to 91.4%. PAE exposure also increased soil electrical conductivity and altered bacterial community composition, shifting the relative abundances of genera such as Sphingomonas and Bacillus. These findings indicate that endogenous PAE mobilization from microplastics varies with aging conditions and mechanical abrasion. In contrast, biological responses to DBP and DEHP depend on exposure concentration, compound identity, and nutrient availability. This study provides experimental insights into the environmental fate of plastic-associated PAEs and their potential ecological effects under various physicochemical stress conditions.

title: Salt-ion etching induced transformation of granular ZIF-8 into Fe-doped nanosheets for activating peracetic acid toward pollutant degradation
abstract: Conventional water treatment processes exhibit inherent limitations in the removal of trace emerging micropollutants. To address this challenge, we rationally designed ultrathin Fe-doped nanosheets via a one-step etching strategy using ferrous sulfate. This approach simultaneously transformed pristine granular ZIF-8 into a layered architecture and facilitated the uniform incorporation of iron active sites. The as-prepared catalyst was subsequently employed in a visible-light-driven peracetic acid (PAA) activation system for the efficient degradation of micropollutants. The etching treatment not only substantially increased the specific surface area of the nanosheets relative to their bulk counterparts but also ensured homogeneous dispersion of Fe species, thereby establishing stable Fe 2+ /Fe 3+ redox cycling centers that significantly accelerate electron transfer kinetics. In the ZIF-8-Fe-Nanosheets/PAA/simulated sunlight system, sulfamethazine (SMT) achieved near-complete degradation within 50 min. Moreover, the catalyst exhibited excellent broad-spectrum degradation activity, robust pH adaptability across a range of 3-9, and strong resistance to coexisting matrix constituents in real water samples. Radical quenching experiments identified hydroxyl radicals ( • OH) and singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ) as the dominant reactive oxygen species. Three plausible SMT degradation pathways were proposed, and toxicity assessment using quantitative structure-activity relationship analysis indicated lower biotoxicity of the transformation products compared to the parent compound. Overall, this work validates the Fe-doped nanosheet catalyst as an efficient PAA activator, and more broadly, paves the way for expanding PAA-based catalytic oxidation toward practical water treatment.

title: Visible-light-driven removal of bisphenol A using a Bi12SiO20/Bi2O3 S-scheme heterojunction: Performance and charge-transfer mechanism
abstract: Efficient removal of the emerging organic contaminant bisphenol A (BPA) remains an important challenge for sustainable water treatment. Herein, a series of BSO-Bi 2 O 3 heterojunction composites were synthesized via a facile in situ precipitation strategy to enhance visible-light photocatalytic degradation of BPA. Structural characterizations confirmed intimate interfacial contact between two components, facilitating strong electronic coupling across the BSO-Bi 2 O 3 interface. Among all as-prepared samples, the composite BSO-5%Bi 2 O 3 exhibited the highest photocatalytic performance, achieving nearly 90% BPA removal within 80 min, significantly outperforming pristine Bi 2 O 3 and Bi 12 SiO 20 . The enhanced photocatalytic performance was mainly attributed to extended visible-light absorption, accelerated charge separation, and efficient interfacial charge transfer. Trapping experiments and ESR analyses revealed that superoxide radicals (·O 2 − ) and holes (h + ) were the dominant reactive species involved in the degradation process. Electrochemical measurements combined with density-functional theory (DFT) calculations further revealed favorable interfacial charge redistribution and enhanced charge-transfer kinetics, supporting an S-scheme charge-transfer pathway that preserves charge carriers with strong redox capabilities. Moreover, the composite BSO-5%Bi 2 O 3 maintained excellent recycling stability and structural integrity after repeated use. This work provides an effective strategy for constructing efficient bismuth-based S-scheme photocatalysts for the photocatalytic removal of emerging organic contaminants.

title: Spatial confinement and electronic modulation of porous carbon-encapsulated Co3Mo3N coral-like architecture: Synergistically boosting peroxymonosulfate activation for robust recyclable 4-nitrophenol degradation
abstract: Cobalt-based nitrides are promising catalysts for the activation of peroxymonosulfate (PMS). However, their catalytic efficiency and stability can be hindered by insufficient interfacial electron transfer and the deactivation of active metal centers. In this study, a bimetallic synergy strategy is employed to synthesize a highly efficient cobalt-molybdenum bimetallic nitride composite (Co 3 Mo 3 N@C) through a two-step H 2 /Ar annealing process. The Co 3 Mo 3 N@C/PMS system achieved a 96.0% removal efficiency of 4-nitrophenol (4-NP) within 25 min, demonstrating kinetic rate constants that are 16.6-fold and 3.2-fold those of the Mo 2 N@C/PMS and Co 4 N@C/PMS systems, respectively. The enhanced catalytic performance can be primarily attributed to the wrinkled porous architecture, which exposes abundant accessible sites, and the synergistic Co-Mo electronic interaction that promotes interfacial electron transfer and redox cycling during PMS activation. Additionally, the system exhibits favorable catalytic performance across a broad pH range and under various water-matrix conditions. Mechanistic investigations reveal the coexistence of radical and non-radical oxidation pathways, along with an interfacial electron-transfer process. Furthermore, Co 3 Mo 3 N@C demonstrates good structural stability, reusability, and applicability towards different organic pollutants. These results indicate that coupling bimetallic electronic modulation with carbon confinement presents an effective strategy for designing efficient and durable PMS-activation catalysts for the remediation of organic pollutants.

title: Contrasting atmospheric behavior of PCDD/Fs and PBDD/Fs in a subtropical megacity: Source characteristics, regional transport, and gas-particle partitioning
abstract: Polychlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins and dibenzofurans (PCDD/Fs) are well-characterized toxic atmospheric pollutants, whereas much less is known about their brominated analogues, polybrominated dibenzo-p-dioxins and dibenzofurans (PBDD/Fs). Here, a year-round active sampling campaign was conducted in Guangzhou, a subtropical megacity in southern China, to simultaneously investigate atmospheric PCDD/Fs and PBDD/Fs in paired gas- and particle-phase samples. The annual mean total concentration of PBDD/Fs (1,435 ± 1,338 fg m -3 ; range: 279-10,403 fg m -3 ) was comparable to that of PCDD/Fs (1,892 ± 1,762 fg m -3 ; range: 313-11,456 fg m -3 ), and both compound classes were higher during winter-spring and lower in summer, although the seasonal contrast was weaker for PBDD/Fs. Backward trajectory and concentration-weighted trajectory analyses revealed stronger continental transport influence on PCDD/Fs, whereas PBDD/Fs showed weaker transport dependence and a more regionally confined pattern centered over the Pearl River Delta and coastal South China. Source apportionment associated PCDD/Fs mainly with industrial thermal processes, waste/biomass combustion, and aged regional background transport, while PBDD/Fs were more closely linked to brominated precursor- and material-related processes, possible traffic-related inputs and episodic thermal activities. PBDD/Fs were more strongly particle-bound than PCDD/Fs. However, PCDD/Fs exhibited systematic temperature-dependent partitioning and reasonable agreement with equilibrium-based models, whereas highly brominated PBDFs showed weak temperature dependence and poor model agreement, suggesting additional influences from source-related inputs, particle removal, and other non-equilibrium processes. Mean carcinogenic risks ranged from 6.75 × 10 -7 to 3.29 × 10 -6 across age groups, with the highest value observed for adults, while hazard quotients remained far below unity. These findings demonstrate distinct source, transport, and partitioning controls for PCDD/Fs and PBDD/Fs and support their independent atmospheric assessment.

title: Road-scale mapping of tire wear particles in Xizang and their potential atmospheric transport to adjacent glaciers
abstract: Tire wear particles (TWPs) are among the primary non-exhaust traffic emissions and present a key source of emerging pollution. As the core region of the Tibetan Plateau, Xizang is experiencing rapid expansion of road transportation, while the emission characteristics and environmental impacts of TWPs in this cryospheric region remain poorly understood. This study developed a road-network-based framework integrating field measurements, emission modeling, and atmospheric trajectory simulations to explore TWP pollution across Xizang. The results show that TWP emissions decreased from 2012 to 2016, followed by a rapid increase from 2016 to 2021, reaching 4589 tons/yr by 2021, with heavy trucks contributing 57.8% of total emissions. Road-scale mapping identifies emission hotspots within the Lhasa-Shigatse-Shannan urban agglomeration. Atmospheric trajectory simulations indicate that Lhasa-sourced TWPs could reach surrounding glaciers, with up to 90% of trajectories passing over these glaciers. This study provides a high-resolution TWP emission map across Xizang accounting for the rapid road network expansion, and offers scientific support for policy development to mitigate TWP pollution in cryospheric environments.

title: Retraction notice to “Photocatalytic degradation of congo red dye using nickel–titanium dioxide nanoflakes synthesized by Mukia madrasapatna leaf extract” [Environ. Res. 202 (2021) 111647]
Intestinal nuclear hormone receptors in response to environmentally relevant concentrations of 6-PPD quinone in Caenorhabditis elegans: Role in modulating multiple intestinal protective responses
abstract: 6-PPD quinone (6-PPDQ) is a fat-soluble pollutant. Considering important link between fat-soluble pollutants and nuclear hormone receptors (NHRs), we here systematically identified NHRs in the intestine in response to 6-PPDQ in nematodes. Among 140 intestinal NHRs genes, expression of 35 intestinal NHRs genes was dysregulated by 0.1-10 μg/L 6-PPDQ. Moreover, 6-PPDQ intestinal toxicity was aggravated by intestinal RNAi of nhr-8, nhr-12, nhr-31, nhr-41, nhr-67, nhr-68, nhr-80, nhr-232 and sex-1, and inhibited by intestinal RNAi of daf-12, nhr-3, nhr-14, nhr-22, nhr-84, nhr-120, and nhr-142. Furthermore, during control of 6-PPDQ intestinal toxicity, for underlying molecular basis, these candidate 16 intestinal NHR genes exhibited their function by modulating Mn-SODs, mitochondrial UPR, endoplasmic reticulum UPR, and their related molecular signals. Our observations highlight crucial role of NHRs in regulating 6-PPDQ intestinal toxicity by modulating certain intestinal protective responses.

title: Waste-derived functional materials for coupled nitrogen and phosphorus removal from eutrophic waters: A critical review
abstract: Waste-derived materials can supply phosphorus-binding surfaces, mineral precursors, electron donors, alkalinity, and porous carriers for nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) removal from eutrophic waters. However, reported performance is difficult to compare because studies differ in nutrient forms, influent loads, hydraulic conditions, test duration, and removal endpoints. This review evaluates steel slag, red mud and bauxite residue, ferruginous and sulfur-bearing mining residuals, magnesian wastes, agricultural ash, and biochar, focusing on composition, modification, removal mechanisms, process configuration, and long-term operation. Three findings emerge. First, compositions favorable for N removal may not favor P removal: sulfur-siderite media showed the highest reported N-removal rate at 25% siderite, but the highest P-removal rate at 75%. Second, beneficial interaction is clearest when one material function removes a measurable limitation on another process. For example, alkaline slag mitigates acidification during sulfur-autotrophic denitrification, while Ca, Mg, and Fe phases retain phosphate. Third, dominant limitations shift during operation from initial dissolution and reaction kinetics to intraparticle transport, surface passivation, clogging, breakthrough, and possible nutrient re-release. Organic-matter and bloom-derived metabolite loading can reverse iron-based phosphorus retention and therefore belongs in any realistic test protocol. Material formulation should therefore address electron supply, proton balance, oxygen distribution, and accessible P-reactive phases rather than rely on a fixed waste-mass ratio. Simultaneous concentration decreases should be distinguished from true process interaction using equal-load single-function controls and measurements of net N 2 production and stable or exported P. Continuous-flow studies in real waters should report breakthrough, head loss, leaching, greenhouse-gas emissions, and spent-media behavior to establish whether short-term removal persists throughout material service life under realistic hydraulic conditions and variable water quality.

title: Multi-scale causal inference and scenario prediction for carbon emissions from energy consumption in the Pearl River Delta urban agglomeration
abstract: Accurately identifying the driving mechanisms of carbon emissions from energy consumption is crucial for regional low-carbon transition. However, existing studies predominantly focus on statistical regression or trend extrapolation, lacking systematic characterization of multi-scale causal mechanisms and comprehensive evaluation of multi-scenario pathways. Therefore, this study integrates multi-source data on socioeconomic conditions, land use, and climate in the Pearl River Delta urban agglomeration (PRD) from 2000 to 2022. It constructs an integrated multi-source data-deep learning model evaluation-interpretability analysis -causal identification-scenario prediction. Key variables were identified using Sharpley Additivity Explanation (SHAP), followed by quantification of net effects and transmission pathways via causal graphs. Scenario prediction for carbon emissions from energy consumption (CE) were conducted using sub-scale optimal models. The results indicate (1) Scale-specific modeling indicates that the Sparrow Search Algorithm-optimized Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory Network (SSA-ConvLSTM) performs best at the pixel scale, while the Ister-Transformer deep learning model-which integrates temporal and spatial features-is optimal at the county and city scales. These models can be utilized for rolling evaluation and calibration. (2) SHAP analysis reveals a "scale synergy-morphological threshold/saturation-efficiency offsetting" relationship. Causal inference further demonstrates that pixel-scale PGDP exerts a negative effect on carbon emissions. At the county scale, GDP and JCQ primarily influence emissions through population, while at the city scale, population's direct impact on emissions is most significant. (3) Scenario simulations indicate that policy implementation should be stratified: municipal-scale "total volume constraints," county-scale "compact development and stock efficiency enhancement," and pixel-scale "energy efficiency and technological offsetting."
