The integrated framework of causal identification-interpretative analysis-scenario forecasting proposed in this study provides robust support for scientific carbon emission prediction and regional low-carbon policy formulation.

title: Climate-induced extreme heat associated with suicide risk mediated by poor sleep and emotional dysregulation: A nationally representative panel study from Bangladesh
abstract: Climate change-induced heat exposure is an emerging public health concern with potential mental health consequences, including suicide risk. Yet, in climate-vulnerable low- and middle-income countries the association between heat exposure and suicide risk, and the mediating mechanisms underlying this connection, remain underexplored. Using a nationally representative two-round panel survey from Bangladesh (n = 7492), we empirically examined whether poor sleep quality and emotional dysregulation mediate the relationship between exposure to extreme heat and suicide risk. Risk was assessed using a validated suicide cognitions scale across two seasonal rounds surveying the same individuals. Exposure to days ≥28°C over a two-week period was the lowest temperature threshold significantly associated with elevated suicide risk, with the highest risk detected at ≥35°C. At this 35°C threshold, 29.5% of the total association was mediated through poor sleep quality and 1.8% through emotional dysregulation. Risk was notably higher during the summer, and among less educated and poorer populations. This study provides novel evidence from a climate-vulnerable country on psychosocial mechanisms connecting heat and suicidality. As heat extremes intensify across the Global South, targeted mental health interventions, both infrastructural and psychological, may need consideration in climate adaptation strategies to protect the well-being of at-risk populations.

title: Developing a context-sensitive framework for evaluating urban greenspace indicators across diverse geographic settings
abstract: Urban greenspace exposure significantly impacts health within densely built environments. However, commonly used greenspace indicators, such as the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index and Green View Index, often yield divergent estimates of exposure. This reduces comparability across greenspace-health studies and leads to inconsistent findings. While recent research has identified that several factors (e.g., slope, building density) contribute to these discrepancies, these factors often co-occur to form complex geographic contexts. Yet, few studies have systematically examined how these co-occurring environmental factors form geographic contexts and subsequently contribute to these measurement differences. This study fills this gap by designing a context-sensitive diagnostic framework to elucidate these measurement discrepancies. We applied this framework in Hong Kong to evaluate five commonly used greenspace indicators, including the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index, the Enhanced Vegetation Index, the Green View Index, and three-dimensional vegetation metrics like Vegetation Volume Index and Canopy Volume Index, to investigate how these indicators vary across different geographic contexts. The findings reveal three context-dependent patterns of divergence among greenspace indicators: differences in measurement sensitivity between satellite indicators, observation-perspective differences between overhead measures and street-level visibility, and contrasts between two-dimensional and three-dimensional representations of vegetation structure. Drawing on these diagnostic insights from the Hong Kong case study, we developed a practical decision-support protocol that links indicator selection to measurement focus, observation perspective, and geographic context. This empirical application illustrates how the framework can support more context-sensitive interpretation of greenspace exposure indicators and inform indicator selection in high-density urban environments.

title: Strain specificity and inoculation sequence shape quorum sensing-based biofilm bioaugmentation: Roles of resource competition and quorum quenching
abstract: Quorum sensing (QS)-based bioaugmentation is promising for accelerating biofilm establishment and bioreactor start-up. However, its effectiveness is determined by biotic interactions between exogenous QS bacteria and indigenous microorganisms, which are shaped by the ecological roles of strain-specific traits and inoculation sequence. This study systematically investigated strain-specific biotic interactions between four QS strains (wastewater-derived strain X3, AM7 and AM9, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1) and forty non-QS strains under three inoculation strategies with different inoculation time (i.e., one-step mixing, pre-inoculation and post-addition). Biotic interactions associated with resource competition and quorum quenching (QQ) activity were distinguished using model strain Escherichia coli with strong substrate uptake capability and Rhodococcus sp. BH4 with QQ activity. The QS-mediated biofilm regulation was jointly shaped by strain-specific characteristics and inoculation sequence. The pre-inoculation strategy enhanced biofilm induction by AM9 and X3, alleviated negative interactions for AM7, but intensified inhibition by PAO1. By contrast, the post-addition strategy strengthened biofilm reduction by AM9, X3 and AM7, while it enhanced biofilm induction by PAO1. Resource competition alone was insufficient to suppress QS-mediated biofilm induction. However, QQ activity induced by BH4 significantly reduced extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) production and QS-mediated biofilm induction, particularly for X3 and AM7, which was distinguished as the major ecological constraint. Notably, AM9 with strong QS activity maintained biofilm-promoting capability. This study provides ecological principles for QS strain selection and inoculation optimization, facilitating the improvement of QS-based bioaugmentation for rapid start-up of biofilm-based processes.

title: Developmental toxicity of curcumin-mediated silver nanoparticles in the freshwater snails Biomphalaria glabrata
abstract: Curcumin-mediated silver nanoparticles (Curc-AgNPs) are promising biogenic nanomaterials in medical and environmental applications. However, their ecotoxicological impact to non-target aquatic species remains understood. This study assessed the toxicity of Curc-AgNPs in the neotropical freshwater snails Biomphalaria glabrata , considering multiple developmental and post-hatching endpoints, including embryonic mortality, hatching success, developmental progression, heart rate, embryonic cell viability, and mortality of newly hatched snails. Curc-AgNPs (14 ± 4 nm) were synthesized by reducing AgNO 3 with curcumin and characterized by multiples techniques. Curc-AgNPs induced mortality, hatching inhibition, developmental delay, decreased heart rate and cell viability in a time- and concentration-dependent pattern. The cumulative developmental toxicity was confirmed by declining 50% effective concentration (LC50) to embryos (20.96 mg L -1 at 24 h to 1.47 mg L -1 at 168 h) and newly hatched snails (53.7 mg L -1 at 24 h to 37.5 mg L -1 at 120 h). Curc-AgNPs almost completely inhibited snail hatching at concentrations ≥ 1.88 mg L -1 and delayed embryonic development, mainly at gastrula and trochophore stages. Sub-lethal effects were observed in terms of cardiac activity (heart rate reduced by ∼41% at 1.88 mg L -1 ) and reduced cell viability in embryos exposed to Curc-AgNPs at concentration ranging 0.18 to 0.75 mg L -1 . Also, Curc-AgNPs induced higher toxicity in embryos than in newly hatched B. glabrata , indicating that the early developmental stages of gastropod are more susceptible to the toxicity of Curc-AgNPs. Overall, Curc-AgNPs exhibited pronounced embryotoxicity and stage-dependent molluscicidal effects. Although toxic, these concentrations exceed predicted environmental levels, representing hazard, not environmental risk.

title: Synthesis-dependent performance of Na-Ni-Al dual-function materials for integrated CO2 capture and methanation
abstract: Integrated CO 2 capture and methanation (ICCM) is a promising route for converting CO 2 into synthetic natural gas using renewable H 2 . ICCM requires a material to capture carbon and make them available for subsequent hydrogenation. This study compares Na-Ni-Al dual-function materials prepared by sol-gel and impregnation route and examines the effects of the sodium precursor. This study compares sol-gel and impregnation routes to examine how synthesis-dependent organization of Na-derived sorption domains and Ni active sites affects ICCM performance. The optimized NaNiAl-SG-CO 3 exhibits superior performance, delivering a desorbable CO 2 capacity of 461.85 μmol g -1 and a CH 4 yield of 380.88 μmol g -1 at 340 °C, representing 30.7% higher yield and 24.8% higher peak rate than the impregnation-derived counterpart, along with enhanced CH 4 selectivity and cyclic stability. The sol-gel material achieved this higher methane yield despite having a lower BET surface area. CO 2 temperature-programmed desorption showed a different distribution of carbon-release temperatures, while temperature-programmed hydrogenation showed CH 4 formation at lower temperature. The results indicate that synthesis-dependent changes in carbon retention and hydrogenation response are relevant to material performance. These findings provide an experimental basis for developing noble-metal-free materials for cyclic CO 2 utilization.

title: Presence and accumulation of aluminum in the aquatic environment of rivers supplying the Baltic coastal lake Jamno (Poland)
abstract: A four-year study (2019-2022) was conducted on water, bottom sediments, and hydromacrophytes collected from three rivers: Strzeżenica River, Unieść River, and Dzierżęcinka River which discharge coastal Lake Jamno (Poland). A total of 168 water samples, 168 bottom sediment samples, and 426 aquatic plant samples were analyzed. The presence of aluminum in the components of the aquatic environment was determined against the background of hydrochemical parameters. Environmental quality was assessed using contamination and accumulation indices (MPI, BCF, CF, Cf, DC). Aluminum concentrations in river water ranged from 0.0187 to 0.2788 mg Al·dm -3 and remained below the environmental threshold of 0.4 mg Al·dm -3 . Mean concentrations in water were 0.0845, 0.0986, and 0.1048 mg Al·dm -3 in the Strzeżenica, Unieść, and Dzierżęcinka rivers, respectively. In contrast, substantially higher Al concentrations were recorded in bottom sediments, reaching mean values of 4137.43 mg kg -1 in Strzeżenica, 267.23 mg kg -1 in Unieść, and 971.49 mg kg -1 in Dzierżęcinka. Mean Al concentrations in aquatic plants were 1690.67, 826.16, and 1125.66 mg kg -1 , respectively. The MPI for water was low in all rivers (0.0670-0.0812), whereas substantially higher values were recorded for sediments (70.77-504.77) and plants (650.47-989.90). The highest accumulation and contamination were observed in the Strzeżenica River, where the contamination factor (Cf) reached 4.1374 and the integrated degree of contamination (DC) for the studied river system was 5.3761. Bioaccumulation factors relative to water (BCFW) reached 29,278.55 in Strzeżenica, compared with 11,950.47 and 19,040.71 in Unieść and Dzierżęcinka, respectively. These results demonstrate a clear contrast between the relatively low Al burden in the water column and its substantial accumulation in sediments and aquatic plants. Bottom sediments therefore represent the major reservoir of Al in the studied river systems and may constitute an important secondary source of metal exposure to aquatic biota. The findings highlight the importance of multi-matrix monitoring of aluminum in coastal river ecosystems, as water-column measurements alone may underestimate the long-term accumulation and environmental burden of this metal.

title: Data-driven approach to estimate ambient ammonia concentrations
abstract: The Netherlands experiences significant environmental impacts from reactive nitrogen, particularly ammonia (NH 3 ), whose long-term deposition harms soil, water, and biodiversity. NH 3 is emitted mainly from agriculture and its levels can be very high and variable in intensive livestock areas. Although monitoring stations are set up across multiple locations, data gaps may still arise due to issues with measurement instruments. Therefore, there is a need for models that can reliably fill in these missing observations. In this study, we first applied Linear Regression, Random Forest, and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) models to predict one day ahead NH 3 concentrations at six sites (De Zilk, Valthermond, Vredepeel, Wekerom, Wieringerwerf, Zegveld) in the Netherlands. All models captured daily NH 3 trends, with Random Forest initially performing best (R 2 up to 0.59 at Valthermond). Predictions were strongly driven by lagged NH 3 values with wind speed and precipitation contributing moderately. After correcting for prediction lag caused by autocorrelation, the linear regression performed best at most sites (with best performance observed at Zegveld with R 2 of 0.84) and was used for gap filling. It maintained reasonable accuracy despite sparse observations (every 2–7 days), with most sites (De Zilk, Valthermond, Vredepeel, Wekerom, Zegveld) exhibiting a significant correlation of almost or more than 0.5 even at 7 days measurement gaps. Additionally, we noted that historical data from existing sites could be effectively used to fill gaps at newly established locations that exhibited similar distributions of NH 3 .

title: Comment on Gutiérrez et al., Environmental Research 308 (2026) 125579 Assemblage-level spatial inference in a mixed resident–migratory fish dataset
Systematic evaluation and machine learning-based driver analysis of cadmium-induced osteotoxicity in mammals
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) is a persistent environmental pollutant with a biological half-life of several decades in animals. However, the osteotoxic effects in the mammalian skeletal system and their underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Using 374 control-observation comparisons from 47 studies, we systematically evaluated Cd-associated skeletal toxicity through meta-analysis and machine learning. The results indicate that Cd exposure significantly impairs overall bone health (13.68%, P 2 = 0.752, RMSE = 0.325), highlighting its strong potential for predicting Cd-induced bone toxicity risk. SHAP analysis identified response indicators (9.5%-23.3%) and Cd concentration plus duration (18%) as major contributors to osteotoxic response variation. Biologically, these findings indicate that Cd-associated osteotoxicity is characterized by heterogeneous sensitivity across bone-remodeling endpoints, while exposure concentration and duration modulate the magnitude of this multi-target skeletal response. These findings provide a basis for refining cadmium risk assessment and screening early-warning biomarkers.

title: Cellular Responses of Microcystis aeruginosa to Environmentally Relevant PFBA Concentrations under Different Nutrient Conditions
abstract: Perfluorobutanoic acid (PFBA), a short-chain alternative to perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), has been increasingly detected in aquatic environments due to its widespread applications. However, its ecological effects on aquatic organisms under environmentally relevant exposure levels and different nutrient conditions remain poorly understood. In this study, Microcystis aeruginosa was exposed to PFBA concentrations of 0.2 and 200 μg/L under different nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) availability, resulting in a 7 × 3 nutrient condition × PFBA concentration experimental design including the PFBA-free controls. The acute toxicity test showed that PFBA inhibited algal growth in a concentration-dependent manner, with a 72-h half-maximal effective concentration (EC 50 ) of 24.83 mg/L, indicating that the concentrations used in this study were far below acute toxic levels. On Day 3, 200 μg/L PFBA significantly inhibited algal growth under N-limited conditions, with inhibition rates of 29.80% and 23.13% in the LN (1 mg/L N, 7.1 mg/L P) and LNP (1 mg/L N, 0.05 mg/L P) groups, respectively. In contrast, 0.2 μg/L PFBA showed a slight growth-promoting effect under moderate nutrient conditions. However, after 10 days of exposure, PFBA did not significantly affect algal density in most treatment groups, and the effects of PFBA observed during the early exposure stage were attenuated over prolonged cultivation. Nutrient limitation significantly reduced algal growth, chlorophyll a content, and intracellular microcystin-LR levels, while promoting oxidative stress responses and extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) secretion. Under the experimental conditions, N limitation exerted stronger inhibitory effects on algal growth than P limitation and induced more pronounced oxidative stress responses. Although PFBA did not significantly alter the final algal density, it still was associated with changes in several physiological and molecular responses under specific nutrient conditions, including changes in reactive oxygen species accumulation, antioxidant enzyme activities, extracellular polymeric substances secretion, and the expression of photosynthesis-related genes (psaB, psbD, and rbcL). This study provides insights into the toxicological effects of PFBA on microalgae in aquatic environments.

title: Surface-engineered nanostructured adsorbents for CO2 capture: From material design to process integration and industrial deployment
abstract: The growing necessity to curb CO 2 emissions from man-made sources has driven the development of highly efficient and economical approaches to carbon capture. The current review is intended to give an overview and critical analysis of nanomaterial-based adsorbents for CO 2 capture with specific consideration of the connections between nanomaterial properties, adsorption processes, process integration, and industrial application. As opposed to the majority of literature surveys, which concentrate on either certain classes of materials or adsorption capacity of various materials separately, the review proposes a holistic view by combining information on the correlations of pore structure, surface chemistry, thermodynamics, adsorption kinetics, selectivity principles, and regeneration behavior of different nanostructured adsorbents, such as metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), covalent organic frameworks (COFs), hierarchical nanoporous carbons, graphene analogs, silica hybrids, metal oxides, and bioinspired materials. Special focus is paid to surface engineering of adsorbents, including amine grafting, heteroatom doping, and compositing, and its influence on CO 2 affinity, cyclic stability, and transport properties of adsorbents. Apart from the lab-scale efficiency, it analyzes issues of scale-up, regeneration efficiency, process intensification, techno-economic viability, and life-cycle sustainability. New possibilities such as machine-learning aided design of new adsorbents, standardized performance measures, and the concept of circular economy are also discussed. This review acts as a guideline and framework for designing nanostructured adsorbents that can be used in carbon management on a large scale.

title: Unraveling divergent water quality recovery in subtropical shallow lakes under climate variability and human pressure: Drivers, bottlenecks, and management implications
abstract: Water quality recovery in shallow lakes remains spatially uneven under climate variability and continuous pollutant inputs, while the relative importance of source-specific pollutant discharges and hydrological conditions remains unclear. We integrated 2011-2023 monitoring data from 104 sites across 11 shallow lakes in Jiangsu, China, with meteorological, hydrological, socioeconomic, and source-specific pollutant discharge data. Spatiotemporal patterns in trophic level index (TLI), total nitrogen (TN), total phosphorus (TP), permanganate index (COD Mn ), ammonia nitrogen (NH 3 -N), and chlorophyll-a (Chla) were assessed. Random forest regression (RFR) coupled with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used to characterize predictive relationships and variable importance, and generalized additive models (GAMs) were applied for scenario simulations. Water quality trajectories differed markedly between regions. TLI and most indicators increased in northern Jiangsu lakes (NJL), with stronger deterioration during flood seasons, whereas most southern Jiangsu lakes (SJL) improved. Lakes Ge and Changdang nevertheless remained nutrient hotspots, with median TN concentrations above 2.0 mg/L. In the NJL, agricultural pollution, temperature, wind conditions, and hydrological variability showed strong predictive associations with water quality deterioration. In the SJL, industrial, domestic, and agricultural inputs remained important predictors, while greater inflow and wastewater treatment rate were generally associated with lower predicted eutrophication levels. Scenario simulations showed that greater pollutant-discharge reduction was consistently associated with lower modeled TN and TP, although the estimated reduction levels needed to approach water quality targets varied among lakes. Agricultural source control remained particularly important in the NJL, whereas hydrological responses were lake specific. In the SJL, coordinated control of industrial, domestic, and agricultural inputs remained important, with inflow regulation showing variable modeled responses among lakes. These findings highlight regional differences in water quality responses and support lake-specific management that prioritizes source reduction while considering local hydrological conditions.

title: Divergent morphological responses accompany the warming-induced competitive shift from Planktothrix (maladaptive plasticity) to Microcystis (functionally beneficial morphological stability)
abstract: Cyanobacterial blooms, particularly those dominated by Microcystis and Planktothrix, are becoming more frequent in eutrophic freshwaters worldwide. Although these two species often exhibit seasonal succession linked to rising temperatures, the role of morphological responses in shaping their temperature-dependent competitive dynamics remains largely unexplored. In this study, we conducted controlled laboratory experiments to examine how temperature (20, 26, and 32 °C) modulates the competitive interaction between Planktothrix agardhii and Microcystis aeruginosa under both mono-culture and co-culture conditions. Population growth and morphological traits of both species were tracked throughout the experiment. Key findings include: (1) At 20 °C, the two species coexisted with only weak mutual inhibition; at 32 °C, M. aeruginosa nearly outcompeted P. agardhii, and competitive displacement rates increased markedly along the temperature gradient. (2) P. agardhii showed strong morphological plasticity in response to competition, characterized by shortened filaments, increased cell width, and a reduced surface area to volume ratio, with the most severe morphological degradation coinciding with the strongest competitive suppression at 32 °C, a pattern consistent with a maladaptive stress response rather than beneficial acclimation; (3) M. aeruginosa maintained stable morphology across all temperatures when competing against P. agardhii. These results indicate that temperature, morphological strategy, and competitive outcome are closely associated, and that opposing morphological responses, maladaptive plasticity in P. agardhii versus a stable and functionally beneficial morphology in M. aeruginosa, accompany the temperature-driven shift in bloom composition. Notably, filament fragmentation in Planktothrix populations may serve as an early indicator of an impending transition toward Microcystis-dominated toxic blooms under climate warming.

title: Microbial-mediated degradation of aflatoxin B1 in agricultural soil
abstract: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is commonly present in agricultural soil and poses severe threats to soil ecosystems due to its high toxicity, yet its environmental fate and microbial-mediated degradation mechanisms remain insufficiently studied. In this study, the environmental behavior of AFB1 in an agricultural soil was investigated. Metagenomic analysis showed that exposure to a higher concentration of AFB1 (5.0 mg kg -1 ) altered soil bacterial community structure and reduced community diversity. After 30 days of incubation, AFB1 was slowly removed from natural soil microcosms but persisted in sterilized soil microcosms, indicating that indigenous soil microorganisms make a major contribution to AFB1 dissipation. Exposure to high-concentration AFB1 significantly enriched the genus Nocardioides, and a novel AFB1-degrading strain, Nocardioides sp. N13 (phylum Actinomycetota), was isolated from the agricultural soil. Strain N13 harbors three genes encoding putative F 420 H 2 -dependent reductase (FDR) homologs, which are hypothesized to be involved in the initial degradation of AFB1. Bioinformatics analysis revealed that putative FDR homolog-carrying bacteria are mostly assigned to the phylum Actinomycetota and are widely distributed across diverse soil environments worldwide. These findings provide a theoretical basis and potential microbial resources for mitigating AFB1 contamination in soil ecosystems.

title: Microplastics modulate aqueous photolysis of phenolic intermediate-volatility organic compounds
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are ubiquitous in the atmosphere, yet their influence on the photochemical fate of coexisting organic pollutants in atmospheric aqueous phases remains poorly understood. This study investigated the effects of polystyrene (PS), polypropylene (PP), and polyethylene (PE) on the aqueous photodegradation of two phenolic intermediate-volatility organic compounds (IVOCs), 4-ethylphenol (4-EP) and 2,6-dimethoxy-4-methylphenol (DMMP), under natural and simulated sunlight. 4-EP loss in solution was significantly inhibited by all three MPs (PE > PP ≈ PS), whereas DMMP showed no significant variation among MP treatments. Adsorption of 4-EP followed the same polymer-dependent trend (PE > PP > PS), while DMMP exhibited uniformly low adsorption across all MPs. Aging introduced oxygen-containing groups onto MP surfaces, with PE showing substantial C-O enrichment. Under simulated sunlight conditions, sorption correction did not substantially alleviate the MP-induced inhibition of 4-EP, accounting for only 2.9%-4.2% of the total inhibition, suggesting that the suppression stemmed primarily from non-adsorptive mechanisms, such as optical shielding or interfacial interactions. Phototransformation also led to changes in product absorbance and oxidative potential (OP), with the extent of these changes modulated by MP type. Product absorbance at 275 nm followed PP > PS > PE for 4-EP, whereas DMMP showed the highest absorbance in the PE system. These findings suggest that atmospheric MPs may alter the aqueous-phase phototransformation of phenolic IVOCs and modulate the optical properties and OP of mixtures in a compound- and polymer-dependent manner.

title: Revitalizing simultaneous nitrification, endogenous denitrification and phosphorus removal under carbon starvation: Redox mediator-modulated electron transfer and metabolic coordination
abstract: The simultaneous nitrification, endogenous denitrification and phosphorus removal (SNEDPR) process provides a resource-efficient paradigm for synergistic nutrient removal. However, its efficacy can be severely constrained by limited electron-donor availability and inefficient intracellular electron transfer under low carbon-to-nitrogen (C/N) ratios. Herein, we demonstrate that anthraquinone-2-sulfonate (AQS) serves as an effective redox mediator to alleviate these electron-transfer limitations. Under severe carbon-limited conditions, with an influent C/N ratio of 3.24±0.11, supplementation with 0.3 mmol/L AQS successfully restored the deteriorated system, recovering total inorganic nitrogen (TIN) removal efficiency to 96.57±0.87% while sustaining robust phosphorus removal (96.47±2.68%). Batch kinetic assays showed that AQS increased electron transfer system activity (ETSA) by over 100%, accompanied by enhanced nitrification-related activity, endogenous denitrification and phosphorus uptake. Integrated metagenomic and metatranscriptomic analyses further revealed transcriptional responses consistent with an electron-shuttling role of AQS, including enhanced ETC-associated electron-transfer potential and increased transcription of downstream denitrification enzymes. ATP synthase-related transcription was also enhanced, indicating an increased potential for PMF-coupled cellular energy conservation. Consequently, increased transcription was observed for key functional genes involved in nitrification (amoABC, nxrAB), denitrification (narGHI, napAB, nirKS, nosZ), and polyphosphate synthesis (ppk). Furthermore, AQS-amended operation was associated with microbial community succession toward a more specialized consortium, in which comammox, Thauera and Candidatus Accumulibacter clade ⅡC were associated with nitrification, endogenous denitrification, and denitrifying phosphorus removal, respectively. Although practical translation will require effective retention or recovery of soluble AQS, these findings demonstrate the potential of AQS-enhanced SNEDPR under carbon-limited conditions and provide multi-omics evidence linking improved nutrient removal with increased electron-transfer activity and coordinated microbial metabolic responses.

title: Meta-omic insight into the community-level tolerance of the activated sludge to limited-dose ionizing radiation (LimDIR)
abstract: Ionizing radiation is a promising advanced oxidation process for wastewater treatment, yet the community-level tolerance mechanisms of conventional activated sludge (CAS) under limited-dose ionizing radiation (LimDIR, 2-50 Gy) remain poorly characterized. To address this knowledge gap, we investigated such tolerance mechanisms by integrating batch experiments, 16S rRNA profiling, metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and metagenome-assembled genome (MAG)-resolved analyses of glucose-fed communities receiving a single acute X-ray dose. Under LimDIR, the CAS community maintained NH 4 + -N removal despite transient inhibition at 2-15 Gy and recovery at higher doses, and progressively enhanced carbon removal (from 64.5% to 71.6%, R 2 = 0.85 with dose), while community diversity and the dominant phylogenetic framework were preserved even though genus-level composition shifted. In contrast, transcriptional profiles responded sensitively to irradiation, indicating that resilience was mainly driven by functional regulation rather than compositional turnover. Mechanistically, the dose-dependent increase in repair transcripts was carried by RecA-mediated homologous recombination together with the SOS/translesion damage-tolerance set, and enzymatic antioxidant systems constituted the major defense against oxidative stress. Community-level tolerance was further supported by quorum sensing, two-component systems, biofilm/extracellular polymeric substance (EPS)-related protection, and syntrophic carbon and nitrogen metabolism. MAG-resolved analysis suggested a core-partner cooperative tolerance model. In this model, self-protective core taxa encoded integrated DNA repair, antioxidant defense, and stress-responsive regulatory functions, whereas partner populations supplied essential structural components, including lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis, and metabolic complementarity required for community-level stability. Functional redundancy across taxa further buffered irradiation stress and sustained process performance. These findings indicate LimDIR tolerance in activated sludge as a cooperative, multilayer community property and provide a mechanistic basis for the resilience of biological wastewater treatment under irradiation stress.

title: BTCA/Ca2+-reinforced sodium alginate/chitosan/MWCNT aerogel for sustainable remediation of herbicide-contaminated water: Adsorption performance and molecular insights
abstract: The efficient removal of pesticide pollution from wastewater using adsorbents is highly desirable. A sodium alginate/chitosan/multi-walled carbon nanotube (SA-CS-MWCNTs) aerogel reinforced with 1,2,3,4-butanetetracarboxylic acid and Ca 2+ was prepared for separate adsorption of sulfentrazone and diuron. The aerogel exhibited a hydrated compressive modulus of 45.60 kPa and 6.50% mass loss after 14 days of aqueous immersion, indicating improved mechanical and aqueous stability relative to the BTCA-treated control without CaCl 2 treatment. Adsorption capacities reached 70.93 and 54.93 mg·g -1 for sulfentrazone and diuron, respectively. Nonlinear fitting favored pseudo-first-order kinetics for sulfentrazone and pseudo-second-order kinetics for diuron. The equilibrium adsorption data were described by the Langmuir model within the investigated concentration range. After five adsorption-desorption cycles, the aerogel retained adsorption capacities of 49.03 mg·g -1 for sulfentrazone and 33.77 mg·g -1 for diuron, demonstrating appreciable reusability. FTIR, XPS and density functional theory calculations revealed that adsorption was governed by multiple non-covalent interactions, including electrostatic attraction, hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic interactions and π-π stacking. These findings highlight the potential of BTCA/Ca 2+ -reinforced aerogels for herbicide adsorption.

title: Synergistic catalytic humification of coal gasification slag and cotton stalk via co-pyrolysis for high-performance humic acid-containing fertilizer
abstract: Achieving high-value conversion of industrial solid waste and agricultural biomass is important for advancing circular agriculture. In this study, an alkaline co-thermal activation strategy was developed to convert coal gasification slag (CGS), rich in Fe 2 O 3 , CaO, and SiO 2 , and cotton stalk (CS), rich in lignocellulose, into a multifunctional humic acid-containing fertilizer. The optimal preparation conditions were a CGS/CS mass ratio of 2 : 5, a pyrolysis temperature of 220 °C, a residence time of 120 min, and a KOH dosage of 20% based on CS, under which the artificial total humic acid yield reached 51.02% ± 1.10%. Under alkaline thermal conditions, the mineral components in CGS are activated and interact with organic intermediates derived from CS. These mineral-organic interactions may have facilitated the transformation and condensation of lignocellulosic derivatives, promoting the formation of aromatic and oxygen-containing carbon structures and contributing to the development of humus-like structures. FTIR and 13 C NMR analyses revealed distinct aromatic and oxygen-containing carbon characteristics between the resulting product and mineral-derived potassium humate (M-HA-K). After solid-liquid separation, the water-soluble fraction (SF) contained water-soluble humic substances and nutrients, showing potential for short-term growth promotion, whereas the solid residue (IF) retained mineral components and carbonaceous structures, showing potential for use as a soil amendment. Hydroponic and pot experiments confirmed that humic substances and activated mineral elements synergistically enhanced wheat growth. This work provides a practical zero-waste route for producing multifunctional humic-based fertilizers from industrial and agricultural wastes.

title: A wireless and passive RFID-based sensing system for the detection of Cd2+ in soil: A novel approach for onsite detection of hazardous metals
abstract: Cd 2+ pollution seriously endangers ecological safety and human health, and it is of great importance to develop a rapid onsite detection strategy for Cd 2+ . This study presented a wireless and passive radio frequency identification (RFID)-based sensing system for the rapid onsite detection of Cd 2+ in soil. The sensing system comprised three core components: a polyaniline/cysteine (PANI/Cys) chemiresistive sensing element, an ultra-high frequency (UHF) RFID tag (which collectively formed the RF-tagged sensor), and a dedicated sensing platform. The sensing principle relies on the specific chelation between Cys and Cd 2+ , which changes the resistance of the PANI/Cys sensing element. The RF-tagged sensor responds to the resistance variation through impedance mismatch. A wireless and passive detection method based on impedance mismatch was developed: the sensing platform captured variations in the minimum response power (MRP) of the RF module induced by this impedance mismatch, and a segmented linear correlation between MRP and Cd 2+ concentration was well established over the ranges of 1-10 ppb (μg/L) and 10-100 ppb (μg/L), with a limit of detection (LoD) of 3.81 ppb (μg/L) for the detection of Cd 2+ . In the analysis of real soil samples, all RMSE values were no more than 10 μg/kg, and the sensing system enabled rapid onsite detection within 30-120 s. It should be noted that this work required soil extraction pretreatment and could not realize direct onsite detection of solid soil matrices. Nevertheless, it offered a practical tool for soil pollution risk assessment and exhibited considerable potential for soil environmental management.

title: FTO deficiency mediates ferroptosis to exacerbate cobalt-induced neurotoxicity
abstract: Cobalt, a toxic environmental contaminant, has been implicated in human neurological damage. However, the detailed molecular basis of cobalt-triggered neurotoxicity remains poorly uncovered. In the present study, we elucidated the N6-methyladenosine (m6A) demethylase fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) downregulation mediates the activation of ferroptosis to drive cobalt-triggered neurodegeneration. We established an in vitro model using H4 cells and an in vivo model using C57BL/6 mice. Animal experiments provided initial evidence underscoring the critical involvement of ferroptosis in cobalt-associated neurotoxicity. Furthermore, in vitro assays revealed that ferroptosis is triggered subsequent to oxidative stress induced by cobalt exposure. Notably, MeRIP-seq profiling of H4 cells and mouse cortex revealed that ferroptosis-associated genes exhibited differential m6A modification, suggesting m6A modification might be involved in modulating ferroptosis. Concurrently, Gene Ontology and KEGG enrichment analyses revealed that genes bearing differential m6A modifications were significantly clustered within pathways linked to ferroptosis as well as neurodegenerative diseases. Moreover, we found that FTO depletion effectively enhanced ferroptosis following cobalt-induced oxidative stress. Mechanistically, FTO depletion enhanced m6A modification of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and transferrin receptor protein 1 (TFRC) mRNAs, leading to reduced GPX4 and elevated TFRC expression, which aggravated cobalt-induced ferroptosis. More importantly, we observed that central nervous system specific knockout of Fto exacerbated cobalt-induced neurobehavioral deficits and neuropathological damage through ferroptosis activation. Collectively, these results provide important insights into cobalt-induced neurotoxicity by targeting FTO deficiency-mediated ferroptosis and offer an innovative strategy for investigating neurodegenerative processes driven by environmental toxicants.

title: Assimilation-dominated metabolism pathway enables efficient inorganic nitrogen removal and biomass nitrogen accumulation in aerobic-heterotrophic strain R. pyridinivorans B403
abstract: Biological treatment is widely used for nitrogen removal from wastewater. The discovery of aerobic-heterotrophic nitrogen removal (AHNR) strains challenged conventional views, yet research has concentrated on nitrification/denitrification while the contribution of ammonia assimilation has received little attention. In this study, the nitrogen metabolism of AHNR strain R. pyridinivorans B403 was characterized. Under optimal conditions (C/N = 11.5, salinity = 0.47%, inoculation amount = 3.0% (v/v)), B403 achieved liquid-phase removal efficiencies of 100%, 86.61%, and 92.24% for NH 4 + -N, NO 3 - -N, and NO 2 - -N, with maximum rates of 18.77 mg/(L⋅h), 6.30 mg/(L⋅h), and 6.62 mg/(L⋅h), respectively. Nitrogen balance analysis indicated that assimilation was the primary nitrogen metabolism pathway, with 79.20%-89.34% of inorganic nitrogen assimilated into biomass nitrogen and no significant total nitrogen (TN) loss. B403 exhibited high activity of key assimilation enzymes and maintained high nitrogen removal efficiency under nitrification-inhibiting conditions. The genome was annotated with 37 nitrogen metabolism-related genes, including assimilation and nitrate/nitrite reduction pathways, but lacked canonical denitrification gas-production genes. The proposed nitrogen metabolism pathway of B403 is: NH 4 + -N→ NH 2 OH → NO 2 - -N ↔ NO 3 - -N → NH 4 + -N → biomass nitrogen. Bioaugmentation of activated sludge with 5% (v/v) B403 under max 400 mg/L NH 4 + -N conditions raised mean removal efficiency from 82.33% to 92.53%, significantly reduced NO 3 - -N accumulation and increased sludge protein content. These findings indicate an assimilation-dominated nitrogen metabolism pathway of AHNR strain B403, enabling simultaneous liquid-phase inorganic nitrogen removal with biomass nitrogen accumulation, providing a promising strategy for the efficient treatment of nitrogen-rich wastewater.

title: Pulmonary toxicity of particulate-phase combustion byproducts from lithium-ion battery fires
abstract: The frequency of lithium-ion battery (LIB) fires is increasing globally, creating new challenges for firefighters and growing public safety concerns from smoke and intense heat. However, the health effects from exposure to LIB fires are not well understood. We collected soot and smoke particulate matter (PM) from LIB thermal runaway events (10 and 2 fire tests for soot and PM samples, respectively), filtered them to remove non-inhalable particles (>10 μm), analyzed for chemical composition and assessed for lung toxicity and pulmonary function in mice at 4 h and 24 h post exposure to 100 μg of the sample. Chemical and biological results were analyzed using a computational approach to identify hazardous chemical components that were potentially responsible for toxicity outcomes. Computational findings were further compared to those produced by other sources of air pollution. The soot sample contained more carbon species than the smoke PM sample (37% vs. 18%), whereas anions were higher in the PM sample (12% vs. 6%), and concentrations of inorganic elements were similar (23% vs. 28%). Fluoride particulate was found to account for up to 5% of the mass of each sample. Only soot significantly increased ventilatory timing and peak expiratory flow in mice and decreased relaxation time, while both samples caused significant increases in inflammatory responses. Soot and PM exhibited similar lung inflammatory outcomes relative to those caused by previously reported combustion-related air pollution sources. Computational analysis indicated that fluoride, Al, Fe, Ni, and Li from both samples were significantly associated with the lung toxicity responses (p < 0.05). The findings indicate that LIB fire soot and PM that contain hazardous metals and fluoride elicit pulmonary toxicity responses comparable to other sources of air pollution, increasing the need for awareness of potential strategies to mitigate public health impacts.

title: A dual-function hydrogel platform for Cu(II)/Fe(III) remediation and controlled nutrient release
abstract: The development of multifunctional materials that address multiple environmental challenges simultaneously represents a paradigm shift in sustainable water and soil management. This study presents a dual functional hydrogel consisting of urea-biochar encapsulated crosslinked hydrogel (U-BECA) designed for Cu(II)/Fe(III) removal and controlled nutrient release. The hydrogel was synthesized through calcium ion crosslinking of sodium alginate incorporating biochar and urea, characterized using FTIR, SEM, EDS, DMA, XRD and evaluated under single and binary metal ion systems. Results demonstrated effective adsorption with selectivity order Fe 3+ > Cu 2+ . The urea-loading strategy also exhibited sustained urea release over extended periods while maintaining metal ion adsorption capacity, offering integrated pollution remediation and nutrient delivery. The Fe 3+ and Cu 2+ adsorption respectively followed Langmuir and Sips model with theoretical adsorption capacities of 131.38 mg/g for Fe 3+ and 95.63 mg/g for Cu 2+ . Dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) confirmed the hydrogel's structural integrity, exhibiting a storage modulus of 319 kPa and no gel-to-sol transition, indicative of a mechanically stable and highly elastic network. SEM-EDS analysis revealed a dense, Ca 2+ -crosslinked microstructure that became rougher and enriched with particulate deposits following Cu 2+ and Fe 3+ adsorption. The persistence of characteristic metal peaks in the EDS spectra further confirmed successful metal uptake and retention within the hydrogel matrix. The effect of pH on urea release was evaluated, revealing pH-responsive release behavior. The Korsmeyer-Peppas model accurately described the release kinetics at pH 4 (n = 0.347), indicating a Fickian diffusion-controlled mechanism. The hydrogel also retained substantial adsorption capacity for both Cu 2+ and Fe 3+ over three consecutive adsorption-desorption cycles. These findings highlight hydrogel as a promising multifunctional material for integrated metal ion remediation and controlled nutrient delivery.

title: Associations of multiple ambient air pollutants and sleep apnea, sleep architecture and nocturnal oxygenation in adult patients with or without obstructive sleep apnea (OSA)
abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) affects an estimated 936 million adults worldwide, yet how environmental exposures relate to sleep architecture and nocturnal oxygenation remains unclear. We conducted a retrospective polysomnography-based study of 4049 adults in Shenzhen, China, to examine the relationships of ambient air pollutants, PM 2.5 inorganic components, and meteorological factors with OSA severity, sleep architecture, and nocturnal oxygenation. Lag 0-180 days was selected post hoc as the main reporting window. Within this window, PM 2.5 , PM 10 , NO 2 , SO 2 , CO, and diurnal temperature range (DTR) were all linked to greater OSA severity. Multiple pollutants were associated with lighter sleep; for example, PM 2.5 and PM 10 were associated with 1.71%TST and 1.32%TST increases in N1 sleep and 1.51%TST and 1.32%TST decreases in N3 sleep, respectively. O 3 and DTR showed the clearest adverse relationships with nocturnal oxygenation and sleep continuity. Non-linear analyses showed increasing exposure-response associations for PM 2.5 , SO 2 , and DTR, but a U-shaped association for O 3 . Interaction and mixture analyses further indicated meteorological modification and more consistent mixture relationships with altered sleep architecture than with categorical OSA severity. These findings highlight the importance of broader polysomnographic dimensions, cumulative exposure windows, and co-exposure patterns in future research.

title: Assessing sources of lead exposure in bearded vultures (Gypaetus barbatus) in the French Alps
abstract: The reduction of mortality is essential for the conservation of long-lived threatened bird species such as the bearded vulture (Gypaetus barbatus) and poisoning due to the ingestion of lead (Pb) ammunition used in hunting is among its main threats. In this study, we non-invasively assessed Pb exposure in the bearded vulture population of the French Alps by analyzing segments of flight feathers. Our aim was to determine the incidence of abnormal Pb exposure and examine its relationship with physiological stress, reflected by corticosterone levels in feathers. We also evaluated the contribution of Pb ammunition and diet, including soil ingestion, to Pb exposure in these birds, and examined its relationship with the Pb isotopic signature observed in birds, including some birds of prey found dead in the study area. The sequential analysis of flight feather segments allowed us to establish a monthly incidence of abnormal lead exposure of 3.3%. Corticosterone concentrations in flight feathers were not affected by Pb exposure. Regarding the contribution of different Pb sources, prey and soil contributed 0.021 and 0.016 mg/kg bw per day, respectively, whereas Pb ammunition particles ingested by scavengers when consuming shot prey frequently exceeded 100 mg. The isotopic signature of Pb ammunition is highly variable among manufacturers, but the discriminant analysis made it possible to associate Pb in the tissues of poisoned birds with the ingestion of Pb ammunition. Although the incidence of Pb exposure in bearded vultures is lower than in other scavenger birds in Europe, their conservation status underscores the need to reduce avoidable causes of mortality. In particular, Pb poisoning could be reduced by replacing Pb-based ammunition with non-toxic alternatives.

title: Functional divergence of biochar and nano-Fe3O4 in microbial chain elongation: Adsorptive regulation as an overlooked equilibrium driver
abstract: Microbial chain elongation (CE) offers a promising route for producing medium-chain carboxylic acids (MCFAs), but its performance is often limited by product accumulation and associated inhibition. Here, biochar was shown to enhance CE not only by improving initial performance but, more importantly, by sustaining MCFA production through adsorption-mediated regulation, in contrast to nano-Fe 3 O 4 . Notably, secondary biochar addition to steady-state fermentation broth reinitiated substrate consumption and led to additional butyrate production. Nano-Fe 3 O 4 , while achieving a higher initial caproate concentration (14.35 ± 0.86 g COD/L, 1.82-fold of the control) through enhanced electron transfer, did not further stimulate CE once steady state was reached. Adsorption analysis showed that biochar retained 2146.7 mg COD/L of caproate and 756.9 mg COD/L of butyrate, substantially lowering dissolved product concentrations. Thermodynamic evaluation revealed that this in situ adsorption reduced product activity and increased the driving force for chain elongation, thereby increasing the apparent thermodynamic driving force and sustaining MCFA formation under near-steady-state conditions. These findings highlight adsorption-mediated equilibrium regulation as a previously overlooked mechanism by which biochar prolongs CE performance.

title: Regenerable Cu2O/SiO2 for efficient methyl iodide capture: copper-vacancy-driven cleavage mechanism
abstract: Developing metal-based adsorbents capable of high-temperature methyl iodide (CH 3 I) capture and facile regeneration still poses a significant challenge. Herein, the micro-spherical cuprous oxide supported on silica (Cu 2 O/SiO 2 ) was synthesized for the investigation of CH 3 I adsorption behavior. The Cu 2 O/SiO 2 material showed a high adsorption capacity (1204 mg/g) for CH 3 I at 150 °C. After regeneration, the spent material retained over 90% of its initial capacity with its Cu 2 O structure preserved. Combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations, these results revealed that the underlying adsorption mechanism of CH 3 I onto Cu 2 O primarily involved the cleavage of CH 3 I facilitated by the readily formed copper vacancies in the Cu 2 O lattice, ultimately leading to the formation of CuI. This work provided a facile regeneration strategy applicable to a wide range of iodine adsorbents for radioactive CH 3 I capture.

title: Acute autonomic and cardiovascular responses to walking in natural versus urban environments: A systematic review and three-level meta-analysis
abstract: Acute physiological responses to walking in natural versus urban environments remain uncertain. We reviewed studies of healthy adults completing single walks in actual outdoor settings. Six databases were searched through January 12, 2026, and reporting followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses framework. We included 21 studies; 20 contributed 57 effect estimates to a three-level meta-analysis. Pooled Hedges' g estimates with 95% confidence intervals were -0.01 [-0.26, 0.23] for heart rate (p = 0.90), 0.11 [-0.40, 0.62] for systolic blood pressure (p = 0.63), and -0.14 [-0.36, 0.08] for diastolic blood pressure (p = 0.18). Evidence was inconclusive for high frequency heart rate variability (g = -0.14 [-0.94, 0.66], p = 0.66) and the root mean square of successive differences between normal interbeat intervals (g = -0.01 [-0.89, 0.87], p = 0.98), with few estimates and wide intervals. Exploratory analyses found no clear moderating associations with walking duration or study sample sex composition, although small subgroups limited precision. Overall, current evidence does not show a consistent additional acute physiological response to natural walking. This does not establish equivalence or rule out true differences. Estimates reflect heterogeneous routes and protocols and cannot isolate a uniform causal effect of nature exposure. Psychological restoration, sustained physical activity, disease prevention, and clinical outcomes require separate evidence. Future studies should better characterize environmental exposures and standardize walking and measurement procedures.

title: Landscape fire-sourced PM2.5 and kidney function in children: evidence from a national cross-sectional study in China
abstract: Introduction Landscape fire-sourced fine particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter ≤2.5 μm (PM 2.5 ) may be more oxidatively active and biologically toxic than PM 2.5 from other sources, but evidence of its kidney effects in children is limited. Objectives To examine the association between landscape fire-sourced PM 2.5 exposure and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in children and identify potentially susceptible subgroups. Methods This cross-sectional study included 12,102 children aged 5-18 years who participated in the China National Nutrition and Health Surveillance of Children and Lactating Women between October 2016 and December 2018. eGFR was estimated from serum creatinine (Scr), and three-year average pre-survey exposure to landscape fire-sourced PM 2.5 was assigned using school addresses. Associations were estimated using linear mixed-effects models, with subgroup analyses by sex, obesity, NDVI, and nutrient intake. Results The mean age was 10.90 ± 3.12 years, and 6064 participants (50.11%) were boys. Each IQR (0.505 μg/m 3 ) increase in landscape fire-sourced PM 2.5 was associated with a 0.83 mL/min/1.73 m 2 reduction in eGFR (95% CI: -1.03, -0.62). The association was stronger among middle school students (β = -1.46 mL/min/1.73 m 2 ; 95% CI: -1.83, -1.09) than among primary school students (β = -0.59 mL/min/1.73 m 2 ; 95% CI: -0.84, -0.34; P for difference for difference Conclusions Landscape fire-sourced PM 2.5 exposure was associated with lower eGFR in the overall population, with stronger associations among middle school students and children with lower NDVI or lower vitamin or carbohydrate intake.

title: Harnessing triple-strategy synergy of bimetallic Cu/Ni sites, interfacial coupling and S-scheme charge transfer in ZIF-8/BiOBr for enhanced photocatalytic dye remediation
abstract: The structural complexity and inherent stability of dyes in wastewater have driven research toward replacing conventional, less effective treatment methods with advanced technologies. In this study, a novel Cu-Ni@ZIF-8/BiOBr (CNZ/BOB) S-scheme heterojunction was synthesized by combining Cu-Ni bimetal-doped ZIF-8 (CNZ) nanomaterial with BiOBr (BOB) using a simple co-precipitation method. The as-synthesized heterojunction demonstrated excellent photocatalytic degradation capabilities for both Congo Red and Malachite Green, achieving efficiencies of 96.5% and 93.9%, respectively within 70 min of light irradiation. The CNZ/BOB composite significantly outperformed pristine ZIF-8 (2.4 and 2.5 times better) and BOB (3 and 3.2 times better) in degrading these toxic organic dyes. Detailed investigations and experimental results confirmed the improved photodegradation activity after incorporation of Cu and Ni dopants, which facilitated dual active sites, strong interfacial contact, and an S-scheme charge transfer pathway between CNZ and BOB. FE-SEM analysis showed a well-organized, flower-like stacked topology of the heterostructure, while XRD spectra confirmed its crystalline structure. UV-DRS analysis further demonstrated that heterostructure formation extended light absorption into the visible region and narrowed the bandgap of the composite to 2.56 eV. Furthermore, activity was observed over five consecutive cycles in reusability tests, demonstrating its robust structural and operational stability. Thus, these results confirm that the CNZ/BOB nanocomposite is a robust, effective, and reusable photocatalyst for visible-light-driven wastewater treatment.

title: Sulfur speciation and phase redistribution during hydrothermal treatment of municipal sludge: Implications for regional recovery potential
abstract: Sulfur transformation during hydrothermal treatment of sewage sludge affects H 2 S emissions, aqueous sulfur loading, and the safe utilization of solid products. This study integrated sulfur speciation analysis and phase-resolved sulfur accounting to investigate sulfur transformation, multiphase partitioning, and resource recovery potential during the hydrothermal treatment of municipal sewage sludge. Hydrothermal severity, characterized by temperature and pressure, promoted organosulfur conversion and H 2 S formation, whereas the liquid-to-solid ratio primarily regulated sulfur partitioning between the liquid and solid phases. Under the representative condition of 250 °C for 120 min at a liquid-to-solid ratio of 10 mL g -1 , 43.95% of the initial sulfur was retained in the solid phase, 25.50% was detected in the filtered aqueous phase, and 3.36% was quantified as measured gaseous H 2 S-S. Meanwhile, solid-phase sulfur shifted from aliphatic and aromatic forms toward sulfate- and sulfide-like species, indicating that hydrothermal treatment primarily induced sulfur transformation and multiphase redistribution rather than simple sulfur removal. he national dry sludge inventory was projected to reach approximately 14.91 Mt yr -1 in 2030. Under the baseline scenario, theoretical recoverable sulfur from captured H 2 S-S was spatially concentrated in regions with larger sludge inventories, while its estimated magnitude was strongly influenced by sludge sulfur content, the H 2 S-S conversion fraction, and sludge production. These findings provide an experimentally constrained basis for coordinating H 2 S emission control, downstream sulfur management, and region-specific sulfur recovery strategies.

title: CaO/MgO nanoparticle-modified diatomite for co-retention of carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus and mitigation of nutrient leaching from soil
abstract: Excessive accumulation of dissolved organic carbon (DOC), dissolved nitrogen (DN), and dissolved phosphorus (DP) in citrus orchard soils may increase the risk of agricultural non-point source pollution. The simultaneous and efficient retention of these dissolved nutrients in complex multi-solute systems, such as lemon waste fermentation broth (LWFB), remains a significant challenge, and the retention behavior of modified materials under such conditions is still poorly understood. Herein, a modified diatomite composite incorporating in situ loaded CaO/MgO nanoparticles (CMNPs@AD) was successfully synthesized via a facile acid-base activation strategy combined with an equal-volume impregnation method to investigate its nutrient retention performance and underlying mechanisms in LWFB. The results showed that CMNPs@AD featured a mesoporous structure decorated with uniformly dispersed metal nanoparticles. In the Langmuir isotherm model, the theoretical maximum retention capacities of CMNPs@AD for DOC, DN, and DP were 22.39, 45.02, and 25.49 mg/g, respectively. Advanced characterization techniques and density functional theory revealed that the nutrient retention mechanism of CMNPs@AD involves multiple physicochemical processes. Soil column leaching experiments showed that, compared with the fertilization group, the application of 1.0 wt% CMNPs@AD significantly reduced DOC, DN, and DP leaching while increasing soil sucrase, urease, and neutral phosphatase activities. The nutrient-laden CMNPs@AD (CMNPs@AD-CNP) significantly improved seed germination performance. Moreover, pot experiments demonstrated that plants grown in the post-leaching T2 soil showed enhanced growth and biomass accumulation and higher chlorophyll content than those in the other treatments. This study developed a novel and cost-effective soil additive that effectively reduced the co-leaching losses of dissolved soil nutrients, providing a promising material-based strategy for mitigating nutrient leaching from soil.

title: Exploring “equigenesis” in the association between the natural outdoor environment, mental health and death by suicide before and during the COVID-19 pandemic: a population-based cohort study of more than 2 million records in Northern Ireland
abstract: : Recent evidence suggests that the natural outdoor environment (NOE) may mitigate socioeconomic inequalities in mental health, but it remains unclear how such associations vary between the pandemic and the non-pandemic period. Therefore, this study focused on the association between NOE and inequalities in mental health before and during the pandemic. We used a population-based cohort of individuals in Northern Ireland (NI), including more than 2 million General Practice participants from 2017 to 2022. NOE was assessed using the proportion of blue space and green space within the administrative neighbourhoods, respectively. Mental health outcomes included death by suicide, mental health-related hospital admissions and prescriptions. We applied multilevel Cox proportional hazards and logistic regressions. Further, we stratified the analysis by area-level deprivation index. The analyses were performed for the pre-pandemic (2017-2019) and during the pandemic (2020-2022), respectively. People living in neighbourhoods with a higher proportion of NOE (e.g., 4 th quintile of blue space) had lower odds of being in receipt of mental-health-related prescriptions (e.g., pre-pandemic: OR=0.835, 95% CI=0.796-0.874; intra-pandemic: OR=0.802, 95% CI=0.763-0.844) and a lower risk of dying by suicide (e.g., pre-pandemic: HR=0.634, 95% CI=0.451-0.890; intra-pandemic: HR=0.684, 95% CI=0.469-0.998). However, there is no evidence that NOE is related to a lower risk of having a mental health-related hospital admission (e.g., pre-pandemic: OR=1.053, 95% CI=0.794-1.396; intra-pandemic: OR=1.044, 95% CI=0.778-1.401). The association between NOE and mental health-related hospital admissions, as well as the association between NOE and prescriptions, was more pronounced in socioeconomically disadvantaged neighbourhoods, especially during the pandemic. However, such “equigenesis” was only observed for death by suicide before the pandemic. Therefore, NOE may mitigate socioeconomic inequalities in mental health, especially during the pandemic. Our findings demonstrate the importance of sufficient NOE to support better and more equal mental health and preparedness for future pandemics.

title: Intracity-scale study reveals spatiotemporal variation of urban airborne microbiota and dynamics of antibiotic resistance/virulence genes
abstract: Airborne microbiota are critical to urban air quality and public health, yet their spatiotemporal differentiation, community assembly, and profiles of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and virulence factor genes (VFGs) across urban functional zones remain poorly characterized. In this study, monthly 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing was combined with seasonal metagenomic profiling of 12 composite samples and environmental data to investigate airborne microbiota at three sites representing commercial, industrial, and recreational zones in Changsha, China. Airborne communities showed similar spatial patterns among the investigated functional zones but strong seasonal variation, with Shannon diversity below 2.0 in July and above 6.0 in January. Proteobacteria dominated most samples, while key seasonal taxa shifted among Delftia, Cupriavidus, and Achromobacter. Neutral community modeling supported stochastic dominance (R 2 = 0.664, Nm = 1200), with 92.6% of operational taxonomic units within the 95% confidence interval. However, βNTI and RCbray analyses indicated increased deterministic selection in autumn-winter, coinciding with high pressure and pollutant accumulation. Metagenomics identified 25 ARG, 14 VFG, and 6 mobile genetic element (MGE) categories, with season explaining 53.9% of VFG compositional differences. Exploratory structural equation modeling identified associations between MGE abundance and ARG/VFG abundances (β = 0.75 and 1.09, respectively; both P < 0.001). Binning and contig co-localization showed that ARG-VFG-MGE co-harboring fragments were potentially affiliated with opportunistic pathogens such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Klebsiella pneumoniae, indicating potential biosafety concerns. These findings identify season as a key driver of urban airborne microbiota and genetic risk factors, providing a basis for atmospheric biosafety monitoring and assessment.

title: A new risk to food security: Co-transport, accumulation, and deterioration of nutritional quality mediated by surface charge of nanoplastics and flame retardants in the soil-crop system
abstract: The pervasive coexistence of nanoplastics (NPs) and organophosphorus flame retardants (OPFRs) in agro-ecosystems poses direct threats to food security and environmental sustainability, yet the underlying synergistic toxicities remain largely unknown. This study explores how surface-charge properties may mediate the combined toxicity of carboxylated (PS-COOH) and aminated (PS-NH 2 ) polystyrene NPs with the OPFR triethyl phosphate (TEP) in rye. Through integrated short-term hydroponics and full-life-cycle soil cultivation coupled with multi-dimensional analyses, we demonstrate that positively charged PS-NH 2 exerts significantly greater toxicity than PS-COOH. Mechanistically, our results suggest that TEP may promote the formation of NP-containing complexes via van der Waals-type interactions, potentially serving as a carrier to enhance root uptake and translocation of PS-NH 2 into grains. This synergistic-like response triggered severe oxidative stress (H 2 O 2 levels 10-fold higher than control), disrupted metabolic homeostasis, and altered the rhizosphere microbiome, with elevated relative abundances of taxa such as Comamonadaceae under TEP-containing treatments. Transcriptomics revealed specific activation of phenylpropanoid biosynthesis and repression of ion transport and energy metabolism pathways. Consequently, the PS-NH 2 + TEP co-exposure delayed heading by 22 days, reduced 1000-grain weight by 28.89%, slashed grain crude fat by 55.58%, and increased indigestible fiber by 62.67%. These findings underscore that NP surface charge is a critical determinant of phytotoxicity. The resultant cascade of physiological disruptions may compromise crop yield and nutritional integrity, creating plausible entry points for contaminants into the food chain and ultimately raising concerns for global food security and ecosystem resilience.

title: Structure–function-guided upcycling of mineral industrial wastes: Compositional pathways, materials design and sustainability constraints
abstract: Mineral industrial wastes represent a critical bottleneck in the global transition toward carbon neutrality and a circular economy. Conventional recycling paradigms predominantly rely on low-value bulk consumption in the construction sector, treating wastes as inert fillers. To transcend this, we conducted a systematic literature review using Web of Science and Scopus (2015-2026) to construct a qualitative structure-function-guided framework for waste upcycling. This framework evaluates upcycling efficacy based on active-component utilization, structural designability, and functional output. We categorize these wastes into three prototypical, albeit sometimes overlapping, systems-Ca-Si-rich, Al-Si-rich, and Fe/Ti-enriched wastes-and elucidate their divergent thermodynamic and structural evolutionary pathways toward structural, porous, and magnetic/catalytic materials. Furthermore, we distill the driving mechanisms of functionalization, emphasizing phase engineering, multiscale architectural reconstruction, and defect/interfacial modulation. Finally, we critically assess the sustainability constraints and boundaries of current "high-value" claims, identifying critical limitations in the existing literature, including high energy and chemical consumption, contaminant leaching risks, scale-up barriers, and market capacity.

title: Asynchronous functional recovery and structural reconfiguration of water-sediment networks in an actively restored lake
abstract: Internal nutrient loading often constrain the recovery of shallow eutrophic urban lakes. While temporal lags between water and sediment recovery are recognized, how active restoration reshapes their structural relationships remains poorly understood. We conducted a one-year in situ restoration experiment in Nanhu Lake (Wuhan, China) using 6 ha-scale ecological enclosures (two replicate enclosures per treatment) to evaluate a gradient of restoration treatments: a baseline ecological restoration (ER; submerged macrophytes (Vallisneria natans), microbial flocculants, and algaecides), phosphorus retention treatment (PR; ER + lanthanum-modified bentonite), and nitrogen-phosphorus reduction treatment (NPR; PR + high-efficiency nitrogen removal materials). Compared with the same season before restoration, water-column conditions changed rapidly across all treatments, with significantly higher dissolved oxygen and lower total phosphorus and chemical oxygen demand, although chlorophyll a and NH 4 + -N also increased. In contrast, sediment responses lagged behind those of the water column. While most sediment physicochemical parameters remained unchanged after one year, sediment phosphorus-binding capacity increased, whereas total nitrogen and the potential DNRA rate decreased. No significant overall differences among the three restoration treatments were detected across the full sampling period. Furthermore, ecological network analysis identified fewer cross-compartment associations after restoration, suggesting reduced coordination between water-column and sediment dynamics, while water-column total nitrogen retained the highest closeness centrality in both periods. These findings highlight asynchronous water-sediment responses during the first year of restoration and support a phased management perspective that accounts for rapid water-column responses alongside slower sediment adjustment.

title: A review of integrated control of volatile fatty acids and downstream nitrogen removal during anaerobic treatment of pharmaceutical wastewater: carbon–nitrogen–sulfur interactions and process optimization
abstract: During the anaerobic treatment of pharmaceutical wastewater, the mineralization of organic nitrogen and sulfate reduction lead to the continuous production of volatile fatty acids (VFAs) and ammonia. Factors such as pH, alkalinity, free ammonia, undissociated VFAs, salinity, sulfide, electron donor competition, and pharmaceutical toxicity can adversely affect reactor stability and reduce nitrogen removal efficiency. This study examines the inhibitory effects of VFA accumulation, ammonium release and sulfur transformation, and proposes targeted control strategies involving hybrid reactors, conductive material addition, supplementation of trace elements, source separation, selective oxidation and sulfide control. A step-by-step selection approach is employed to identify an appropriate post-anaerobic nitrogen removal process based on the stability of anaerobic biodegradation, the presence of inhibitors, nitrogen species, electron acceptor supply, alkalinity balance, and carbon source reserves. Partial nitritation-anammox (PN/A) is suitable for ammonium-rich wastewater with low biodegradable carbon and acceptable toxicity; partial denitrification-anammox (PD/A) needs a stable nitrate source and adjustable VFA supply; and sulfur-driven partial denitrification produces nitrite when the sulfide is below the inhibition threshold. If elevated VFA concentrations are accompanied by propionate accumulation, alkalinity consumption, methane yield decline, or sulfide toxicity, anaerobic stability should be restored prior to autotrophic nitrogen removal. This is a process-oriented C-N-S framework for designing combined anaerobic-nitrogen removal systems treating high-strength pharmaceutical wastewater.

title: A mysterious danger for kidney disease exacerbations: short-term impacts of ultrafine particles on hospital visits
abstract: Ultrafine particles (UFPs) are more toxic than fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) but are generally ignored. Limited health research existed on UFPs, especially for kidney diseases. We investigated if UFPs could increase kidney-disease related hospital emergency department (ED) visits. Time-stratified case-crossover design was used for evaluating the short-term impacts of UFP. Daily exposure to UFPs was assessed by a previously validated chemical transport model. ED visits with principal diagnosis of kidney diseases, geocoded at street level, from 2013 to 2018, were obtained from New York State hospital discharge database covering 95% of all hospitals. Conditional logistic regression was used to estimate the excess risks (%ER) for every inter-quartile range (IQR) change (ER IQR ). Among 269,945 ED visits, increasing kidney-disease ED visits were associated with UFPs on individual lag 1 day and all cumulative lag days (lag 0-1 to lag 0-6). The ER of ED visits peaked on lag 0-3 days (ER IQR = 0.74, 95% confidence interval: 0.28, 1.20). Stronger associations were found among non-African American, older adults (>65 yrs), during days with high temperatures, low humidity, and fall/winter season. Our findings suggested the kidney toxicity of UFPs and suggest that routine measures should be taken to monitor UFP concentration and control its emission.

title: Upcycling coal gasification fine slag into an efficient denitration catalyst by using MnCeOx composite oxides
abstract: Realizing the high-value applications of coal gasification fine slag (CGFS) remains a key scientific challenge in the industrial solid waste resource recovery sector. To address this challenge, an ingenious "acid leaching-metal loading" approach was developed to construct an efficient catalytic interface, thereby achieving efficient nitrogen oxide removal. Catalytic performance evaluation indicated that the MnCeO x composites modified fine slag catalyst (MnCe-AFS) achieved 93% NO conversion at 125 °C. Acid leaching increased fine slag surface roughness, thereby ensuring the homogeneous distribution of active metals. The formed Mn-O-Ce interfaces served as the core for the enhanced catalytic activity. By facilitating interfacial electron transfer (such as the Mn 3+ /Mn 4+ and Ce 3+ /Ce 4+ cycles), activating oxygen species, and optimizing acidic sites, it significantly improved the efficiency of the selective catalytic reduction reaction. Transient response experiments indicated possible reaction pathways on MnCe-AFS. This work provides a novel route for the high-value conversion of industrial solid waste in the field of catalysis.

title: Life-history strategies of soil microorganisms and their interactions with plant diversity: a review
abstract: Faced with the global challenges of biodiversity loss and soil function degradation across ecosystems, deciphering the synergistic mechanisms between soil microorganisms and plant diversity is essential for supporting ecological restoration and sustainable development. This study reviews the evolutionary progression of microbial life-history strategies, from the r-K dichotomy to the CSR/CSO and YAS frameworks, and onward to multidimensional modern frameworks, revealing their central role in driving microbial ecological adaptation. Focusing on the evolution and drivers of microbial life-history strategies, this work synthesizes plant-microbe interactions in grassland ecosystems, which are globally extensive, highly responsive to management and climate, and central to restoration practice. Evidence from forests and croplands is used only where it clarifies a general mechanism or its boundary of applicability. It further addresses these relationships within grassland ecosystems, elucidating the coevolutionary dynamics between plants and microorganisms and the divergent microbial life-history strategies shaped by dominant plant functional groups including grasses and legumes. This review synthesizes current evidence linking microbial life-history strategies with plant diversity and functional-group composition in grasslands. It discusses how plant inputs, soil resource availability, environmental stress, and management practices may shape microbial traits and plant-microbe interactions. By distinguishing experimentally supported mechanisms from observational associations and conceptual hypotheses, this review identifies potential applications in grassland restoration and highlights the methodological limitations that must be addressed before microbial life-history strategies can be used as operational indicators of restoration outcomes.

title: Aeration-free microalgal-bacterial granular sludge for simultaneous nitrification, denitrification and phosphorus removal: Rapid start-up and functional differentiation
abstract: The simultaneous nitrification, denitrification, and phosphorus removal (SNDPR) process based on aeration-free microalgal-bacterial granular sludge (MBGS) offers a promising pathway for sustainable wastewater treatment, but suffers from prolonged and unstable start-up. In this study, we co-inoculated aerobic granular sludge (AGS) capable of SNDPR with pre-cultivated MBGS to achieve rapid start-up of the aeration-free MBGS-SNDPR process in a photo-sequencing batch reactor. This strategy maintained a stable biomass concentration, improved physicochemical properties of the granules, and achieved efficient removal of COD (88.3% ± 3.6%), NH 4 + -N (99.2% ± 0.7%), total nitrogen (TN, 85.2% ± 6.3%), and PO 4 3- -P (90.5% ± 7.4%) throughout 100 days of reactor operation. Two morphologically and functionally distinct MBGS types that evolved from the AGS inoculum were identified: MBGS-S originated from small AGS ( 1 mm) colonized by phototrophs. MBGS-S was dominated by nitrification and phosphorus removal, whereas MBGS-L was dominated by denitrification.
