Typical cycle tests and mass balance calculations demonstrated that the reactor achieved efficient SNDPR performance, produced less net CO 2 production than activated sludge, and retained phosphorus in harvested biomass as a potential recovery pool. Microbial community analysis further indicated that SNDPR-related functional microorganisms persisted and abundances of key functional genes increased throughout the operation, thereby ensuring stable and efficient pollutant removal. Overall, this study provides insights into strategies for the rapid start-up of the aeration-free MBGS-SNDPR process and for the successful integration of functional microorganisms into this sustainable process.

title: Dual-Pathway Peroxymonosulfate Activation on FeNi-CNT@Al2O3 for Efficient Tetracycline Hydrochloride Degradation
abstract: Transition metal alloy catalysts are promising for advanced oxidation processes, but their application is often limited by insufficient interfacial electron transfer and poor stability. Herein, we engineered a robust FeNi-CNT@Al 2 O 3 catalyst, derived from waste aluminum ash, for the activation of peroxymonosulfate (PMS) and tetracycline hydrochloride (TCH) degradation. The catalyst features nitrogen-doped carbon nanotubes (CNTs) with encapsulated Fe-Ni alloy nanoparticles grown on an alumina-rich carbon matrix, creating an efficient interfacial catalytic platform through the synergy between CNT-mediated electron transfer and Fe-Ni-enhanced redox cycling. The optimized Fe 1 Ni 2 -CNT@Al 2 O 3 /PMS system achieved 100% TCH degradation with 73.5% chemical oxygen demand (COD) and 69.3% total organic carbon (TOC) removal within 30 min. Mechanistic investigations revealed that the degradation is dominated by a non-radical 1 O 2 pathway, with radical species ( and ) and direct electron transfer as secondary contributors. Density functional theory calculations further elucidated the critical role of Fe-Ni alloy loading in enhancing interfacial PMS adsorption and charge transfer. Notably, the catalyst maintained 91.8% TCH removal after 100 h of continuous operation. This work provides a sustainable strategy for upcycling solid waste into high-performance catalysts and elucidates the mechanism of 1 O 2 -dominated PMS activation for persistent organic pollutant remediation.

title: Alleviation of ammonia inhibition associated with enhanced quorum sensing signaling system under trace elements supplementation during biomethanation
abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) represents a mature and extensively adopted technique to dispose organic waste, yet ammonia toxicity remains a major bottleneck for stable AD operation. For activating methanogenesis-related enzymes, regulating the microbial community structure, and optimizing the reaction efficiency of AD process, supplementation of trace elements has been validated as an effective approach to counteract ammonia inhibition. However, mechanisms of how different trace elements modulate the biosynthesis and release of N-acyl homoserine lactones (AHLs), as well as the subsequent relieving ammonia inhibition are still unknown. Therefore, the current study investigated the effects of different trace elements on the secretion of AHLs under ammonia stress. The results showed that optimal concentrations of Fe, Co and Ni could enhance the secretion of AHLs, mainly N-butyryl- DL -homoserine lactone (C4-HSL) and N-hexanoyl- L -homoserine lactone (C6-HSL), and adjust microbial social behaviors under high ammonia levels. In addition, microbial community changes (enriched Bacteroidetes_vadinHA17, Syntrophomonas and Methanosarcina) were closely associated with increased methane production and stimulated AHLs accumulation by trace elements. Furthermore, increased AHLs signals correlated with intercellular communication could regulate critical genes transcription (glk, pgk, and yhdR) and enzymes synthesis (glucokinase, acetate kinase, and Coenzyme-B sulfoethylthiotransferase) to alleviate ammonia inhibition during the whole AD process. Trace elements could serve for multiple enzymes, which could be beneficial for AHL secreting hydrolytic-acidogenic consortia. The current study could provide primary insights for applying trace elements to relieve ammonia stress via AHLs regulation.

title: Scale-dependent associations between land use and dissolved organic matter in the mainstem and tributaries of the Three Gorges Reservoir region
abstract: The spatial patterns of dissolved organic matter (DOM) in the Three Gorges Reservoir (TGR) are highly heterogeneous, yet how land use regulates these patterns across different spatial scales remains poorly understood. In this study, we characterized DOM composition and optical properties in the mainstem and representative tributaries of the TGR. After rigorous False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction, most bulk DOM optical properties did not show statistically significant differences between the two systems, suggesting a macroscopic homogenization. Model selection based on the Akaike Information Criterion corrected for small sample sizes (AICc), however, revealed distinct scale-dependent associations: the mainstem DOM was optimally explained by broader-scale land use (500 m buffer), whereas the tributary DOM was highly sensitive to local-scale land use (100 m buffer). In the tributaries, agricultural runoff strongly enhanced DOM aromaticity, whereas urban impervious surfaces reduced it. This macroscopic homogenization is likely driven by the massive water volume and longer hydraulic retention time of the mainstem, which buffer and dilute these localized inputs. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that hydrological mixing drives macroscopic homogenization while land-use control remains highly scale-dependent. This dual perspective provides a scientific basis for developing zone-specific pollution control measures tailored to different spatial scales in the TGR region.

title: Preferential adsorption of perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids with different chain lengths via hydrophilic-hydrophobic interface regulation
abstract: Recently, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) pollution has gradually shifted from a pattern dominated by traditional long-chain PFAS to a more complex situation where both short-chain and long-chain PFAS coexist. This poses significant challenges to conventional adsorbents such as activated carbon (AC) and ion exchange resins, whose adsorption performance is strongly influenced by PFAS chain length, adsorbent surface chemistry, and multiple interactions. Herein, we designed and prepared aminated polyurethane (PU) sponge materials by introducing alkylamines with different carbon-chain lengths, denoted as PPU-C 2 , PPU-C 6 , and PPU-C 14 according to the carbon-chain lengths of the grafted alkylamines, thereby constructing interfaces with progressively tuned hydrophilic-hydrophobic characteristics. The resulting material exhibited chain-length-dependent adsorption preferences toward perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acid (PFCA) of different chain lengths. Specifically, PPU-C 2 achieved a removal efficiency of 72% for ultra-short-chain trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) with a maximum adsorption capacity of 596 mg g -1 , whereas PPU-C 6 exhibited the highest adsorption capacity toward perfluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA) (829.2 mg g -1 ) with a removal efficiency of 89%. In contrast, PPU-C 14 showed superior affinity toward long-chain perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA), achieving a removal efficiency of 96% and a maximum adsorption capacity of 848.2 mg g -1 . Experimental and theoretical results supported a chain-length-dependent matching relationship between PFCA molecular structure and local interfacial polarity. Appreciable PFCA adsorption performance was also retained in natural water samples. The material also exhibited good reusability. This study highlights the role of interfacial hydrophilic-hydrophobic regulation in governing chain-length-dependent PFCA adsorption and provides a basis for designing adsorbents with tunable affinity toward PFCA of different chain lengths.

title: Green-Synthesized Nanoparticles for Sensing: From Molecular Mechanisms to Next-Generation Sensing Platforms
abstract: Green synthesis has emerged as a sustainable and mechanistically versatile strategy for fabricating nanomaterials with tunable physicochemical and interfacial properties for advanced sensing applications. Unlike conventional synthesis routes that depend on toxic chemicals, harsh reaction conditions, and post-synthetic functionalization, green synthesis integrates nanoparticle formation, stabilization, defect generation, and surface engineering within a biomolecule-rich environment. Biological entities such as plant extracts, microorganisms, proteins, polysaccharides, flavonoids, and polyphenols act as reducing and capping agents, producing intrinsically functionalized nanostructures with enhanced biocompatibility and sensing performance. Recent studies demonstrate that biomolecule-mediated synthesis strongly influences nucleation kinetics, morphology evolution, defect chemistry, electronic structure, plasmonic behaviour, and interfacial charge transfer, which collectively govern sensitivity, selectivity, and signal amplification in sensing systems. This Review critically discusses the mechanistic foundations of green nanoparticle synthesis and their use in electrochemical, fluorescence, colorimetric, SERS, and photoelectrochemical sensing platforms. Emphasis is placed on morphology engineering, defect-mediated electronic modulation, biomolecular corona formation, heterojunction design, and nano-bio interface engineering. Current challenges related to reproducibility, scalability, and mechanistic understanding are also highlighted, alongside future opportunities involving AI-assisted synthesis optimization and sustainable next-generation sensing architectures.

title: Rainfall–runoff duration shapes divergent water quality and microbial assembly patterns in a drinking water reservoir
abstract: Under climate change, the frequency of extreme rainfall events is increasing. However, how rainfall-runoff duration shapes water quality dynamics and microbial ecological processes in drinking water reservoirs remains poorly understood. Using Jinpen Reservoir as a case study, this study investigated ecological responses to contrasting short- and long-duration rainfall-runoff events by integrating water quality monitoring, microbial community analysis, community assembly assessment, and functional potential prediction. Short-duration rainfall-runoff resulted in rapid pulse inputs of allochthonous nutrients and organic matter, leading to transient deterioration of water quality. In contrast, long-duration continuous rainfall-runoff promoted enhanced water renewal and vertical mixing, coinciding with improved water quality conditions during the later stage of the event. Microbial communities exhibited distinct response patterns under contrasting rainfall-runoff regimes. Short-duration rainfall-runoff induced transient microbial community fluctuations and maintained higher community evenness, whereas long-duration rainfall-runoff was linked to persistent microbial community reorganization, altered microbial association networks, increased community richness, a higher proportion of specialist taxa, and stronger environmental filtering signals. Redundancy analysis (RDA) and Mantel tests revealed that nitrogen, phosphorus, dissolved organic carbon (DOC), CODMn, and turbidity were key environmental factors associated with microbial community variation. PICRUSt2-based functional prediction further indicated that long-duration rainfall-runoff was linked to enhanced predicted microbial functional potential, particularly for nitrogen cycling-related functional pathways. Overall, this study reveals that rainfall-runoff events with different durations correspond to distinct ecological response modes, with prolonged disturbances associated with stronger environmental coupling and microbial community reorganization. These findings advance our understanding of reservoir microbial responses under changing precipitation regimes and provide scientific insights for adaptive management of drinking water reservoirs under climate change.

title: Seasonal divergence and long-term dynamics of dissolved organic carbon concentration and storage in the open-water regions of Lake Taihu from 2000 to 2024
abstract: Concentration-based assessments may overlook changes in dissolved organic carbon (DOC) inventory when lake water volume varies seasonally. Here, we combined MODIS observations, an XGBoost retrieval model, and lake water storage (WSC) to reconstruct DOC concentration (DOCc) and DOC storage (DOCs) over 100 consecutive seasons from spring 2000 to winter 2024 across the analyzed open-water domain of Lake Taihu. The model was developed from 411 satellite-in situ matchups and achieved an R 2 of 0.69 and an RMSE of 0.61 mg/L on the held-out validation dataset. DOCc exhibited a distinct bimodal seasonal cycle, with higher values in spring and autumn and lower values in summer and winter, whereas DOCs remained relatively high from spring through autumn and declined markedly in winter. Log-scale accounting partitioned DOCs variability into DOCc (44.7%) and WSC (56.0%) variance terms, together with a -2.1% covariance term and a 1.4% residual, showing that the DOCc and WSC terms were of comparable magnitude. Long-term changes were also season dependent: DOCc showed net declines from 2000 to 2024 in spring and summer but no robust monotonic trend in any season, whereas autumn DOCs showed the clearest positive long-term tendency in the baseline analysis, with a slope of 121.55 t C/yr. The runoff proxy also covaried consistently with WSC in spring and winter. Overall, DOCc and DOCs captured complementary but non-equivalent aspects of lake carbon dynamics, demonstrating that seasonal water-volume variability is integral to DOC inventory estimates and can yield patterns not evident from concentration alone.

title: Mineral triboelectricity as an electron source for microbial autotrophy: implications for carbon and nitrogen cycling in energy-limited environments
abstract: Triboelectrification converts mechanical contact and separation into interfacial charge, yet whether mineral-derived triboelectric electrons can sustain microbial growth and metabolism remains unclear. Here, we report a mechanically powered autotrophic pathway in which mineral-mediated triboelectrification converts mechanical energy into an extracellular electron supply. Within the α-Fe 2 O 3 -Rhodopseudomonas palustris biohybrid, triboelectrically generated electrons were routed through cell-envelope redox conduits into respiratory metabolism, thereby converting interfacial charge into cellular energy and reducing power. This bioenergetic conversion coupled inorganic carbon fixation to nitrate respiration, sustaining autotrophic growth and lycopene biosynthesis in the dark without conventional chemical electron donors. Its compatibility with distinct mechanical inputs, electroactive microorganisms, and terminal electron acceptors demonstrates the broad adaptability of this energy-coupling pathway, whereas mineral-dependent performance identifies interfacial charge generation as an important control on microbial electron supply. These findings identify mineral-solid triboelectric contact as a distinct interfacial route linking mechanical energy to microbial carbon and nitrogen transformations, highlighting its potential relevance to biogeochemical processes in energy-limited environments.

title: Decoding dissolved organic matter reorganization and multitrophic regulation of biogeochemical cycling in effluent-dominated hyporheic sediments
abstract: Continuous wastewater effluent discharge sustains pronounced redox heterogeneity in the hyporheic zone (HZ), with consequences for dissolved organic matter (DOM) transformation and sediment biogeochemistry. However, the ecological pathways linking redox-dependent DOM transformation to multitrophic organization and coupled nitrogen (N) and sulfur (S) cycling remain poorly understood. We integrated fluorescence and molecular DOM characterization, bacterial and eukaryotic community profiling, metagenomics, ecological network analysis, and structural equation modeling across oxic and anoxic zones. The summed relative contribution of protein-like fluorescence did not differ significantly between zones, while tyrosine-like fluorescence was 31% higher in the oxic zone and the median tryptophan/tyrosine ratio was 52% higher under anoxia. FT-ICR MS analysis showed that formulas positively associated with HIX had higher O/C ratios and a median NOSC of 0.35, whereas negatively associated formulas had a median NOSC of -0.90, linking optical humification to molecular carbon oxidation characteristics. Bacterial genera exhibited broader estimated niche breadths than eukaryotic genera, with median Levins' B values of 7.19 and 5.86, respectively. Under oxic conditions, DOM was associated with basal communities within a connected sequence of bacterial, protozoan, and metazoan associations. Bacterial and algal communities were primarily associated with N and S cycling potentials, respectively. Under anoxia, significant DOM associations with basal groups and the bacteria-to-protozoa association were not detected, while both cycling potentials shifted toward bacteria-centered regulation. N and S cycling potentials remained strongly coordinated, while modeled network robustness was 20.5% lower under anoxia. These findings reveal that redox-associated DOM reorganization shifts multitrophic regulation of coupled N and S cycling, thus providing a framework for integrating DOM composition and multitrophic organization when assessing aquatic interfaces exposed to sustained organic matter loading and redox heterogeneity.

title: Habitat heterogeneity shapes chemoautotrophic microbial diversity, ecological interactions, and carbon fixation function in an oligotrophic karst cave
abstract: Karst caves represent important yet understudied components of the global carbon cycle, where microbial dark carbon fixation contributes substantially to subterranean carbon sequestration. However, how habitat heterogeneity regulates autotrophic microbial communities and how CO 2 concentration impacts on their carbon fixation performance remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated autotrophic microbiomes across weathered rocks of cave wall and sediment along the cave passage, as well as the overlying-soil, in Luohandu Cave, a typical karst ecosystem in southwestern China, by integrating community profiling, ecological network analysis, and microcosm validation experiments. Functional prediction based on 16S rRNA gene sequencing identified six carbon fixation pathways, among which the Calvin-Benson-Bassham (CBB) cycle, Wood-Ljungdahl pathway, and 3-hydroxypropionate bicycle exhibited marked variation across the three habitats. High-throughput sequencing of the cbbL gene further revealed pronounced habitat-specific community structures: overlying soils exhibited the highest diversity and enrichments of Mesorhizobium, Variovorax, and Bradyrhizobium, whereas sediments were dominated by Pseudonocardia. cbbL communities were significantly influenced by total organic carbon, total nitrogen, pH, Ca 2+ , and Mg 2+ . Co-occurrence network analysis revealed highly modular interaction structures with predominant positive links among nodes and a limited number of keystone taxa. Microcosm incubations under a CO 2 gradient further demonstrated a nonlinear response of microbial carbon fixation, with both the microbial inorganic carbon incorporation rate (1.29 mg C kg -1 ·d -1 ) and cbbL abundance (1.77 × 10 6 copies g -1 ) peaking at 2000 ppm CO 2 . Collectively, these findings establish an ecological framework that links habitat heterogeneity, autotrophic community structure, microbial interactions, and carbon fixation function, thereby providing mechanistic insights into microbial contributions to carbon sequestration in karst cave ecosystems.

title: Effect of environmental factors on attachment of Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus to polypropylene microplastics
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) serve as substrates for bacterial colonization, facilitating pathogen transport in aquatic environments. Therefore, this study investigated the attachment of Escherichia coli (E. coli) and Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) to five MP polymers and evaluated the effects of pH, temperature, hydrodynamic conditions, natural organic matter (NOM), and salinity using polypropylene (PP)-MPs. PP-MPs supported the highest bacterial attachment efficiencies due to their hydrophobicity (water contact angle = 98.4°) and weak negative surface charge (zeta potential = -16.6 mV). Bacterial attachment decreased as pH increased (4.5-8.6) because of increased electrostatic repulsion. Increasing temperature (20 to 35 °C) decreased E. coli attachment, possibly through reduced curli production and increased motility, whereas it increased S. aureus attachment, which may be attributed to enhanced EPS production and surface hydrophobicity. Under varying hydrodynamic conditions, E. coli attachment peaked at 150 rpm, whereas S. aureus attachment remained high under both static and high-mixing conditions. Increasing NOM concentrations suppressed E. coli attachment through enhanced electrostatic repulsion but increased S. aureus attachment owing to the charge heterogeneity of its cell envelope. Elevated NaCl concentrations promoted bacterial attachment by screening electrostatic repulsion, consistent with the extended Derjaguin-Landau-Verwey-Overbeek theory, although this effect was less pronounced for S. aureus due to its high attachment. E. coli attachment decreased from 79.72% in sterilized water to 17.10% in lake water and 4.87% in WWTP effluent, whereas S. aureus retained high attachment efficiencies of 78.26% and 90.14%, respectively. These findings highlight how environmental conditions and species-specific traits collectively govern MP-associated bacterial attachment.

title: Environmental endocrine-disrupting chemicals as ototoxicants: a systematic review of epidemiological evidence
abstract: Hearing loss affects over 1.5 billion people globally and is projected to rise substantially by 2050. While several environmental pollutants are established ototoxicants, those that act as endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) have received far less attention as auditory hazards, despite mechanistic evidence for effects on thyroid hormone signaling, oxidative stress, and direct cochlear toxicity. No systematic review has comprehensively synthesized the human evidence linking EDC exposure to auditory outcomes. We conducted a systematic review in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines (PROSPERO CRD420261383642). PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to June 10, 2026. Observational studies assessing EDC exposure through biological samples and hearing function by pure-tone audiometry or otoacoustic emissions (OAE) were eligible, and risk of bias was assessed using the Office of Health Assessment and Translation (OHAT) tool. Twenty-three studies were included (16 cross-sectional, 6 cohort, 1 case-control), encompassing ten EDC classes: polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), organochlorine pesticides, organophosphates, parabens, phenols, pyrethroids, volatile organic compounds, phthalates, and polychlorinated dibenzofurans. Evidence was most consistent for PCBs, for which postnatal exposure was associated with reduced OAE amplitudes across repeated analyses of a single birth cohort, and for PFAS, with perfluorononanoic acid showing the most robust audiometric associations. Parabens and bisphenol A were associated with cochlear dysfunction in pediatric populations, though on the basis of a single research group. Within-class heterogeneity for phenols and PCBs cautioned against class-level generalizations. Overall, the evidence suggests that exposure to several EDC classes may be associated with impaired hearing in humans, supporting the inclusion of cochlear outcomes in EDC risk assessment and environmental health surveillance while underscoring the need for independent replication.

title: Factors affecting mercury accumulation and toxicological risk in coastal and estuarine bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops sp.) within a mercury hotspot
abstract: Mercury (Hg) accumulation in marine ecosystems is a global concern, yet its toxicity can be mitigated by selenium (Se). Despite this important antagonistic relationship, Hg:Se dynamics remain poorly understood in free-ranging cetaceans, which serve as valuable sentinels of ecosystem contamination due to their long lifespans and high trophic positions. We quantified total Hg (THg), methylmercury (MeHg) and Se accumulation in skin tissues of bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops sp.) across sex, estimated age, and sampling locations in the Florida Coastal Everglades, South Florida, USA - a mercury hotspot. We also explored how THg and Se concentrations varied with dolphin trophic ecology inferred by δ 13 C and δ 15 N values and spatiotemporal variation in THg and Se concentrations of potential prey. THg and Se were positively correlated with δ 15 N values, indicating an effect of relative trophic level. Also, individuals feeding more heavily in estuarine and freshwater food webs (inferred from δ 13 C values of dolphins and prey) exhibited higher THg accumulation, which matched spatial patterns of THg concentrations. Methylmercury comprised the majority of THg in the subset analyzed (78-100%), consistent with THg reflecting the biomagnifying fraction of mercury. Between 55.0% and 68.5% of 89 dolphins exceeded the species-specific estimated threshold for THg-associated liver disease risk. However, all dolphins exhibited Se concentrations high enough to potentially counteract Hg toxicity. Future research should clarify how interactions of Hg and Se influence dolphin health to better assess individual- and population-level consequences of high Hg in coastal Everglades food webs and potential influences of increased freshwater flow expected with ongoing ecosystem restoration.

title: Mineral amendments drive Compost Humification and Mineral-Associated Organic Carbon Formation in Acidic Soil
abstract: The need to valorize organic wastes and strengthen soil carbon sinks has highlighted mineral-organic matter (OM) interactions as key regulators of compost humification and soil carbon transformation. This study evaluated the effect of five minerals (shale, calcite, kaolinite, sepiolite, and hematite) on OM transformation during vegetable-residue composting and redistribute soil organic carbon (SOC) fractions after soil application. Composting and acidic soil incubation experiments were used to characterize compost humification and organo-mineral complexes (OMCs) formation, and to assess soil properties, enzyme activities, and SOC fractions after compost application. Results showed that mineral amendments accelerated compost humification. Hematite produced the strongest stimulation of humic acid (HA), increasing HA by 1.86-fold. Adsorption experiments showed rapid sorption of dissolved organic matter by minerals, which altered the distribution of mineral-associated organic fractions. The structurally embedded fraction increased by 1.19-1.64-fold, and hematite produced the largest increase in the chemically occluded fraction (1.43-fold). Hematite enhanced carbon stability by preferentially enriching HA within OMCs. Application of mineral-amended composts markedly reshaped SOC partitioning and increased the carbon pool management index by 2.67-3.11-fold. Hematite-amended compost further shifted SOC toward more protected fractions, with mineral-associated organic carbon and non-active organic carbon increasing by 2.51- and 2.78-fold, respectively. These findings show that mineral identity regulates compost maturation and SOC fraction distribution, providing a basis for designing mineral-amended composts for carbon management in acidic soils.

title: Valorizing Hazardous Spent Pot Lining in Alkali-Activated GGBS System: Synergistic Effects of Mineralized Polyacrylamide on Hydration, Strength, Microstructure, and Environmental Impact
abstract: Resource utilization of hazardous modified spent pot lining (MSPL) within alkali-activated materials faces a critical dual bottleneck, which is the inherent brittleness of alkali-activated materials and severe performance degradation triggered by MSPL incorporation. To address this limitation, this study proposes a synergistic regulation strategy employing pre-synthesized calcium carbonate-mineralized polyacrylamide (CaCO 3 @PAM) hybrid micro-filler, yet enabling safe resource utilization of MSPL while mitigating the intrinsic brittleness and performance degradation of waste-blended matrices. Unlike conventional physical blending approaches, which suffer from alkaline degradation and particle agglomeration, this organic-inorganic architecture is fabricated via in-situ mineralization to retain structural integrity under highly alkaline conditions. Multi-scale characterization techniques are utilized to elucidate dosage-dependent regulating mechanisms across systems with MSPL dosages of 0-30 wt.% and hybrid filler dosages of 0-1.5 wt.%. The results show that MSPL inhibits C-A-S-H gel formation through CaF 2 passivation. By contrast, the addition of CaCO 3 @PAM reverses such degradation via concurrent pathways. First, chemical compensation enabled by heterogeneous nano-nucleation and localized Ca 2+ supply, which increases 28-d flexural strength to 6.6 MPa (G100M0-P5) and 6.7 MPa (G100M0-P10). It also improves immobilization of fluorides and heavy metals through precipitation and chelation, ensuring leachability below regulatory thresholds. Importantly, the hybrid filler effectively mitigates the abnormal rapid-setting behavior induced by MSPL and extends the workable setting time to satisfy practical engineering requirements. This study establishes a micro-regulation strategy based on mineralized polymers that simultaneously resolves mechanical fragility, durability risks and environmental hazards of MSPL-containing alkali activation. This study offers a feasible framework for the safe valorization of hazardous industrial waste in low-carbon sustainable construction materials.

title: Interpreting optical-biogeochemical associations underlying satellite nitrate retrieval in coastal waters using Explainable AI
abstract: Sea surface nitrate (SSN) monitoring is essential for understanding coastal eutrophication and anthropogenic water cycle. However, SSN is optically inactive, and the mechanisms that enable its retrieval from satellite observations remains unclear, limiting the reliability of large-scale and early diagnosis of coastal eutrophication from space. To address this gap, we employ an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) model to identify the latent associations between SSN and individual satellite spectral bands. By estimating daily SSN distributions in the East China Sea, the Pearl River Estuary, and Chesapeake Bay, the XAI model explicitly quantifies the spectral contributions and reveals the optical-biogeochemical association underlying SSN retrieval. According to optical complexity, the coastal waters are classified as low-turbidity water and high-turbidity water. In low-turbidity water, XAI reveals a distinct spectral fingerprint characterized by positive contributions from the red band near 673 nm and negative contributions from the violet band near 400 nm. Further analysis demonstrates that the red-band contribution reflects the biological nitrate uptake by phytoplankton, whereas the negative violet-band contribution is associated with shortwave absorption by CDOM and detrital material that co-vary with nitrate transport and enrichment. In high-turbidity water, strong particle scattering obscures the spectral fingerprint, indicating that satellite-derived SSN estimates should be interpreted with greater caution under highly turbid conditions. These findings highlight the optical-biogeochemical associations underlying satellite nitrate retrieval and provide both an explainable basis and practical guidance for future monitoring of coastal nutrient dynamics from space.

title: PPAR/RXR dysregulation involved in hepatic lipid accumulation in HFPO-TeA-exposed zebrafish: Insights from multi-omics and spatial imaging
abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) is known to induce hepatotoxicity in wildlife and humans. Perfluoro-(2,5,8-trimethyl-3,6,9-trioxadodecanoic) acid (HFPO-TeA), an emerging PFOA alternative, has been increasingly used following PFOA restrictions, but its toxicity to aquatic organisms remains poorly understood. Here, an integrated multi-omics strategy combining histopathology, non-targeted lipidomics, transcriptomics, and Matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI-TOF-MSI)-based spatial lipid imaging was applied to reveal HFPO-TeA-induced hepatotoxicity in adult zebrafish. HFPO-TeA exposure caused marked hepatic injury, characterized by hepatocellular edema and cytoplasmic vacuolation, together with lipidomic evidence of steatosis-like remodeling. Non-targeted lipidomics identified 4681 lipid species across 43 classes, with abnormal profiles mainly characterized by triglycerides (TGs) upregulation and lysophosphatidylcholines (LPCs) downregulation. Transcriptomics indicated transcript-level alterations associated with the PPAR/RXR axis, involving PPARγ (pparg) upregulation together with PPARβ/δ (ppardb) and RXR down-regulation, suggesting a shift from fatty-acid oxidation toward lipid synthesis and triglyceride storage. Specifically, HFPO-TeA promoted the expression of genes involved in fatty acid synthesis and TG storage, including acsl1b, scd, and plin2. Representative significantly altered lipid species were further visualized by MALDI-TOF-MSI, providing spatial supporting evidence for heterogeneous lipid redistribution within liver tissue. These findings support a mechanistic framework broadly consistent with AOP 529, in which HFPO-TeA exposure was associated with a distinct PPAR-subtype regulatory pattern, lipid metabolic reprogramming, TG accumulation and phospholipid homeostasis disruption, and hepatic steatosis-like injury. This study provides mechanistic and spatially resolved evidence for HFPO-TeA hepatotoxicity and highlights the ecological risks of emerging PFAS alternatives.

title: Detoxification of PCDD/Fs in MSWI fly ash: A critical review of state-of-the-art technologies and synergistic multi-pollutant management
abstract: Municipal solid waste incineration fly ash (MSWI FA) contains polychlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins and dibenzofurans (PCDD/Fs), which pose significant toxicity and environmental risks. This review covers the toxicity assessment, formation mechanisms, and occurrence characteristics of PCDD/Fs, and establishes an integrated framework for detoxification technologies and synergistic multi-pollutant treatment. First, the principal formation pathways of PCDD/Fs are systematically elucidated, with particular emphasis on their occurrence and distribution within the fly ash matrix. PCDD/Fs are predominantly generated via low-temperature heterogeneous pathways and are mainly enriched in the nanopores of residual carbon. Subsequently, this review compares the mechanisms, advantages, and limitations of different detoxification technologies. High-temperature treatment achieves up to 99.9% PCDD/Fs degradation but is energy-intensive and may induce dioxin reformation. In contrast, low-temperature thermal, hydrothermal, and mechanochemical methods operate under milder conditions, although their efficiency and engineering applicability remain constrained. Flotation-based decarbonization enables efficient PCDD/Fs removal through physical separation but does not directly degrade PCDD/Fs. Biological and advanced oxidation technologies remain promising but underexplored. In addition, synergistic treatment pathways for heavy metals and chloride salts are systematically evaluated. This review integrates treatment performance, engineering constraints, and practical applicability within a multi-pollutant framework. Comparative analysis shows that high-temperature technologies offer superior performance and maturity, while other approaches require further optimization. Treatment technologies are further interpreted as complementary functional modules, supporting site-specific strategy selection according to pollutant-control requirements, regional conditions, and engineering constraints.

title: Flooding and legionellosis notifications in the United States, 2019–2024: a transparent null reanalysis after correction of surveillance-data extraction errors
abstract: Background National-scale evidence linking flooding to legionellosis relies heavily on aggregated surveillance time series, which are vulnerable to data-extraction error and seasonal confounding. An earlier version of this study reported a positive flood-legionellosis association in U.S. surveillance data; during revision we discovered errors in our data-extraction pipeline. This article corrects the record in full. Objectives To present a corrected, transparently audited reanalysis and to quantify how extraction errors and shared seasonality can generate spurious flood-health associations. Methods We re-parsed all 299 CDC NNDSS weekly tables (2019-2024) using a coordinate-anchored parser reconciled week-by-week against the printed U.S. totals (299/299 weeks reconciled exactly). Flood exposures came from the NOAA Storm Events Database. Fixed-effects Poisson and negative-binomial distributed-lag models included state and year-week fixed effects, state-specific linear trends, state-specific Fourier seasonality, and temperature terms, with permutation and event-study diagnostics. Results The corrected panel comprises 15,197 state-weeks and 11,676 legionellosis cases. The originally submitted association (average lag-0-5 IRR 1.11, 95% CI 1.06-1.17) arose from inflated 2023 counts caused by column misreads (weekly national totals of roughly 300-400 versus 15-46 after correction) acting together with seasonal confounding. On the corrected data the headline association is null (IRR 1.015, 95% CI 0.981-1.051; p = 0.39; permutation p = 0.58; event-study post-event coefficients all null). Discussion The flood-legionellosis association in our earlier submission was an artefact. Surveillance-based flood-health studies should reconcile extracted series against printed totals and treat flexible seasonal adjustment as mandatory.

title: Nitrogen-doped hierarchically porous bio-scaffold with a coordination-active interface for superior pertechnetate (TcO4−) sequestration
abstract: Long-lived and highly mobile pertechnetate (TcO 4 - ) poses a persistent challenge for radioactive-wastewater treatment, particularly in the presence of competing anions. Herein, a nitrogen-doped architected super-porous bio-scaffold (NASB) was prepared from Alocasia macrorrhiza stems. NASB exhibited a high TcO 4 - adsorption capacity, with rapid and spontaneous uptake that followed a pseudo-second-order kinetic model. It enabled preferential TcO 4 - uptake even in the presence of a 100-fold molar excess of NO 3 - . Spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations indicate that TcO 4 - sequestration mainly results from enhanced site accessibility. Nitrogen doping remodeled the interfacial electronic structure and strengthened TcO 4 - binding, with graphitic N showing the most favorable adsorption energy of -48.273 kJ/mol. These results demonstrate that combining biomass-derived porosity with nitrogen functionalization provides a carbon platform for TcO 4 - immobilization in complex radioactive wastewater.

title: Latitudinal Variations in Marine-Atmosphere Organic Matter Transfer Revealed by Suspect Screening Across Global Ocean Transects
abstract: Marine-atmosphere exchange links oceanic biogeochemical cycles with atmospheric composition. However, molecular-scale controls on organic matter transfer across the sea-air interface remain poorly understood. We investigated coupled seawater and PM 2.5 aerosol organic matter across ∼150° of latitude (75°S-75°N) using ultrahigh-resolution Orbitrap mass spectrometry and suspect screening. Principal component analysis (PCA)-based k-means clustering identified three distinct environmental regimes. In sea ice-influenced regions (cluster 0), seawater showed the highest proportion of lignin-like compounds (18.6%), suggesting a possible contribution from terrestrial inputs via glacial meltwater. In the marginal ice zone (cluster 1), seawater was rich in lipid-like compounds (81.8%), suggesting enhanced biological productivity during sea ice melting. In warm, saline, coastal-influenced regions (cluster 2), unclassified compounds accounted for 26.4%, potentially reflecting complex biogeochemical transformation. Across all clusters, aerosol samples contained higher relative proportions of peptide-like compounds than paired seawater, consistent with a possible contribution from exopolymeric substances during sea spray aerosol production. Suspect screening identified 187 anthropogenic compounds (105 in aerosols and 118 in seawater), with only 36 (19.3%) co-detected in both matrices. Molecular weight (MW) showed a clearer association with matrix co-occurrence than predicted octanol-water partition coefficients. Compounds with MW 400 g/mol showed markedly lower co-occurrence (13.6%). Nitro compounds (54.0%) and sulfates/sulfonates (32.1%) dominated the detected anthropogenic fraction. Organic matter composition differed among environmental regimes, while matrix co-occurrence varied with MW.

title: Nitrogen-fixing shrubs shift deep-soil MAOC formation from microbial necromass to an EPS-associated pathway in desert ecosystems
abstract: Shrub restoration is a widely applied strategy for combating desertification and enhancing soil carbon sequestration in arid regions. Microbial necromass carbon (MNC) is considered a major precursor of mineral-associated organic carbon (MAOC), whereas the contribution of extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) to long-term carbon stabilization remains poorly understood. Here, we examined depth-dependent associations of MNC and EPS with MAOC under contrasting shrub functional types in a restored desert ecosystem in northwestern China. We compared bare land, non-nitrogen-fixing shrubs (NNFS), and nitrogen-fixing shrubs (NFS) across surface (20-40 cm) and deep (80-100 cm) soils by integrating carbon fractionation, molecular biomarkers, microbial community analyses, and partial least squares path modeling. Relative to bare land, both shrub types increased soil organic carbon (SOC), particulate organic carbon (POC), and MAOC, whereas significant increases in MAOC/SOC and MAOC/POC were observed only under NFS, particularly in deep soil. In surface soil, NFS increased MNC-related proportional indices, and integrated modeling revealed a significant positive association between MNC and MAOC. In contrast, deep soil exhibited a distinct EPS-associated pattern: EPS and its proportional indices were significantly higher under NFS than under NNFS, whereas MNC-related indices showed no significant differences between shrub functional types. EPS was strongly associated with deep-soil MAOC (R 2 = 0.76, P = 0.001). Elevated inorganic nitrogen availability was associated with extracellular protein accumulation, while microbial community analyses identified candidate indicator taxa associated with EPS-related variables and MAOC. Under equal carbon input, EPS amendment produced a significantly greater net increase in operationally defined MAOC than MNC amendment during laboratory incubation. Collectively, these findings highlight a depth-dependent difference in microbial associations with MAOC and identify extracellular microbial products as potentially important contributors to deep-soil carbon stabilization under nitrogen-fixing shrub restoration.

title: Ingestion of anthropogenic particles by wild birds from urban riparian habitats
abstract: Plastic contamination is a recognised widespread threat to the environment, but exposure of wildlife to plastic particles has been studied mostly in marine habitats. However, plastics are mainly produced inland and carried by freshwater systems to the ocean, while also moving between aquatic and terrestrial environments. Given this, we used common bird species belonging to different dietary and foraging niches, captured in urban and sub-urban riparian areas, as indicators of exposure to anthropogenic particles, including plastics, in freshwater systems. We aimed to assess the prevalence of anthropogenic particles across different species and evaluate whether observed differences were associated with dietary preferences, foraging substrates, and urbanization. We collected faeces from six bird species, in sixteen locations along an urbanisation gradient in Coimbra city, Portugal, during the 2024 breeding season. Anthropogenic-origin suspected particles were found in 68 out of 159 faecal samples (42.7%), and thrushes, in particular the song thrush, showed the highest prevalence and abundance. Suspected particles were mainly filaments (37%) and fibres (23%), followed by fragments (21%) and pellets (15%), and most were blue (55%). There were no significant relationships between soil imperviousness and population density with the abundance of particles in the faecal samples of birds. Twenty-one percent of the successfully chemically characterised particles by micro-Fourier transform Infrared Spectroscopy were plastic (11.5% of the suspected particles). Thrushes can be used as useful indicators of anthropogenic particle contamination in urban environments.

title: Mechanism exhibited by phosphate in activating oxidants and accelerating the degradation of organic contaminants in mediated AOPs
abstract: Phosphate is widely present in natural and engineered aquatic systems, originating from sediment release, agricultural runoff, wastewater, and industrial effluents. It is also commonly used as a pH buffer in sulfate radical-based advanced oxidation processes (SR-AOPs). Traditionally regarded as an interfering ion in advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), phosphate is increasingly recognized as a potential promoter of oxidant activation and organic contaminant degradation under suitable conditions. This promotional effect is strongly dependent on the oxidant, catalyst, phosphate speciation, and reaction environment. Recent studies, particularly in peroxymonosulfate (PMS) systems, have shown that phosphate can promote radical, reactive phosphate species, non-radical, and electron-transfer pathways, while emerging evidence also indicates promotional effects in peracetic acid (PAA) and periodate (PI) systems. However, such effects are not universal across oxidants and may depend strongly on reaction conditions. This review critically evaluates the mechanisms and controlling factors underlying phosphate-promoted oxidation, with emphasis on the roles of reactive oxygen species, reactive phosphate species, singlet oxygen, interfacial electron transfer, and phosphate-catalyst interactions. A comparative assessment of representative systems is provided to clarify common and system-specific mechanisms and to identify key challenges for the practical application of phosphate-promoted AOPs.

title: Economic and environmental effects of graphene oxide incorporation strategies in recycled aggregate cementitious systems
abstract: Aggregate gradation and interfacial defects influence recycled aggregate cementitious systems, while graphene oxide incorporation routes affect reinforcement efficiency and production burdens. This study compared an unmodified reference mixture with two graphene oxide incorporation routes at the same dosage: direct addition after ultrasonic dispersion and coating of the recycled aggregate surface. Six fractal gradations (D = 2.3-2.8) were evaluated using compressive and splitting tensile strengths at 7 and 28 d. Backscattered electron images were further analysed using a convolutional neural network and deep Taylor decomposition. A cradle-to-gate inventory quantified production cost, greenhouse gas emissions, and primary energy demand on mass- and strength-normalised bases. Direct incorporation gave higher mean strengths than Ref across the investigated gradations, whereas the mean strengths obtained with surface coating varied more strongly with gradation. At D = 2.6, surface coating increased the 28 d compressive strength by 64.2% relative to the gradation-matched reference. Image analysis highlighted gradation-dependent differences in pore-like and interfacial features. On a mass basis, both graphene oxide strategies substantially increased cost but caused only modest increases in greenhouse gas emissions and energy demand. Under the baseline inventory assumptions, normalisation by the 28 d compressive strength at D = 2.6 gave greenhouse gas and energy intensities 37.7% and 33.3% below the matched reference for surface coating, without a cost advantage. Sensitivity analysis identified graphene oxide price and production energy as the principal controlling factors. These findings demonstrate that aggregate gradation and functional performance must be considered when evaluating graphene oxide-modified recycled aggregate systems.

title: Humic Acid with Manure Promotes Fungal Necromass Carbon Accumulation in Saline-Alkali Soils
abstract: Microbial necromass carbon is increasingly recognized as a vital precursor for stable soil organic carbon (SOC). However, how diverse organic amendments regulate its accumulation and the underlying mechanisms in saline-alkali soils remains poorly understood. Based on a 4-year field experiment and an additional 13 C-labeling incubation, we investigated the variation in fungal necromass carbon (FNC) and bacterial necromass carbon (BNC) under four organic amendments (organic manure (OM), organic manure plus crop straw (OM+CS), organic manure plus humic acid (OM+HA), and an unamended control). OM stimulated nitrogen mineralization through leucine aminopeptidase activity, while structural C sources in crop straw amendments (OM+CS) enhanced cellulolytic enzyme activities and biomass accumulation. In contrast, OM+HA upregulated N-acetyl-glucosaminidase at 0-20 cm and alkaline phosphatase activity at 20-40 cm, concurrently enriching K-strategist fungi (e.g., Basidiomycota) through deterministic assembly. This was accompanied by more complex, highly modular fungal networks. Glucose-derived C was preferentially retained in the FNC pool after 150 days, with 13 C-labeling confirming FNC contributes 28.8%-30.4% of 13 C-SOC versus merely 4.6%-4.7% for BNC. While OM+CS promoted necromass via biomass-enzyme co-enhancement, OM+HA synergizes enzyme-driven FNC/BNC co-transformation with K-strategist fungal enrichment and increased 13 C-BNC efficiency by 19.0% versus OM. These findings highlight OM+HA as a promising strategy for promoting microbial necromass C accumulation in degraded saline-alkali ecosystems.

title: Aquatic Macrophyte Coverage and Organic Matter Enrichment Drive Greenhouse Gas (CO2, CH4, N2O) Emissions in Aquaculture Ponds
abstract: Freshwater aquaculture ponds differ in environmental conditions and nutrient enrichment, resulting in substantial variation in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, including methane (CH 4 ), carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), and nitrous oxide (N 2 O). However, the mechanisms linking cultured species to GHG emissions remain unclear. Here, ponds culturing fish (Micropterus salmoides), crayfish (Procambarus clarkii), and crab (Eriocheir sinensis) were compared. Fish ponds had the highest suspended particulate matter (SPM) concentration (84.23 ± 43.81 mg L -1 ), whereas crab ponds had the lowest (18.50 ± 12.38 mg L -1 ). Fish ponds were also enriched in particulate organic matter (POM) and dissolved organic carbon (DOC), whereas crayfish ponds contained more aromatic and humified dissolved organic matter (DOM). Macrophyte coverage was highest in crab ponds (36.11 ± 26.18%) and lowest in fish ponds (2.08 ± 1.65%). Fish ponds showed the highest CO 2 and N 2 O cumulative emissions (584.06 ± 93.17 and 0.34 ± 0.04 g m -2 ), whereas Crab ponds had the highest CH 4 cumulative emissions (6.70 ± 0.41 g m -2 ). Random forest analysis (RFA) identified macrophyte coverage and organic matter properties as major predictors of GHG emissions. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) revealed gas-specific pathways linking macrophyte coverage and organic matter to GHG emissions. Macrophytes and organic matter jointly promoted CH 4 emissions, whereas macrophytes reduced CO 2 emissions despite the positive effect of organic matter. Nitrogen and phosphorus enrichment was the main driver of N 2 O emissions. Aquatic macrophyte coverage and organic matter were identified as key factors. This study provides a theoretical basis for the regional selection of low-carbon aquaculture species, and the development of technologies for the efficient utilization of organic matter.

title: Urinary biomarkers of organophosphates, pyrethroids, neonicotinoids and cognitive performance in adolescents and young adults in agricultural communities in Ecuador
abstract: Background As pesticide use shifts from organophosphates toward pyrethroids and neonicotinoids, few studies have used biomarkers of several pesticide classes to examine cognition in adolescents and young adults, particularly in agricultural communities. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 491 participants (50% female; mean age 20.3 years) from the ESPINA cohort in agricultural communities of highland Ecuador in 2022. One first-morning urine sample per participant was analyzed for organophosphate, pyrethroid, and neonicotinoid metabolites and the herbicide 2,4-D. Cognition was assessed with the NIH Toolbox Cognition Battery. Covariate-adjusted robust regression examined associations of individual biomarkers and pesticide-class summary scores with cognitive outcomes; quantile g-computation evaluated biomarker mixtures. We also explored differences by sex. Results Twelve of the 120 exposure-outcome associations were statistically significant at p 2x = -1.12; 95% CI: -2.03, -0.22) and Total (β 2x = -0.68; -1.27, -0.09) Cognition Composites. Most associations involved organophosphates, particularly 3,5,6-trichloro-2-pyridinol (TCPy), and measures of fluid cognition and executive function (organophosphate summary score: Dimensional Change Card Sort β 2x = -0.56; Flanker Inhibitory Control and Attention, β 2x = -0.56). Mixtures were not associated with cognition in the full sample. In exploratory analyses, neonicotinoid biomarkers showed sex-divergent associations, positive in females (crystallized cognition, vocabulary and episodic memory) but null or inverse in males, and organophosphate mixture associations appeared stronger in males. Conclusions This study provides evidence that higher urinary organophosphate metabolite concentrations may be associated with lower cognitive performance, particularly in fluid cognition and executive function. Exploratory analyses suggested sex-specific patterns for neonicotinoid biomarkers, including positive associations with crystallized cognition and memory among females, consistent with our earlier findings in this cohort during adolescence. Replication in other populations is warranted.

title: Illumination selectively strenghens performances of nitrification inhibitor in reducing mixed pesticide residues and nitrous oxide emissions: a tradeoff effect
abstract: Pesticides and nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions are critical concerns in agricultural systems. Soil nitrogen management could promote pesticide degradation and reduce N 2 O emissions, and dicyandiamide (DCD) is one of the most widely used nitrification inhibitors. The illumination can serve as a crucial mechanism for degrading various pesticides, and the effects of nitrification inhibitors on the soil nitrogen cycle might vary with different illumination conditions. This study investigated the combined effects of DCD and illumination on mixed pesticide residues (carbendazim and paclobutrazol) and N 2 O emissions in soil. Under illumination, DCD application significantly reduced soil carbendazim residues. Meanwhile, the DCD application substantially reduced the N 2 O emission rates by 27% and 13% under dark and illuminated conditions on day 28, respectively. Paclobutrazol residues did not show a detectable response to DCD or illumination during the incubation. Lower carbendazim residues in DCD-treated soil co-occurred with higher soil pH and microbial biomass carbon, greater chitinase activity, and shifts in bacterial taxa and the relative abundances of N-metabolism genes, including norB/C, gdhA/B, and gltS. The illumination augmented DCD's ability to accelerate carbendazim dissipation but impaired the DCD's ability to inhibit the N 2 O emission rates. Meanwhile, illumination concided with higher relative abundances of nitrification-related amoA/B/C and hao genes and a lower proportion of N 2 O-reduction gene nosZ. Under the tested experimental conditions,the illumination could selectively strenghen the performances of nitrification inhibitor in reducing mixed pesticide residues and N 2 O emissions. The tradeoff between carbendazim dissipation and N 2 O emissions should be considered when utilizing the illumination to strengthen the performance of nitrification inhibitors to promote pesticide dissipation.

title: Chemotaxis-Driven Rapid Enrichment and Isolation of Phenanthrene-Degrading Bacteria Overlooked by Conventional Cultivation
abstract: Microbial remediation is a promising countermeasure for organic pollutants that pose significant environmental and health risks. Conventional growth-based enrichment methods have been used for decades and successfully isolated many efficient pollutant-degrading microorganisms. However, their diminishing capacity to access previously uncultured or functionally novel microbes now poses a bottleneck for discovering next-generation bioremediation agents. This study demonstrates that chemotaxis-based enrichment can overcome this limitation and accelerate enrichment rates. After just 1-hour chemotactic enrichment, the proportion of phenanthrene-degrading bacteria and the degradation efficiency of enrichment consortia were 1.4 and 2.3 times higher, respectively, than those obtained from a 4-week enrichment culture. Moreover, because chemotaxis and conventional enrichment rely on different selection principles, they enrich distinct sets of degraders, enabling chemotaxis to access functional strains that conventional methods typically overlook. Through this approach, a unique bacterium, Stenotrophomonas sp. S62, was isolated and found to markedly enhance phenanthrene degradation under microaerobic conditions, supported by nitrate respiration via its membrane-bound nitrate reductase NarG. Contrary to traditional understanding, S62 maintained robust narG expression at dissolved-oxygen concentrations of approximately 1.4 mg/L, indicating that nitrate respiration can proceed under microaerobic stress conditions. These results establish chemotaxis-based enrichment as a rapid, efficient strategy for screening pollutant-degrading microorganisms and highlight S62 as a promising bioremediation candidate for refractory contaminated environments where oxygen is limited.

title: Spatio-Temporal Modeling for Wetland Evolution Prediction
abstract: Wetlands are crucial ecosystems, they store carbon, participate in material dynamic cycles, and provide urban ecosystem services. However, wetlands are shrinking at an alarming rate. Predicting wetland changes is vital for wetland protection. Existing spatiotemporal prediction models have made significant progress in temporal sequence modeling, yet they commonly rely on local convolutional operations for spatial representation and tend to decouple spatial feature learning from temporal memory updating, limiting their ability to capture long-range spatial dependencies and multi-scale geospatial dynamics. To this end, this paper proposes a wetland multiscale spatiotemporal aggregation network (WMS-SAN) to enhance the spatial information capture of multi-temporal wetland data. At the same time, a geospatial information-aware enhanced recurrent memory unit (GRM unit) is proposed in combination with CMT and LSTM to better integrate the local and global features of multi-temporal wetland images. WMS-SAN models time step associations in a single-input and single-output recursive mode, and learns strong dependencies with the help of LSTM hidden state transfer. Experiments show that the model can accurately simulate the evolution range of wetlands, highlighting the advantages of spatial feature learning in comparison with other models. The Moving MNIST experiment provides a standardized supplementary evaluation of the model's generic spatiotemporal prediction capability and enables comparison with established forecasting models.
